content: To set config values in Gobby's DB-first config store at runtime: PUT http://localhost:60887/api/config/values with {"values": {"key.path": "value"}}. Returns {"ok": true, "requires_restart": true} when a daemon restart is needed.

Memory-dream storage should stay side-effect-free at construction time. Use MemoryDreamService.start_async/run/revert to initialize MemoryDreamStore schema asynchronously before store access, and offload direct store I/O with asyncio.to_thread in async paths.

The block-escaped-quotes rule blocks Bash commands containing backslash-escaped double quotes in inline scripts. Workaround: write scripts to a temp file using a heredoc with a single-quote delimiter, then run the file. This avoids the escaping pattern that triggers the rule. Use: cat > /tmp/fix.py << 'SCRIPT' ... SCRIPT && uv run python3 /tmp/fix.py

Task MCP coverage tests are split across tests/mcp_proxy/tools/conftest.py and focused modules: test_tasks_create_coverage.py, test_tasks_crud_coverage.py, test_tasks_lifecycle_coverage.py, test_tasks_registry_edge_cases.py, and test_tasks_schema_coverage.py.

WorkflowHookHandler dirty-file collection is intentionally lazy and cached per _evaluate_rules invocation: baseline initialization awaits the synchronous Git scan through asyncio.to_thread, while has_dirty_files and has_target_task_dirty_files trigger the same cached snapshot during off-loop condition evaluation. Ordinary hooks with an existing baseline avoid get_dirty_files_categorized entirely; project-path resolution and Git/workflow timeout budgets remain unchanged.

Task #13848 rewrote the dispatcher rule layer to be stage-native: `src/gobby/dispatch/rules.py` computes the current row from `task.stages`, uses stage row counters/caps (`work_attempt_count`, `review_round_count`, `max_work_attempts`, `max_review_rounds`), emits `StartStageAction`/`AdvanceStageAction`, and intentionally keeps rule code pure by not importing `StageStatesManager`. `src/gobby/dispatch/dispatcher.py` owns executing those stage actions via `StageStatesManager`.

Gobby 0.5.0 intentionally removed provider-level session summary APIs and LLMService.get_provider_for_feature. Session summaries render prompts in src/gobby/llm/prompt_rendering.py via render_summary_prompt, which preserves Jinja2 and Python format template support, then route through LLMService.call_feature(config.session_summary, ...).

For Gobby 0.4.0 testing docs, `.gobby/project.json` pre-push verification runs backend lint/format/type_check plus frontend ts_check/frontend_tests, but it does not run backend pytest or backend coverage. Backend CI coverage is enforced in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` with `uv run pytest --cov=gobby --cov-fail-under=80`; agent-run backend pytest should keep `GOBBY_TEST_PROTECT=1`.

Per-chat communications session contract (task #17896, commit 1a46adcd4): IdentityManager.resolve_inbound_identity returns an IdentityResolution separating sender attribution from the effective conversation session. DMs keep external_id comms:<channel_id>:<external_user_id> and persist that session on the sender CommsIdentity. Telegram group/supergroup messages use external_id comms:<channel_id>:group:<chat_id>; the group session is effective only for the message and is not written onto the sender identity, so multiple senders share one chat context while DM links and cross-group attribution remain intact. InboundCommunications derives the group key from conversation_type plus chat_id and rejects group metadata without a stable chat_id.

Memory-dream review-vs-delete gating is prompt-only, and that is sufficient — the deterministic code-side staleness/value prior proposed in task #17206 was evaluated and rejected as unnecessary (closed wont_fix). Evidence: the #17190 prompt tightening (decision tree in src/gobby/install/shared/prompts/memory/dream.md — `review` is an uncertainty-only escape hatch; `delete` requires a citable obsolescence signal) was measured against a full sweep (run 7be75d0d, full_sweep=true, 1824 candidates, 10 pages, 0 planner errors). The 'review' bucket collapsed from 41 (old-prompt baseline run 78bc9e92) to 2, and delete verdicts each cite concrete signals (high age_days + ~0 access_count, closed task/migration, removed UI). Durable architecture/convention/preference memories all landed on keep at 0.9-0.95 confidence; nothing valuable was swept. So: do not build the deterministic prior; the prompt alone gates cleanly. A numeric self-scoring table was also explicitly rejected during #17190 as uncalibrated and JSON-parse-fragile.

During coordination bug #15065, planned daemon restarts were canceling active terminal agents because setup_signal_handlers consumed the restart shutdown marker on the first SIGTERM, then a follow-up markerless SIGTERM reported STOP and overwrote runner._shutdown_intent. Fix commit 760ea9fa5 preserves a recorded RESTART intent across later STOP intents in the same signal handler closure; regression test covers restart marker consumed then second signal without marker.

SafeExpressionEvaluator in safe_evaluator.py supports IfExp (ternary: x if cond else y) as of commit bafc3d51 (visit_IfExp). Lesson: pipeline conditions using unsupported Python AST node types fail silently (ValueError caught by should_run_step, defaulting to True), so always add test coverage for any new AST node type used in pipeline conditions.

Bundled pipeline MCP steps must pass session identity through the call_tool wrapper/ambient pipeline context, not as an inner target argument when the target schema does not accept session_id; gobby-tasks:create_task rejects an inner session_id. Agent-spawn pipeline inputs also need a non-empty model default because an empty templated string normalizes to null; wiki-research defaults to sonnet.

MCP server configs synthesized from GitHub/search import output are preview-only. Return `requires_approval` when no secrets are missing, `needs_configuration` when placeholders remain, and avoid persisting via `_add_server`; explicit add-server is the approval/persistence step. The MCP import route should broadcast `server_imported` only when the result includes a non-empty `imported` list.

Gobby web uses a tracked postinstall patch script, web/scripts/patch-tailwind-node-dep0205.mjs, to patch installed @tailwindcss/node@4.3.0 so Node registerHooks is used when available and DEP0205 warning suppression can stay removed from package scripts. The script no-ops for other versions or already-patched installs.

Task MCP lifecycle/status tools now use `TaskToolErrorCode` from `src/gobby/mcp_proxy/tools/tasks/_errors.py` for workflow-branchable failures. Closed task failures return `error_code: "TASK_CLOSED"`; claim conflicts return `TASK_CLAIM_CONFLICT`; invalid lifecycle statuses return `TASK_INVALID_STATUS`. `build_synthetic_tool_output()` promotes direct MCP `error_code` to top-level `tool_output`, and plan-adversary branches on `tool_output.error_code == "TASK_CLOSED"`.

For gcode real-binary conformance tests in this repo, point the subprocess at the pytest PostgreSQL schema with GCODE_DATABASE_URL='<postgres_database_url>?options=-csearch_path%3D<postgres_schema>' (using '&' when the base URL already has a query). This lets /Users/josh/.gobby/bin/gcode write into the same isolated DB schema that CodeIndexStorage assertions read.

Task #17229 decomposed src/gobby/sessions/transcript_index.py by extracting persistent sidecar serialization and the bounded async index cache into src/gobby/sessions/transcript_index_sidecar.py. transcript_index.py remains the compatibility facade for public imports such as get_or_build_index, load_index_sidecar, persist_index_sidecar, clear_index_cache, INDEX_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES, and compatibility attributes including INDEX_SIDECAR_SUFFIX, _INDEX_CACHE, and _encode_adjustment_value. Sidecar logging intentionally uses logger name gobby.sessions.transcript_index so existing caplog/monkeypatch expectations remain stable after the split.

Reinstalling Rust binaries into ~/.gobby/bin on macOS: `cp` over the existing file keeps the inode and invalidates the kernel's cached code signature, so the next execution dies with SIGKILL (exit 137) before main. The working flow is `rm` the old binary, `cp` the new one (fresh inode), then `codesign -f -s - ~/.gobby/bin/<bin>` to ad-hoc re-sign. Probe success with `<bin> --version` (exit 0) before trusting the install.

When syncing bundled DB records that have a UNIQUE index (e.g., agent_definitions with idx_agent_defs_name_scope_project), do NOT use import-then-delete to achieve atomicity — the import will fail with UNIQUE constraint violation because the old record still exists. Instead, use manager.update() for in-place atomic updates, which issues a single UPDATE SQL statement that can't leave the DB in an inconsistent state. The delete-then-import pattern is also risky because if import fails after delete, the old record is permanently lost. The manager.update() approach solves both problems.

Voice dependency decision: faster-whisper>=1.0.0 and chatterbox-tts are now base project dependencies, while the `voice` extra remains as an empty compatibility alias. Runtime voice health checks report missing required packages with `run uv sync` guidance and no longer auto-install packages via `uv pip install`; `gobby install --voice` only enables voice config and prints reference-audio guidance.

Merging duplicate gwiki entity concept pages durably: union the loser's title+aliases into the survivor's frontmatter aliases, then delete the loser. This is stable because entity pages only re-synthesize from BROKEN-link clusters (upkeep derives its work queue from lint broken_links) — once [[Entity]] mentions resolve via the survivor's aliases, nothing recreates the deleted page. Entity-name wikilinks retarget automatically via aliases (page_targets resolution is case-insensitive over path/stem/title/aliases); path-form links like [[knowledge/sources/x]] must be retargeted by hand. Also: an alias exactly equal to the page title is pure redundancy (title is already a resolution key) and trips the duplicate_aliases lint. Applied in #17630: gobby-core→gcore, mcp-server→mcp, worker-process-spawning→spawn-agent merges with zero broken-link regressions (147→147, dup aliases 5→0).

Codewiki aggregate page reuse must include every non-source dependency in the invalidation key. For repo overview and architecture pages, include audit-link sets, source hashes, file/module summaries, graph edges, component ids, and leading chunks; when a key also needs source hash enforcement, mark the BuiltDoc source-sensitive and check source/neighbor hash key sets before reusing.

Project route mutations that combine LocalProjectManager database writes with project-file writes must execute inside a single server.run_db callback containing pm.db.transaction(). The database ambient transaction is propagated within that worker thread, so LocalProjectManager.update participates and rolls back when a later file operation raises.

Build HTTP control routes `/api/build/stop`, `/api/build/resume`, `/api/build/clean`, and `/api/build/restart` use the normalized control envelope shape `{success, result, error, error_code?}`. The CLI daemon control shim `_control_payload_from_daemon` unwraps only this envelope and treats legacy bare dict payloads as unusable fallback.

In the Skills activity UI, SkillsInstalledDetail catches rejected onSave promises, forwards the Error message through onError, and keeps the useDetailDraft draft dirty/open. SkillsTab.withSkillBusy similarly catches rejected row actions such as export and renders their Error message in the shared error banner. API action helpers should throw responseError for non-OK responses to activate these paths.

CONVENTION: plan-doc revision naming is audit-trail hygiene and applies ONLY when revising a plan AFTER its task tree has already been expanded. When that happens: copy-and-version rather than edit in place. Create `{original-name}-rev1.md` (then `-rev2.md` for subsequent revisions), prepend a change note explaining why the pivot + what the prior design was + date, and leave the original file untouched as the audit trail. Update downstream tasks' `> Plan reference:` lines to point at the latest rev. Does NOT apply during normal drafting before expansion — iterate in place on the original plan file. Rationale (user, 2026-04-21): editing the source plan in place AFTER expansion destroys the link between expanded tasks and the design they were spawned from. Applies to any `.gobby/plans/task-*-plan.md` file that has been expanded into a task tree.

Task #17483 intentionally updated /Users/josh/Projects/gobby/.coderabbit.yaml so CodeRabbit reviews the in-repo Rust workspace under crates/: Rust source path instructions cover crates/**/*.rs, Cargo manifest instructions cover **/Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock remains reviewable by removing the broad !**/*.lock filter, and CodeRabbit tools explicitly enable clippy and osvScanner for Rust lint/dependency evaluation.

Epic #15741 child #15748 C language skill uses 6 references: configuration, types-and-abi, memory-and-lifetime, errors-and-resources, testing, portability-and-performance. Discovery rule require-c-skill triggers on suffixes .c, .h, .c.in, .h.in, .pc, .pc.in and exact basenames Makefile, makefile, GNUmakefile, CMakeLists.txt, meson.build, meson_options.txt, configure.ac, configure.in, Makefile.am, Makefile.in, compile_flags.txt, compile_commands.json, .clang-format, .clang-tidy, .clangd. It intentionally skips C++ suffixes .cpp/.hpp/.cc/.cxx, C# .cs, and generic package/appsettings/editorconfig/YAML files; tests pin that loaded skill csharp does not satisfy skill_loaded('c').

Task #18822 / commit d3c27dd8c added `ToolResultStore` in `gobby.storage.tool_results`. Saves use one hub transaction, run configured retention cleanup before insert, store full content, and create contiguous line-aware chunks capped by configured `chunk_chars`, including hard splits for oversized single lines. `get_slice` and `get_meta` canonicalize result IDs through `uuid.UUID` before SQL and enforce project ownership plus configured read-time TTL. `gobby.search.keyword` now registers `tool_result_chunks` for BM25 with a result_id filter and `(ordinal, id)` tie breaks, and defines the shared fixed `MAX_PG_SEARCH_QUERY_CHARS = 1_000` authority for later offload query surfaces.

Gobby monolith refactor-task convention: automatic refactor-task creation for oversized files applies only to non-test Python, TypeScript, and CSS source files: non-test `.py`, `.ts`, `.tsx`, and `.css`. Tests such as `tests/`, `test_*.py`, `*_test.py`, `*.test.ts`, `*.test.tsx`, `*.spec.ts`, and `*.spec.tsx` are excluded from automatic monolith refactor-task creation unless cleanup is explicitly requested.

As of commit 2151fbf0a in gobby, non-dry `gobby build` launch calls an idempotent guard in `src/gobby/build/lifecycle.py` that runs `build_resume` when project build automation is paused before the initial dispatcher tick, and adds a warning to the BuildResult. This keeps fresh build targets from being created while project automation remains stopped.

Recall drift contract (task #18427, commit d30f67496): `memory.digest_shadow_usefulness` is dark by default and model validation rejects enabling it unless `recall_signal_hub=true`; the legacy digest_memory_usefulness reader/field is removed. Drift has no label-source or calendar-window override. It rehydrates the shipped decision cohort, requires its evaluator_version to equal the current pairwise evaluator, and freezes source, protocol, judge model, judge config fingerprint, candidate scope, weighting regime, project scope, and weighting mode from that record. It fetches only digest-shadow requests whose constants_provenance equals the active decision_digest, so static intervals and gate baseline rows never enter the live cohort even across rollback/re-enable cycles. Fewer than 10 mixed requests returns insufficient_data; a missing/unshipped/inactive/incompatible record returns idle without reading signal rows.

Codewiki module pages after #18570 use `render_module_call_sequence`: canonical Call edges are traversed from in-page components with no in-page incoming call edge, with deterministic cyclic fallback; flat stars remain SparseEvidence and only a depth-2 chain emits. A canonical depth-2 witness is reserved before caps (8 participants, 12 messages, 2 hops), messages are ordered by call depth, output carries the static-trace disclaimer and shared `is_valid_mermaid` gate. Module builders record independent ModuleDependency and ModuleCallSequence outcomes for every page. `RENDER_VERSION_MODULE` is 21 so restored dependency and call-sequence sections regenerate together; graph edges remain outside module reuse keys.

Plan/expand skill content preservation: The plan skill (src/gobby/install/shared/skills/plan/SKILL.md) now uses a heading-based template format (### N.N sections) instead of checklist bullets. Each section's content becomes the subtask description verbatim during expansion. The expand skill (src/gobby/install/shared/skills/expand/SKILL.md) Phase 3 now has anti-summarization rules: TDD header (3-4 lines) + full plan section content below a --- separator. Key principle: the implementing agent only sees its own subtask, so each plan section must be self-contained with file paths, code examples, schemas, and behavioral specs. The /gobby:x invocation syntax was also fixed to /gobby x throughout both files.

Telegram comms parity effort: epic #17888, plan at .gobby/plans/telegram-parity.md, parity matrix at docs/reviews/channel-parity-matrix.md, reusable playbook in the bundled channel-parity skill. Key decisions: responder = ChatSession reuse (the web-chat/voice agent-turn engine behind a new transport interface), NOT terminal-agent spawns; access = allow_from allowlist (Josh only initially, ID captured from first inbound DM metadata); scope = core loop + streaming-by-edit + voice STT, long-tail features (pairing, reactions, topics, inline keyboards, TTS) are backlog. Task refs: F1 destination #17889, F2 dedup/offset #17890, F3 media inbound #17891, F4 send route #17892, F5 init errors #17893, responder #17894, transport #17895, group sessions #17896, adapter capabilities #17897, voice STT #17898, guide rewrite #17902, live validation #17903. Parity targets researched 2026-07-11: OpenClaw (docs.openclaw.ai/channels/telegram) and Nous Hermes Agent (hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/messaging/telegram); both are self-hosted gateways with per-chat sessions, allowlist+pairing auth, streaming-by-edit, voice in/out, mention-gated groups.

Telegram structured callback contract (task #18854, commit f138ccae9): gobby-communications.send_message accepts inline_keyboard rows of {text,value} plus a bounded callback TTL when session_id is present. TelegramCallbackRegistry validates at most 8 rows, 8 buttons per row, and 32 total buttons; raw values remain server-side while Telegram receives one-use cryptographically opaque callback_data tokens within the Bot API 64-byte limit. Tokens are scoped to the originating chat/topic and session, expire after 1-3600 seconds, and replays/scope mismatches resolve invalid. Telegram subscribes to callback_query updates, normalizes valid clicks as callback user messages routed back to callback_session_id, suppresses invalid/expired content before responder fan-out, and answers callback queries for polling and webhooks so the client progress indicator clears.

Agent isolation was decomposed in task #17086. `gobby.agents.isolation` is now a thin compatibility facade that re-exports the historical import surface. Implementation lives in sibling modules: `isolation_models.py` for dataclasses/ABC/branch naming, `isolation_none.py`, `isolation_worktree.py`, `isolation_clone.py`, `isolation_repair.py` for hooks/project metadata/MCP preflight helpers, `isolation_code_index.py`, and `isolation_factory.py`. Tests that patch internals should target owning modules such as `gobby.agents.isolation_worktree.repair_isolation_environment`, `gobby.agents.isolation_clone.uuid4`, or `gobby.agents.isolation_repair._copy_cli_hooks`, while public imports can continue using `gobby.agents.isolation`.

In Gobby configuration and prompt routes, prompt override reads/deletes should go through LocalPromptManager.get_override/delete_override rather than direct prompt SQL, so storage behavior stays centralized and testable.

Task #18695 / commit a82f813ad2b71b0fa8fff415baf9c7af3e2f51d0 made IdleCheckHandler provider-neutral. AgentLifecycleMonitor owns and injects WatchdogReaderRegistry; each idle check resolves the reader from session.source with AgentRun.provider fallback. Recent-session capacity probing is driven by reader.capacity_pane_message, transcript reads call reader.read directly, completed-turn recovery consumes normalized snapshot tri-state signals, and reasoning interruption requires reader.supports_reasoning_interrupt. Capacity retry state and durable actions use provider-neutral names. Providers without readers, including AGY, retain the shared idle path and perform zero transcript reads.

ToolCallCard treats CLI/MCP tool arguments and results as untrusted protocol payloads. In web/src/components/chat/ToolCallCard.tsx, narrow file_path through the existing stringValue helper before pathBasename/getLanguageFromPath; in ToolCallCard.helpers.ts, getToolSummary returns null for non-string file_path. Completed AskUserQuestion values are normalized by normalizeAnsweredValues, which preserves strings, joins string arrays, and JSON-serializes other values.

As of task #13905 / commit 92b13b5b6, the legacy front-half conductor surface is removed from Gobby. gobby-tasks-ops no longer exposes front_half_tick, src/gobby/mcp_proxy/tools/tasks/_front_half.py and _front_half_artifacts.py are deleted, requirements-analyst and block-front-half-on-interactive-lock are no longer active bundled definitions, and task_has_label_prefix is no longer registered in workflow condition helpers. Stage-native planning/build dispatch remains the active flow.

Gobby daemon task #17906 removed import-time secret salt/KEK path caching. `src/gobby/storage/secrets.py` now keeps only immutable filenames (`.secret_salt`, `.secret_kek`) and resolves each operation's concrete path once through `gobby.paths.get_gobby_home()`. This allows isolated contexts to change GOBBY_HOME after module import without reading or writing another context's key material, while preserving 0600 creation/chmod behavior and the shared filenames used by pack/code-index isolation.

Gobby should not forward Claude Code OAuth env tokens such as CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN into spawned tmux agents. Claude spawned-agent auth should work through on-disk login/config discovery via HOME/XDG/CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR or API/provider keys such as ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. The removed DB config key agent_auth.forward_claude_oauth_env is stale and should be purged by migration.

Task #18823 / commit 279813442 implemented `ToolResultOffloader` in `gobby.mcp_proxy.services.result_offload`. Oversized successful MCP results are classified through `classify_raw_tool_result`, serialized in two stages, stored with `ToolResultStore`, and replaced by envelopes budgeted to `max_envelope_chars - 512`. Intent is truncated to `MAX_PG_SEARCH_QUERY_CHARS` before sanitization; BM25 match search is advisory, while persistence failures return bounded inline non-retrievable envelopes. Identity fields reuse `render_bounded_identity`, stored-tail truncation is reported honestly, and `GobbyDaemonTools.call_tool` now uses the same canonical classifier for MCP error conversion. `classify_raw_tool_result` treats a direct mapping containing `error` without `success` as failed, preserving the prior enriched-error front-door contract.

rule_engine.py has _clear_edit_write_state(variables) helper that sets edit_write_pending=False and edit_write_stop_blocks=0. Used at 3 sites: circuit breaker tripped, no-rules after_tool success, with-rules after_tool success. Keeps the clearing logic DRY.

Bundled agent YAML must use current AgentDefinitionBody fields: prompt is ignored by the model and should be represented as instructions, and skills must be a dictionary of named lists such as methodology: [triage-judgment], not a bare list. Bundled SKILL.md files must start with YAML frontmatter delimited by --- so SkillLoader can parse and sync them.

gwiki source pages have TWO naming schemes that must be reconciled by stable identity: (1) manifest-derived digest path `knowledge/sources/src-<id>.md` via `paths::derived_markdown_path(record)`, and (2) synthesis title-slug path `knowledge/sources/<slugify(title)>.md` via `synthesis::paths::source_page_paths`. A source id is `src-<16hex content_hash>-<location-slug>` (built by `sources::render::source_id(canonical_location, content_hash)`); the content hash ROTATES on every re-fetch while the location slug is STABLE. Any identity match/dedup/link-resolution MUST key on the stable location slug (everything after the hash), NOT the full hash-prefixed id — see `compile::select::source_id_slug` and (added #17705) `synthesis::paths::source_identity_slug`. `page_matches_source_identity` originally required an exact `source_path` frontmatter match, so hash rotation (and legacy stubs lacking that frontmatter key) minted `-2` sibling stubs and left sources uncompiled. This volatile-hash-identity disease is the shared root cause behind #17705 (duplicate stubs / stuck uncompiled), #17704 defect 2 (dangling concept->source links), and #17702 (topic-compile stale hash pointers).

FIXED for links in #17704 (commit on 0.5.0): `crates/gcore/src/vault/lint.rs::source_identity_lookup_key` emits a private-keyspace stable key (`\x01source-identity\x01knowledge/sources/<slug>`) for any `knowledge/sources/src-<hex>-<slug>` PAGE (in `page_targets`) AND LINK (in `link_lookup_keys`), so a link minted against an old hash still resolves to the page under its rotated name whenever they share the location slug. Shared gcore lint => covers `gwiki lint` + `gwiki trust`/health; on-disk, no re-index. Verified live 2026-07-07 gwiki 0.8.0: session-source danglers 19 -> 0 (sessions 3e4c4a13 rotated to src-103b0fac, ec749a42 to src-efd2ef44). Does NOT change the deliberate content-addressed naming.

Pending sources are drained (marked compiled) by `gwiki upkeep` (upkeep::run reconcile step: pending sources not in any broken-entity-link cluster reconcile with no synthesis); the wiki-upkeep cron runs every 24h, so sources ingested mid-cycle are transiently pending until the next run.

Core pattern: spawn-time auto-claim links the assigned task to the spawned child session once; later provider SessionStart/default-agent activation should preserve workflow instance, current step, variables, task ownership, and progress. When first MCP calls block or a spawned agent lands in an already-satisfied claim step, correlate agent_run_id/session_id across spawn, terminal preparation, SessionStart, workflow preservation/creation, auto-claim, and the first blocked MCP call.

Strict typing convention from #18668 and #18688: wiki cron factories expose string-returning async handlers and depend on a structural coordinator protocol with handle_write_result; MCP before-tool event builders explicitly return HookEvent. The seven active regression modules in #18688 pass standalone strict mypy without suppressions. SessionMessageProcessor tests assert current processor state because the processor no longer owns message_manager. Implemented in commit 4d1e7dfb4.

spawn_agent_impl treats model names as provider-scoped: when a call explicitly overrides an agent definition's provider to a different effective provider and omits/blank-passes model, it must not inherit agent_body.model; the selected provider should use its CLI default unless the caller supplied an explicit model.

Task #18552 replaced close_task prose-regex verdict overrides with structured current_failure_evidence. Gobby test-quality analyzer skips functions decorated as pytest fixtures (`fixture`, `pytest.fixture`, `pytest_asyncio.fixture`) during test discovery, even when their names start with `test_`. Added in task #14272 commit c6dfeb381.

Bug #9064: close_task in _lifecycle.py failed to clear task_claimed/claimed_task_id session variables after successful close. Root cause: the claimed_task_id comparison and clearing logic was outside the `if state:` block where claimed_task_id was defined, and the outer `except Exception: pass` silently swallowed any errors. Fix: moved comparison+clearing inside `if state:`, added UUID normalization for robust comparison, replaced silent exception swallowing with logger.warning(). File: src/gobby/mcp_proxy/tools/tasks/_lifecycle.py lines ~250-290. The observer fallback in observers.py intentionally does NOT clear for Claude Code (no tool_output in AFTER_TOOL hooks), so CC users are entirely dependent on this MCP proxy clearing code.

As of gobby-#17331, daemon codewiki refresh is shared through `CodewikiRefreshService` in `src/gobby/code_index/codewiki_refresh.py`. The post-commit `CodewikiRefreshTrigger` only gates/debounces `wiki.codewiki_on_commit` and logs best-effort failures; nightly cron registration lives in `src/gobby/code_index/codewiki_nightly.py`, creates/reconciles one disabled-by-default system job named `gobby:codewiki-nightly:<project_id>` with handler `codewiki_nightly:<project_id>`, schedules `0 3 * * *` in host-local/configured timezone, and stores cron execution timestamps as UTC via CronJobStorage. Gobby docs/runbooks/postgres-rollback.md is now a PostgreSQL recovery export runbook, not a SQLite runtime rollback runbook. It documents cutover-ticket parsing, pgaudit-managed/pgaudit-file/wal-archive/none capture_kind export paths, artifact attachment, and PostgreSQL fix-forward/operator-managed restore guidance. `gobby postgres deactivate` is removed and `hub_backend=sqlite` is not a supported runtime path.

Merge agent removed from autonomous dev-loop and orchestrator pipelines (commit c0508c2c). Merge is now manual — the pipeline terminates when all tasks reach review_approved status. The merge agent definition still exists but is not spawned by any pipeline. Reason: pushing to remote and closing tasks autonomously is the highest-risk operation and should be tested on a test project with packaged gobby before enabling. The merge agent also has a no-push conflict with worker-safety rules that needs resolution (push should be an MCP tool, not raw Bash).

Gobby design principle: LLM-backed feature configuration is adapter-agnostic and must not assume Haiku/Sonnet/Anthropic specifically. New LLM-backed features should avoid hardcoded Anthropic model names and should be built against adapter-agnostic feature config/routing (call_feature) so they work across all CLI/ACP adapters.

Critical bug: If hook_dispatcher.py is deleted or missing while Claude Code hooks are configured, the Stop hook failure creates an infinite loop. Each response triggers the stop hook, which fails and generates a new 'Stop hook feedback' message, which triggers another response, ad infinitum. The only way to break the loop is for the user to Ctrl+C and fix the hook file externally. The agent cannot fix it because PreToolUse hooks also fail, blocking all tool calls. Root cause in this case was unclear — the file existed at ~/.gobby/hooks/hook_dispatcher.py but uv run couldn't find it temporarily (possibly during venv rebuild or daemon restart).

Context-window resolution is source-aware. Use gobby.llm.context_windows for precedence: explicit overrides, provider-reported runtime metadata, provider-reported/provider-owned catalog values, OpenRouter/model_costs registry, then static defaults. Provider model entries should carry context_length_source so stale source-less cache values do not outrank registry/runtime data.

DECISION (2026-04-23): For #12651 skill fetch directives, use the canonical wording `Call get_skill(name="<skill>") on gobby-skills, then continue.` Do not tell agents to pass `session_id` inside get_skill arguments; when Gobby invokes tools through the MCP proxy, session context belongs to the outer call/proxy context, not the inner tool args. Use `loaded_skills` as the replacement ledger for successful agent-visible skill fetches, not `injected_skills`.

gobby-cli now has pinned daemon-facing CLI contracts for gcode and gwiki. `gcode contract --format json` must match `crates/gcode/contract/gcode.contract.json`; `gwiki contract --format json` must match `crates/gwiki/contract/gwiki.contract.json`. Provider/auth design decision: Gobby should offer generation through either explicit local/OpenAI-compatible endpoints (`local`, configured in Gobby with endpoint/model/key) or user-owned CLI/app-server providers such as Codex. Codex auth, including subscription, API-key login, access-token, auth.json/keyring/env handling, belongs to Codex CLI/app-server. Gobby should not scrape Codex auth files, infer OpenAI API keys, or instantiate OpenAI SDK clients for Codex-backed generation; using OpenAI API keys with Codex is the user's Codex auth responsibility.

Plan-mode resolution at semantic turn_start is surface-specific: managed web chat trusts HookEvent.metadata.chat_mode and falls back to persisted session chat_mode; terminal hooks prefer structured chat_mode, provider-native state, prompt markers, then workflow variables; terminal Codex reads the newest turn_context.payload.collaboration_mode.mode directly from raw JSONL in the workflow observer layer without transcript-package imports. Context compaction guidance uses 40%/60% thresholds below 1,000,000 tokens and 30%/40% at or above 1,000,000, with missing-window ratios using 40%/60%. Implemented by task #18356 / commit acbe12577.

Task #18825 / commit 59002e0a0 added the internal `gobby-results` registry. `search_tool_result` gates every search through canonical UUID parsing plus project/TTL-aware `ToolResultStore.get_meta`, sanitizes only after that authorization read, hydrates pg_search chunk hits, and trims matches to `max_envelope_chars - _WRAPPER_MUTATION_RESERVE`. `get_tool_result` uses the same caller project context and bounds slices to that shared working target. CLA tooling research for task #18708 (verified 2026-07-24): contributor-assistant/github-action was archived on 2026-03-23 and declares itself unmaintained. LocalSessionManager (storage/sessions.py) uses get() not get_session() to fetch a single session by ID. The sessions/manager.py SessionManager has get_session() but the storage layer does not.

Telegram reaction contract (task #18851, commit fb6f14bdb): TelegramAdapter explicitly subscribes polling/webhooks to message_reaction and message_reaction_count, normalizes per-actor old/new ReactionType lists and anonymous ReactionCount entries (whose type field contains a nested ReactionType), and assigns each update a unique platform event ID while retaining reaction_target_message_id for action routing. Isolated gwiki smoke-test vault recipe: gwiki project scope requires a project identity file, so to test the installed ~/.gobby/bin/gwiki against a throwaway vault, create <dir>/.gobby/project.json with just {"id": "<uuid>", "name": "<name>"}, then run `gwiki init --project <dir>` (creates <dir>/wiki), and use `gwiki <cmd> --project <dir>` for ingest-file/sources/refresh/upkeep/lint etc. Use --no-ai on ingest-file to avoid AI routing — note --no-ai ingest writes ONLY the raw capture (raw/<src-id>.md) and manifest entry; it does NOT create the derived digest, so hand-seed wiki/knowledge/sources/<src-id>.md yourself for digest-dependent smoke tests (upkeep clustering, supersede/refresh cleanup). Upkeep smoke: `gwiki upkeep --project <dir> --ai off` clusters wikilink mentions from those seeded digests (min 2 mentions) into knowledge/concepts pages. Source-manifest details for smoke assertions: the manifest is NOT a JSON file — it is `<!-- gwiki-source {json} -->` marker lines in wiki/raw/INDEX.md (SourceManifest::read/index_path); record ids are the raw filename stems (raw/<src-id>.md), and `gwiki refresh` takes repeatable `--id <src-id>` flags. Discovered while fixing #17650/#17651/#17652; useful for #17653 and any future gwiki ingest work.

Gobby dispatch mutexes attached to active agent runs must be refreshed during normal AgentLifecycleMonitor maintenance, not only daemon restart recovery. Use TaskDispatchMutexManager.refresh_mutex_for_run(task_id, run_id, ttl_seconds) so only existing matching active-run mutex rows are extended; do not mask active_run_expired_lease in observability or create new mutex rows for manual agents.

As of 2026-06-28, Gobby's SecretStore derives its Fernet key from the local machine_id plus a shared salt, and SecretStore.get returns None on InvalidToken. In a shared PostgreSQL hub / remote daemon setup, client-side config loading that resolves $secret values may fail to decrypt secrets created on the daemon machine unless the design routes secret resolution through the daemon or changes the identity model.

Codex model-capacity recovery in IdleCheckHandler uses two signals: the tmux pane's exact capacity message triggers an immediate probe, and the latest structured transcript turn must confirm an event_msg error with codex_error_info=server_overloaded between task_started and task_complete. Successful continuation sends consume a per-run bounded consecutive retry budget; duplicate transcript error lines are suppressed; later model output resets that budget; exhaustion delegates to centralized idle-agent failure recovery. Implemented by task #18382 at commit 97a4b1920.

For gobby-cli task #557 / gwiki shared-code Falkor edge limits, the accepted configuration surface is config_store plus ~/.gobby/gcore.yaml only; do not add .env or GOBBY_* environment-variable overrides for these gwiki edge-limit settings.

Current Gobby build automation behavior: explicit `gobby build ...` ticks respect the project dispatcher hard stop. If `gobby:dispatcher.enabled=false` from `gobby build stop`, build kick helpers return `dispatcher_cron_disabled` until `gobby build resume` re-enables the row. Gobby FalkorDB Docker installer contract: installer module `src/gobby/cli/installers/falkor.py` resolves passwords as provided > existing `databases.falkordb.requirepass` secret > generated, validates with `validate_falkordb_password`, writes config_store and `bootstrap.yaml` only after Docker health returns PONG, stores bootstrap key `falkordb_password`, maps Redis to host port 16379 and browser to 13000, and returns `password_source` plus `password` only for generated values.

Terminal session registration enriches terminal_context with parent_create_time and parent_name from psutil for parent_pid. kill_terminal_session permits the PID SIGTERM fallback only when no tmux pane was recorded and both stored identity fields still match; any unresolved tmux kill failure returns false without signaling the PID.

Gobby 0.5.0 local auth CLI is a Click group: `gobby auth credentials [--remove]` manages web UI credentials, while `gobby auth token` reports local token path/existence, stored SHA-256 hash prefix, and file/DB agreement. `--show` reveals plaintext and `--rotate` replaces both file and `auth.api_token_hash`; help includes the exact `gobby auth token --rotate` remediation. `gobby install --auth-mode required|disabled` persists the bootstrap setting via update_bootstrap_yaml. Agent-facing wiki artifacts refresh through the daemon's six-hour `exports` cron job. `GwikiGateway.export_pages()` runs `gwiki export pages` and `graph_artifacts()` runs file-writing `gwiki graph`; both are in `SERIALIZED_WRITE_COMMANDS`. The scheduled handler always attempts both steps, records per-step status/ok/error, returns top-level `status=degraded` with `ok=true` when exactly one step fails, and raises when both fail. The handler lives in `src/gobby/wiki/scheduled_exports.py` to keep `scheduled_jobs.py` below the 1,000-line source limit.

Agent run stale-timeout cleanup now keys off child session heartbeat (`sessions.updated_at`) before timing out long-running runs, and timeout persistence backfills `tool_calls_count` and `turns_used` from linked session stats so active work is not mislabeled as a zero-activity timeout.

Gwiki targeted-compile identity invariant: a project-scoped explicit target requires an explicit compile topic; checkpoint sources may be reused only when the requested topic matches the checkpoint's effective topic (compile state, topic-scope name, or project question). An existing explicit target must have parseable frontmatter with a non-empty title exactly matching the requested topic after trim. Write intent and synthesis_mode never bypass identity checks, and persisted compile handoffs record the effective vault-relative target plus write intent.

Pipeline CLI approval commands (`gobby pipelines approve` and `gobby pipelines reject`) should prefer the daemon HTTP routes (`/api/pipelines/approve/{token}` and `/api/pipelines/reject/{token}`) so daemon-started pipeline resumes keep the daemon's MCP/LLM-capable execution environment. Local executor fallback is only for unreachable or unhealthy daemon cases.

workflow_definitions table has FK constraint: project_id TEXT REFERENCES projects(id). PostgreSQL FK enforcement is active. Tests using project-scoped workflows must create a real project via LocalProjectManager.create() first, then use project.id as project_id. Raw path strings like '/my/project' will cause IntegrityError.

Watchdog circuit breaker state is now persisted to ~/.gobby/watchdog_state.json. The _load_state()/_save_state() methods read/write restart_times as JSON. This means the circuit breaker survives watchdog process restarts — new watchdog instances inherit previous restart counts instead of starting fresh. ## Lesson
- principle: Requests carrying `X-Gobby-Local-Token` may be sent only to daemon URLs that resolve exclusively to loopback addresses.
- root_cause: The local daemon token is a loopback trust-boundary credential; sending it to a non-loopback destination exposes that credential outside its intended boundary.
- prevention: Resolve and validate the daemon URL before every broker POST, reject any destination with a non-loopback resolution, and attach `X-Gobby-Local-Token` only after validation succeeds.

gobby image vision works via two paths. Direct: gwiki describe_image (crates/gcore/src/ai/vision.rs, default routing 'direct') calls an OpenAI-compatible endpoint (e.g. LM Studio local models) and returns {description, ocr_text} JSON; the request sets VISION_MAX_TOKENS = 2000 because reasoning models like gemma-*-qat emit hidden reasoning_content first and need enough token budget to also emit visible content — too small a max_tokens can produce an empty visible response. Daemon: POST /api/llm/vision/extract (multipart file=) calls Claude vision (haiku) and returns a rich description; VisionExtractService treats adapter output as description text and leaves ocr_text null unless the underlying service explicitly returns genuine OCR text. To probe an OpenAI-compatible local backend like LM Studio directly, send Authorization: Bearer $OPENAI_API_KEY (key stored in .env, mode 600 — never print it).

Repeated exact resolved or conflict-bearing pending merge_start calls reuse the existing resolution; exact pending rows without conflicts may be refreshed with the same resolution id; active pending resolutions on the same worktree with different branches return a clean conflict error with the active resolution id.

Terminal focus routing contract: `gobby:show-activity-tab` is the sanctioned cross-component escape hatch. useActivityPanel normalizes `detail.tab`; for the terminal tab only, a string `detail.sessionId` is stored as `terminalSessionRequest` before showTab so events survive TerminalTab lazy-mount timing. ChatPage passes that request to ActivityPanel as terminalFocusSessionId and passes clearTerminalSessionRequest as onTerminalFocusHandled. Keep this channel separate from ChatPage routing focusSessionId, which has SessionsTab selection semantics.

LiteLLMProvider in llm/litellm.py sets os.environ from config api_keys. Previously had 'if value and key not in os.environ' guard which meant env vars always won over config. Changed to unconditionally set from config since config is now the source of truth (resolved from secrets store > env vars). This ensures secrets-store priority propagates to LiteLLM.

SessionsFilterDropdown should enable the shared web/src/hooks/useDialogFocus.ts only for its mobile aria-modal variant (`isOpen: isMobile`). The hook moves focus into the panel, traps Tab, handles Escape, and restores prior focus on unmount; the component's window Escape listener must ignore defaultPrevented events to avoid double-closing bubbled modal Escape events. Covered by task #16801 / commit 56826dcfd.

In web useSettings, API settings remain authoritative over localStorage after initial load, while explicit per-field changes made before the GET resolves override the corresponding remote fields. Persistence is gated by the initialized ref until the GET settles, and pending changes are recorded by the shared updateSettings helper so user intent is preserved even when the chosen value equals the initial value. Covered by task #16591 / commit 3be4af3aa.

2026-05-20: Task #14884 fixed stale merge_conflicts row hydration surfaced by #14094/#12761. merge_status now updates existing rows with null ours_content/theirs_content from live Git conflict markers, so compact has_* flags and include_content responses are truthful. merge_resolve was already reading live hunks, so this fixes stale metadata/reporting and retry coordination, not necessarily complex conflict resolution quality.

Task #18781 / commit 7691b656d adds the shipped `gobby test-types audit` mypy ratchet. The new src/gobby/test_types package resolves target-project mypy with marker+executable pinning, parses engine-namespaced line-stable fingerprints, filters followed imports outside requested paths, renders bounded CI output, and mirrors test-quality baseline/CLI semantics. Shared test_quality baseline writes are now same-directory temp + os.replace atomic and baseline errors are dimension-neutral. Builtin validation detection recognizes the command only with both --baseline and --fail-on-new. Validation: 168 focused regressions passed; strict mypy passed 1,582 src files and the new tests; Ruff, Bandit, build, test-quality ratchet passed; watchdog smoke reported 5 errors across 4 files as planned.

GitHubMCPHelper treats MCP SDK CallToolResult(isError=True) as a transport/domain failure before JSON or plain-text result parsing. `_call_github_mcp` raises GitHubMCPToolError with the tool name and raw text detail; create_branch and get_file_contents then exercise their existing git fallbacks, while push_files propagates the typed error. Valid isError=False JSON and plain-text results keep their prior shapes.

In gobby-cli #928 / Gobby #17344, `gcode prune` reconciles code-index orphan SQL child rows whose project_id appears in code-index child tables but is absent from `code_indexed_projects`; it best-effort clears FalkorDB/Qdrant derivatives first, then deletes hub child rows so SQL consistency is restored. The existing #802 behavior remains: stale indexed projects are pruned globally, unscoped prune cleans valid-project projections for all remaining indexed projects, and scoped `gcode --project <root> prune` limits valid-project projection cleanup to that project. The indexer now seeds/upserts a minimal `code_indexed_projects` row before per-file writes via `PostgresCodeFactSink::new`; the final index stats refresh remains authoritative.

Managed native binary promotion is centralized in src/gobby/install/bin_freshness_promotion.py. Installer writers must acquire the per-tool lock from bin_freshness_locks before calling the shared staged promotion helpers; the background freshness updater already owns that lock around promotion.

Build profile registry design in Gobby: build_profiles.source is constrained to installed|project; custom is a computed UI/API state. Profile resolution checks project-scoped, global project-source, then installed rows, and a disabled highest-priority match is an immediate BuildProfileError rather than falling through. Bundled installed profiles live at src/gobby/install/shared/registry/build_profiles.yaml and are synced on install/daemon startup.

Invalid-argument MCP responses always include the tool's current input schema when one is available. Emitting that schema idempotently records or retains the current-context schema lease, so a corrected call can proceed without repeating schema discovery.

WorkflowHookHandler.handle() now delegates directly to evaluate() (rule engine). The step-based workflow engine (engine.handle_event) is dead code — 0 workflows in DB use it. Before this fix, handle() ran evaluate() then ran the dead engine and returned its empty response, discarding rule metadata including mcp_call effects. This caused title synthesis and other mcp_call-based features to silently fail.

Event handlers (_agent.py, _tool.py, _session.py) no longer call _evaluate_workflows() — rules are evaluated once in hook_manager.handle() via workflow_handler.handle(), not twice. The _apply_debug_echo() method no longer takes a wf_response parameter; it reads debug_echo_context from WorkflowConfig only.

Qwen CLI transcripts use a line-oriented current-envelope format even when the file extension is `.json`. Treat these files like JSONL for incremental byte-offset processing, transcript index sidecars, reader windows/counts/status, and lifecycle backfill. Source detection must recognize Qwen records with `message.parts` before the overlapping Claude `message.role` shape.

useTmuxSessions lifecycle contract (task #18541, commit 15d2ffc72): the hook owns a dedicated /ws connection. Every socket callback and 2 s reconnect is guarded by both a monotonically increasing connection generation and exact current-socket identity; cleanup increments the generation and closes the current socket. Public state includes connected, sessionsLoaded, socket-qualified attachedTarget {name, socket}, streamingId, requestPending, attachError, and clearAttachError. Attach/detach requests carry generation-bound correlation tokens; duplicates are suppressed while pending; switching targets performs correlated detach then attach; socket close synchronously clears attachment, streaming ID, loaded/pending/error state, and stale replies are ignored. sendInput emits terminal_input with run_id; resizeTerminal emits tmux_resize with streaming_id. onOutput deliberately has one callback consumer, TerminalTab.

Gobby docs now include docs/guides/shared-stack.md for trusted Tailscale shared-stack setup: one daemon/PostgreSQL hub, client GOBBY_DAEMON_URL or bootstrap daemon_url plus database_url, Tailscale ACL trust boundary, daemon-mediated secrets for ordinary clients, and current remote execution limitations. Added in commit 6be276e24 for task #17432.

Task stage manifest force replacement must be performed through StageStatesManager.initialize_manifest(..., replace_existing=True). The manifest operation holds the runtime mutex and performs DELETE, inserts, and lifecycle-event recording in its existing transaction, preserving the prior manifest if initialization fails. An external transaction around initialize_manifest conflicts with its immediate mutex acquisition.

De-biased usefulness-judge recipe validated by #17193: gemma4:31b via local Ollama /api/chat with think:false, temperature 0, num_predict caps, keep_alive 30m runs ~7s/row for classification (299 rows / 37 min) and ~31s/row for LOO regen+grade ablation. Satisfies the memory-usefulness-label contract §4: Gemma family differs from both Claude and GPT generator populations; position-randomization = seeded shuffle of block siblings with [TARGET] marker; length control = fixed truncation budgets (prompt 1200 / memory 900 / response 2200 chars) + anti-verbosity rubric, verified by response_len AUC ≈ 0.46. Judge confidence output is near-binary (0.9/1.0), so confidence-weighted analysis adds little; use confidence=1.0 subset for sensitivity. Protocol id 17193-v1, harness in docs/research/memory-recall-spike-17193/harness/judge.py.

User preference: workflow filter UI should use a dropdown/select element, not chips/buttons. Chips take up too much space. The dropdown should match the height of the search box (same padding, font-size, border styles).

As of task #17540, Linear bidirectional sync stats include `deferred` alongside `errors`. Transient issue-list fetch exhaustion during `pull_linear_updates` (httpx network/timeout causes or retryable HTTP 429/5xx status wrapped by LinearGraphQLError) sets `pull.errors=0` and `pull.deferred=len(linked_rows)`. `sync_all` treats errors or deferred counts as non-clean, does not advance `synced_at`, and skips push after a non-clean pull to preserve pull-first safety; cron raises only for real errors and reports deferred-only runs as `Linear sync deferred`.

POST /admin/restart endpoint added to admin.py (src/gobby/servers/routes/admin.py). Pattern: spawns a detached subprocess with inline Python script that waits for current PID to exit, then starts `python -m gobby.runner`. Uses same _process_shutdown() as /admin/shutdown. Has a nonlocal _restart_in_progress guard against double-restart. The restarter script handles PID file cleanup, port release wait, and log file redirection. No `signal` import needed at module level — only used inside the inline script string.

The web cron management surface no longer has CronJobsPage. Project-scoped listing and creation logic lives in web/src/hooks/useCronJobs.ts, consumed by web/src/components/activity/CronTab.tsx. Cron create payloads should derive project_id from useCronJobs(projectId) so callers cannot persist invisible unscoped jobs.

src/gobby/servers/routes/admin/_health.py agent_stats['running'] feeds gobby status to warn users about restart fallout. Use list_running (status='running' only), not list_active (running + pending). Running agents get cancelled mid-stream on restart; pending/paused get resumed by the lifecycle so they're not at risk. Confirmed by Josh on 2026-04-10 after a mypy fix flagged the original (broken) call to LocalAgentRunManager.list_active_runs() — a method that never existed. The dict key is intentionally 'running', not 'active'. If you need a separate 'pending will be resumed' surface, add a new key — don't widen the existing one. Audience for the field is 'what breaks if I restart now?', not 'what's in the system'.

When calling call_tool via MCP, always use the 'arguments' parameter (not 'args') for passing inner tool arguments. The rule engine's argument unwrapping (rule_engine.py:547) only checks raw_tool_input.get('arguments'), not 'args'. Using 'args' means rule conditions like tool_input.get('commit_sha') can't see inner arguments, causing false blocks from rules like require-commit-before-close.

Rules in src/gobby/install/shared/rules/ are templates with enabled: false by default. They get synced/installed to the database where they're actually enabled. Don't modify the install folder to enable rules — they're already installed and enabled in the DB.

AgentsTabData.AgentDraft retains a shallow copy of the full agent workflows object so AgentsTabActions can apply edits to known workflow fields without discarding hidden selector data or unmodeled workflow keys. Duplicate agent payloads are built directly from AgentDefInfo.definition, with sandbox remapped to the API's sandbox_config field, to preserve passthrough lifecycle and step configuration.

In the Gobby ecosystem, `gcode` means the Rust code-index CLI built from crates/gcode in the gobby monorepo (formerly the separate gobby-cli repo), not CNC G-code; the user explicitly confirmed CNC G-code is not part of Gobby. `gcode outline <file>` is implemented in crates/gcode/src/commands/symbols.rs: it queries `code_symbols` for a project/file, maps each `Symbol` through `to_outline()` in crates/gcode/src/models.rs, and prints compact symbol metadata. The Python daemon invokes `gcode index` for initial/incremental/maintenance indexing via src/gobby/cli/init.py, src/gobby/code_index/trigger.py, and src/gobby/code_index/maintenance.py.

The pipeline CLI is split behind src/gobby/cli/pipelines.py as a facade: command implementations in pipelines_runs.py access shared dependencies and helpers through _facade(), preserving patch points under gobby.cli.pipelines. As of task #18304 / commit 96ba21154, local CLI approve/reject fallbacks resolve getpass.getuser() via _cli_actor() and pass it to PipelineExecutor for approval audit identity.

Feedback: Check connected MCP servers before designing integration wrappers.

Before designing CLI wrappers (gh, etc.) for an integration, run list_mcp_servers and list_tools on the relevant server. The Gobby daemon already has github, linear, brave-search, chrome-devtools, context7, playwright as configured stdio MCP servers.

Why: in the #13552 PR/merge plan I drafted a `gobby-pr` server wrapping `gh pr create/merge/...` only to have josh point out the GitHub MCP server already exposes 26 tools including create_pull_request, merge_pull_request, get_pull_request_status, get_pull_request_reviews, create_pull_request_review, and update_pull_request_branch (GitHub's native server-side rebase).

How to apply: when planning any external-system integration (GitHub, Linear, Slack, etc.), the first step is to enumerate connected MCP servers and their tools. Only fall back to CLI shell-outs or new HTTP wrappers for capabilities the MCP server doesn't expose (e.g., GitHub branch protection API isn't in the MCP tool list).

In Gobby E2E tests, isolated daemons run outside dev mode, so bundled workflow definitions are not synced on startup. Memory recall helper E2E coverage should seed required bundled rules/agents into the test Postgres schema before daemon boot via an e2e_pre_daemon_setup fixture. Successful internal MCP tool payloads have top-level success=true stripped by the proxy; tests should treat absent success as success and only fail on success=false.

Bug fix #9071: Stop hook fails to block when agent has claimed task. Root cause: dual-write desync between workflow_states and session_variables. claim_task/create_task wrote task_claimed=True to workflow_states only, but the rule engine evaluates session_variables with higher precedence. If session_variables has stale task_claimed=false from init-task-claimed at session start, it overrides the truth. Fix: mirror writes to session_variables via ctx.session_var_manager.merge_variables() in claim_task, close_task, and create_task(claim=True). Also added SessionVariableManager to RegistryContext in _context.py. Secondary fix: removed [:8] truncated UUID usage in 5 places across task tools (_lifecycle.py, _crud.py, _session.py, _expansion.py).

When the user asks for Codex subagents in Gobby review/coordinator workflows, use native Codex subagents via multi_agent_v1, not the Gobby agent system with provider=codex. Do not call gobby-agents.spawn_agent for that phrasing unless explicitly requested.

ACP session/update handling in Gobby routes plan, session_info_update, current_mode_update, and usage_update through existing chat/session surfaces. Plan updates replace the existing pending-plan state. currentModeId only changes Gobby chat_mode when it maps to a known posture: plan->plan, act/normal/accept_edits->normal, yolo/bypass->bypass; unknown provider modes stay non-authoritative and do not change permissions. usage_update uses current ACP 1.0 top-level size/used/cost and emits existing session_usage_updated frames. Session metadata updates reuse session_info and must not clear ACP config/auth controls when those fields are absent.

Spawned Gemini and Qwen sandboxed agents use the upstream CLI `-s` flag with `SEATBELT_PROFILE` and pass resolved external write paths as repeated `--include-directories` args. Gobby omits the workspace root and workspace-internal paths, dedupes external paths, and enforces the built-in Seatbelt profile limit of five include directories.

Design decision: memory knowledge-graph entities in FalkorDB must be identified only by the `_Entity` label plus `entity_key`; type labels such as `Person`, `Tool`, or `Project` are classification metadata and must be applied after the `_Entity` MERGE so one entity_key can safely gain multiple type labels.

Gobby system-requirements guide facts: `gobby install` prompts/configures the embedding provider before Docker services; provider `none` disables semantic search and skips Qdrant/FalkorDB; installer-managed services use `src/gobby/data/docker-compose.services.yml` profiles `qdrant`, `falkor`, and `all`; embedding dimensions live under `embeddings.dim`, with Ollama/LM Studio defaults at 768 and OpenAI `text-embedding-3-small` at 1536.

Stage manifest HTTP implementation for Gobby task #13843 lives in src/gobby/servers/routes/stages.py for registry/default-stage reads and src/gobby/servers/routes/tasks.py for /api/tasks/{id}/stages plus PATCH stage actions. Stage-specific 422 responses intentionally return top-level JSON error discriminators (`illegal_stage_transition`, `illegal_manifest_mutation`) instead of FastAPI HTTPException `detail` wrappers.

gwiki librarian disambiguation verdicts (#17782/#17865): reviewed-distinct near-duplicate pairs are recorded in <vault>/meta/librarian/distinct-pairs.json as {"pairs": [{"left": "<vault path>", "right": "<vault path>", "reason": ...}]} and honored by expected_similarity_pair in crates/gwiki/src/librarian.rs (order-insensitive, .md-suffix tolerant). Verdicts deliberately live in a meta artifact, NOT page frontmatter — compile/upkeep recompiles regenerate frontmatter from a fixed field set and would silently drop in-page markers. Generated per-folder _context.md files and pages whose frontmatter contains a `redirect` key are excluded from the near-duplicate scan. Redirect/tombstone pages must retain a non-empty H1 body because the PostgreSQL wiki index derives its required title from parsed page content and otherwise fails a NOT NULL constraint. Generated `_index.md` and per-folder `_context.md` catalogs still list verified redirect pages; give redirect aliases subject-specific titles such as `Redirect: <canonical title>` when generic legacy titles would create indistinguishable catalog entries, then run `gwiki index --project` to refresh PostgreSQL search identity. When merging duplicate entity concept pages: fold the loser's sources/excerpts/citations/backlinks into the survivor, add the loser's title as an alias (upkeep's case-insensitive stem/title/alias resolution then binds future mentions to the survivor instead of recreating the deleted page), delete the loser, and prune the dead 'Used by' entries in source digests — they accumulate forever and nothing removes them automatically.

Session handoff commit context has a two-stage producer: TranscriptAnalyzer records shell commit calls as a fallback, then sessions.workspace_context.enrich_git_context replaces them with real git-log entries when available. Both paths must preserve the formatting.py contract of {hash, message}; transcript fallbacks use an empty hash and the commit command as message.

User-created workflow definitions must use source='custom' by default and must not retain the reserved 'gobby' tag. Bundled rule/pipeline orphan cleanup is ownership-scoped to rows with both the gobby tag and source='installed'.

The _personal project name is mapped to 'Personal' in App.tsx (line 86). This causes UI confusion when components use project names as labels - any toggle or display showing 'Personal' may collide with the _personal project name. The ChatInput scope toggle was redesigned to use fixed 'Personal'/'Project' labels with a search dropdown instead of showing project names directly.

Task #18495 (commit 8fade8961) standardized the 13 bundled agent templates migrated in 6f5ee31f9—analyst, architect, backend-developer, frontend-developer, fullstack-developer, holistic-reviewer, plan-adversary and taskless variant, plan-enhancer and taskless variant, product-manager, researcher, and tech-writer—on provider codex, model gpt-5.6-sol, and reasoning_effort xhigh. Task #17661 now covers only the remaining build-profile stage_efforts override; its former backend/frontend template work and planner-family constraint were superseded.

Bundled agent workflow definitions are canonical under `src/gobby/install/shared/workflows/agents/`; do not keep agent definitions in project-local `.gobby/workflows/`. The `gemini-image-gen` agent should use the Gemini image-generation model `gemini-3-pro-image-preview` and self-complete with `gobby-agents:end_agent_run`.

ToolProxyService.call_tool is a shared execution seam, not a conversation-only boundary. src/gobby/workflows/pipeline/handlers.py::execute_mcp_step calls it and returns the resulting dict into pipeline dataflow, while FastMCP/HTTP/stdio conversational entrypoints also call it. Any result transformation placed in tool_execution._execute_tool_dispatch therefore affects deterministic pipeline consumers; context-only output shaping needs an explicit delivery policy or a transport-facing boundary.

Gobby validation command detection is now configured through DaemonConfig.validation_detection and optional project-scoped .gobby/project.json validation_detection. Observers classify shell commands via gobby.config.validation_detection and record matcher metadata so close_task can append successful validation evidence to the LLM validation context.

Memory recall injected-context rendering has two relevant paths: `src/gobby/memory/context.py::build_memory_context()` renders `memory_id` only, while workflow/MCP injection via `src/gobby/workflows/engine/effects.py` -> `src/gobby/hooks/dispatchers/mcp.py::_format_project_memories()` renders `<project-memory>` lines with `memory_id`, `similarity` as score, and `search_via` as via. Retrospective transcript parsers for recall usefulness should test against the actual delivery/MCP path when they need score/via.

Communications provider/model selection is configuration-driven through chat candidates and optional responder overrides, not hardcoded by the comms-agent persona. The default managed session resolves the configured candidate's provider, model, and reasoning effort; explicit responder provider/model values override it. Telegram /status reports the resolved binding.

API keys in the Gobby codebase resolve from SecretStore (machine-bound via Fernet), NEVER from `os.environ`. User stated this as a project convention.

**Scope:** The convention is canonical for *skill-hub auth resolution* (see task #12053 fix in `src/gobby/mcp_proxy/registries.py:366-372`). The non-hub install prompts at `src/gobby/cli/_install_prompts.py:69-179` still read env for MCP-server keys (GitHub, Linear, OpenAI, Brave, Context7) — that's existing behavior, unclear whether it's intentional or pending cleanup. Don't extend the pattern; do migrate new credential paths to SecretStore-only.

**How to apply:**
- Resolve new hub/provider credentials exclusively through `SecretStore.get(name)`.
- If you see `os.environ.get(<API_KEY>)` in hub/auth resolution code, treat it as a bug to remove.
- Error messages for missing auth should direct users to `gobby install` or `gobby secrets set <NAME>` (value is prompted interactively — never pass it as a CLI argument; `gobby secrets set X VALUE` is not a valid invocation per `src/gobby/cli/secrets.py:44-79`).
- Install-flow prompts for new credentials persist via `SecretStore.set(name, value, category=..., description=...)` with categories in {general, llm, mcp_server, memory, integration}.

The wiki parity+ bake-off (WP4, task #734) lives in ~/Projects/wiki-bakeoff/ (OUTSIDE the gobby-cli git repo). Its outputs/ dir holds raw artifacts per competitor (deepwiki-open, CodeWiki, CodeWiki-python, gobby-codewiki-agents, graphify, opendeepwiki): SCORECARD/SETUP/RUN_LOG + rendered wikis + raw JSON/graph blobs (graphify graph.json ~13.5MB, graphify-out ~43M).

Josh (2026-06-14): do NOT commit these to the repo, and do NOT dispose of them. They are the 'before' baseline — the battery will be RE-RUN after gobby implements the adoption candidates (C1-C9 in ADOPTION-CANDIDATES.md) to measure improvement.

Why: the bake-off's value is a before/after comparison; deleting the outputs destroys the baseline. Competitor Docker images (deepwiki/codewiki/opendeepwiki, ~5.7GB) are rebuildable but re-running costs time, so don't reflexively prune them either.

How to apply: during any cleanup, tear down running containers but PRESERVE ~/Projects/wiki-bakeoff/outputs/ and inputs/. At WP5, commit only lightweight evidence (scorecards/analysis) into docs/evidence/, leaving heavy raw blobs in place under wiki-bakeoff/.

CO_OCCURS densification (#17492): the gobby-memory MCP tool densify_knowledge_graph_cooccurrence bulk-retrofits derived CO_OCCURS edges from MENTIONED_IN structure + stored _Entity.embedding vectors, no LLM (src/gobby/memory/services/knowledge_graph/densify.py). Idempotent (delegates each batch to writer.merge_cooccurrence_edges, which recomputes support from the live graph). Run it after enabling materialize_cooccurrence on a graph built with the flag off, and after any bulk memory import.

Rust gcore daemon URL resolution (crates/gcore in the gobby monorepo) matches the Python bootstrap contract: gcore reads bootstrap.yaml `daemon_url` as the explicit bootstrap endpoint before falling back to `bind_host`/`daemon_port`, and `GOBBY_PORT` is canonical with deprecated `GOBBY_DAEMON_PORT` honored only after `GOBBY_PORT`. ghook uses this through gobby_core::daemon_url(), so bootstrap-configured remote daemon URLs work without setting GOBBY_DAEMON_URL. (Implemented pre-merge as gobby-cli task-17431.)

Spawn trace correlation pattern: correlate agent_run_id and session_id across `spawn_agent_impl`, `prepare_terminal_spawn`, provider SessionStart, `build_persona_changes`, workflow preserve/create decisions, auto-claim, and the first MCP call or block.

Gobby daemon audio capability bindings now use voice.openai_compatible_audio for OpenAI-compatible STT/translation endpoints. Each binding has provider, url, model, optional api_key, transcription_enabled, translation_enabled, and timeout_seconds; /api/voice/transcribe accepts multipart form fields capability, provider, model, language, and prompt and defaults to Whisper audio_transcribe for legacy file-only calls.

In gobby-cli gwiki, commands that declare a hard attached PostgreSQL index dependency can enforce it through `crate::support::postgres::require_attached_index(command)`, which resolves the DSN via the local broker/env/config path, opens a read-only PostgreSQL connection, and validates `crate::schema::validate_runtime_schema` before emitting reports. `gwiki librarian` defaults to requiring this hard dependency while `Options::offline()` remains available for pure unit/report tests.

Gobby's FastAPI app (src/gobby/servers/app_factory.py:create_app) has app-wide GZipMiddleware (minimum_size=1024, added innermost/first). This is safe for the MCP streamable-HTTP mount because the installed starlette 1.3.1 GZipMiddleware excludes text/event-stream content types via DEFAULT_EXCLUDED_CONTENT_TYPES, so SSE streaming is never gzip-buffered; WebSockets bypass it entirely (scope type != http). When adding streaming HTTP endpoints, no gzip exclusion work is needed as long as they set an event-stream content type.

Task #17025 hoisted workflow execution helpers for the one-surface migration. The implementations now live in web/src/components/shared/executions/: execution-utils.tsx, executionFormatters.ts, and isolationColors.ts. Legacy workflow paths remain as thin re-export shims so Workflows subtree imports continue to work until teardown. Activity consumers (PipelinesTab, CronTab, TracesTab) import from shared/executions, and the acceptance grep for workflows/executionFormatters|workflows/execution-utils|workflows/isolationColors under web/src has no hits outside the workflow shims/internal imports.

In the Gobby repo, code-index hook blocks are teaching prompts: after loading the requested gobby-skills skill once, continue the requested work. Treat the first block as guidance, not a lasting hard blocker. The user clarified that the hook exists to remind agents that gcode exists and should be used for token savings; it should not preclude using other tools when they are the right fit.

Gobby UI dev server auto-start: GobbyRunner.run() now spawns Vite via spawn_ui_server when ui.enabled=true and ui.mode=dev, and stops it on shutdown. Port lineup: 60887 (HTTP daemon), 60888 (WebSocket), 60889 (Vite dev). Config default is UIConfig.port=60889. The spawn/stop helpers live in gobby.cli.utils (spawn_ui_server, stop_ui_server, find_web_dir).

LLM model routing map (as of 2026-02-23): Haiku is used for: session title synthesis (SessionTitleConfig), memory extraction (MemoryExtractionConfig), skill description (SkillDescriptionConfig), digest generation (DigestConfig), tool summarization, task description, MCP server import, memory fact/dedup/entity extraction. Sonnet is used for: merge conflict resolution (MergeResolutionConfig), session summary, tool recommendations. Opus is used for: code review (ReviewConfig), chat (ChatConfig). All are configurable via DaemonConfig fields.

Gobby #14962 code-index isolation fix: isolated spawn preflight now prepares a per-workspace gcode wrapper at <workspace>/.gobby/bin/gcode. When daemon_config.database_url is available, the wrapper points gcode at a private ~/.gobby/gcode-runtime/<workspace-hash>/bootstrap.yaml with inline PostgreSQL DSN plus symlinks/copies for machine_id, .secret_salt, models, and services. spawn_agent passes the wrapper PATH through SpawnRequest.extra_env; on preflight failure it sets code_index_preflight_warning, removes code-index from additional_skills, appends a prompt warning to use normal file search/read tools, and the require-code-index-skill rule skips when that warning variable is present.

In the Gobby one-surface activity panel, MCP server create/edit now uses web/src/components/activity/mcp/McpServerFields.tsx with save orchestration in McpTabActions.ts. ActivityMcpTab no longer imports the legacy McpServerForm modal; Add selects server viewMode=create. Server config updates use PUT /api/mcp/servers/{name} for config and PATCH for enabled changes. LocalMCPManager now persists requires_oauth, oauth_provider, and connect_timeout via migration 283.

## Lesson
- principle: A global concurrency cap is enforceable only when every producer rechecks capacity under the same lock immediately before inserting active work.
- root_cause: Heartbeat precomputed available slots outside CronRunAdmission and later inserted through plain create_run, while run_now alone used locked atomic admission.
- prevention: Route scheduled and manual cron producers through CronRunAdmission and retain a deterministic different-job interleaving test that pauses heartbeat after its early count while manual admission fills the last slot.

Gobby's close_task LLM validator compares the diff against the literal text of validation_criteria — not the spirit. When a reasoned mid-implementation decision diverges from the criteria (directory renames, path shifts, choice-of-approach changes), validation will fail even if the deviation was correct. The recovery path is: (1) update_task(task_id, validation_criteria=<rewritten to match reality>), then (2) close_task(task_id, commit_sha, changes_summary) — re-run normally, no skip.

Do NOT try skip_validation=true with commit_sha. Gobby explicitly blocks that combination with: 'Cannot skip validation when a commit_sha is provided. If you're linking a commit, you did real work — let validation verify it.' The block is intentional: real work must be verified against something rewritten, not bypassed.

Discovered on task #11793 (2026-04-15) when I committed `.upgrade/` after the criteria said `_upgrade/`. The switch was the correct call (dot-prefix dirs are auto-skipped by SkillLoader._load_skill_files at src/gobby/skills/loader.py:658; underscore dirs would have leaked into loaded_files as resources), but the validator couldn't tell from the diff alone.

How to apply going forward: any time a mid-implementation change diverges from the text you wrote at claim time, plan on update_task before close_task. Better still — write validation_criteria at creation time loosely enough that reasonable judgment calls don't require a rewrite: specify *what must be true when done*, not *which exact path or name to use*. If the divergence is too large to rewrite cleanly, escalate_task instead of fighting the validator.
