Project verification existing-command confidence is centralized in src/gobby/project_verification/evidence.py as existing_command_confidence. Both collected EvidenceItem rows and generated existing CommandCandidate rows use it, so synthesis sees one confidence for the same command. The policy preserves task #16663: generic commands score 0.62, deliberate short commands floor at CI confidence 0.82 (0.84 custom), and richer commands retain higher confidence.

compact_self terminal compaction now has two continuation delivery paths: SessionStart/pre-created-session consumption remains first, and compact_self itself schedules a delayed tmux fallback that consumes compact_self_continue_pending before sending the shared continuation prompt. This covers Codex same-pane compactions where no SessionStart hook fires, while avoiding duplicates when a provider consumes the marker earlier.

The gobby-plans MCP boundary treats any explicitly provided project reference that LocalProjectManager cannot resolve as invalid_project before calling LocalPlanManager. This applies to get/list/archive/hash/manifest/delete operations so an unknown project can never degrade to project_id=None and widen storage access across projects. Implemented for task #16632 in commit 4889b7b38.

Bug pattern: add_dependency(task_id, depends_on) uses positional args where task_id is the dependent and depends_on is the blocker. When calling from create_task's blocks/depends_on handlers, it's easy to swap these. The expansion code (_expansion.py) avoided this by using named parameters (task_id=..., depends_on=...). Lesson: always use named parameters for add_dependency calls to make the semantic meaning clear and prevent arg-swap bugs.

Task de-escalation must be atomic at the HubDatabase boundary: stage restoration, claim release, and work-attempt reset belong in one outer transaction because the lifecycle manager reuses the ambient transaction. Restoration of a stopped approved stage is valid only when the latest transition into `<stage>:ready` is exactly `<stage>:review_approved` → `<stage>:ready` with reason `build_stop`; an older matching event must not authorize restoration after a newer different transition.

GitHub issue triage delivery processing now uses GitHubTriageStore.claim_delivery_for_processing(project_id, delivery_id), a conditional pending -> processing update, before payload side effects run. Repeated triage with the same content_hash and verdict returns the existing task/vector ids without applying triage outcome side effects or re-upserting the vector index. Linked GitHub issue tasks are protected by partial unique index idx_tasks_github_issue_link on non-null (project_id, github_repo, github_issue_number).

Gobby machine identity generation uses py-machineid's machineid.hashed_id("gobby") to produce an app-scoped hardware identifier. Existing values persisted in ~/.gobby/machine_id remain authoritative and are returned unchanged, preserving identity for existing installations.

Gobby retired bundled definition contract as of commit fbbdf0496 (#15368): retired bundled agents use tombstone YAML files under `src/gobby/install/shared/workflows/agents/deprecated/`; retired bundled pipelines also use tombstone YAML files under `src/gobby/install/shared/workflows/pipelines/deprecated/` with `deprecated: true`, `enabled: false`, and `steps: []`. Active YAML for retired names must remain absent, and sync ignores deprecated directories.

When ending an auto-task workflow, set pre_existing_errors_triaged at BOTH session scope AND workflow scope (workflow='auto-task'). The stop hook checks the workflow-scoped variable, not the session-scoped one. Setting only session scope will cause the stop hook to block.

In Gobby storage, `gobby.storage.migrations` is a flat module (`src/gobby/storage/migrations.py`) that sets `__path__` to `src/gobby/storage/migrations/`, allowing focused migration submodules such as `rename_yolo_to_unattended.py` without converting the public migrations module into a package.
ACP session roots should track provider-accepted additionalDirectories from the ACP session response, not blindly trust request extras; request extras may be rejected or narrowed by the provider.

Gwiki integration uses `src/gobby/gwiki_gateway.py` as the single async wrapper around `gwiki --format json`. The wrapper returns daemon envelopes with `ok`, `command`, `payload`, and `stderr` for command results, returns a degraded envelope for timeouts, and raises `GwikiCommandError` on nonzero exits while preserving parsed stdout payload plus stderr.

In gobby-cli gwiki, task #549 added `gwiki review-report` as a Markdown artifact command. It accepts `--file`, `--symbol`, and `--diff`, requires PostgreSQL for wiki facts, uses optional FalkorDB shared `gobby_code` neighborhoods plus `gobby_core::graph_analytics::analyze` for risky dependency shifts, and degrades with front matter `degraded`/`degraded_sources` when graph analytics are unavailable.

ChatMode type in web/src/types/chat.ts is "accept_edits" | "bypass" | "plan". The UI labels these as "Act", "Full Auto", and "Plan" respectively. When optimistically switching mode after plan approval, use "accept_edits" not "act".

Task #17408 added orphan tool_result rendering in src/gobby/sessions/transcript_render_blocks.py. If a ParsedMessage with content_type tool_result/mcp_tool_result cannot be paired to state.pending_tool_calls, the renderer now appends a synthetic completed tool_chain with tool_name msg.tool_name or 'unknown_result', id msg.tool_use_id or orphan-result-<index>, and ToolResult(content=msg.tool_result or msg.content). tests/sessions/test_orphan_tool_result_rendering.py covers full render, incremental/windowed render, preserved tool_use_id, no unknown block/log fallback, and paired result behavior.

Session title synthesis: Updated to use PromptLoader system (sessions/synthesize_title prompt), model='haiku' instead of default opus, max_tokens=30. Post-truncation safety net: first line only, strip quotes, cap at 100 chars. Manual rename validates title <= 200 chars (400 error). New prompt file at src/gobby/install/shared/prompts/sessions/synthesize_title.md.

Wiki activity tab canonical rebuild (#17043, commit 44ec580f5): WikiTab.tsx now composes a multi-file family using ActivityPanelSearch, top source list, ResizeHandle, bottom WikiDetailPanel with DetailPaneHeader, and QuickMenu row actions. Former WikiTab.utils behavior was moved into web/src/components/activity/wiki/WikiTabData.ts. Existing status-bar/command-bar buttons intentionally stay compact on touch due typographyLadder.test.ts expectations; the Wiki panel's own search/filter/refresh/list row controls meet the 44px mobile target.

In the Gobby repo, CodeIndexStorage is a public facade in src/gobby/code_index/storage.py composed from private mixins under src/gobby/code_index/_storage/. Keep prune_storage.py as a compatibility re-export, and keep code-index search helpers resolving through the gobby.search.keyword module at call time so monkeypatches on gobby.search.keyword.* affect storage search behavior.

Known spawned-agent activation symptom: Codex tech-writer agents stuck in `tech-writer-steps/claim` after already owning the task usually indicate SessionStart/default-agent activation reset the step workflow instead of preserving the existing workflow instance.

Watchdog architecture settled by epic #18693: the existing AgentLifecycleMonitor/IdleCheckHandler loop consumes an injected WatchdogReaderRegistry keyed by normalized provider ID; no second watchdog loop exists. Each reader implements async read(path) -> WatchdogTranscriptSnapshot. Snapshots are structural-only: bounded event summaries, allowlisted/coerced categories, timestamps and line numbers, with no transcript content fields; to_log_dict() preserves that redaction boundary. Malformed recognized records poison conclusiveness, well-formed unknown records are ignored, and invalid completion timestamps disable time-based recovery. Transcript path fallback is read-only: prefer a valid session transcript path, otherwise discover and cache per run without updating the session row, so supervision cannot mutate resumability or activity state.

Gobby/gcode PostgreSQL DSN handling no longer uses daemon-brokered database_url_ref runtime homes. Isolated gcode helper bootstraps write database_url directly; POST /api/local/runtime/database-url and local_cli_token DSN brokering were removed with the database_url_ref cleanup.

Droid installer support writes hooks to ~/.factory/hooks/hooks.json (or project .factory/hooks/hooks.json) and MCP config to ~/.factory/mcp.json with server field type="stdio". Gobby uses src/gobby/install/droid/hooks-template.json with exactly DROID_PASCAL_HOOK_NAMES and matcher only on PreToolUse/PostToolUse.

Plan registry lifecycle contract: LocalPlanManager.create_plan preserves an existing plan_id's root_task_ref, refuses archived rows unless reactivate=True, and archive_plan refuses an existing completed-file destination. Hook session lookup/registration serialization is keyed by (external_id, source) so unrelated hook sessions proceed concurrently.

In the daemon AI paths, Claude reasoning_effort does not flow through src/gobby/ai/_text_generation_adapters.py::_extend_reasoning_args; that helper is called for Grok, Codex, and Droid CLI adapters, and it intentionally has no claude-effort arm. Claude text/json generation uses ClaudeLLMProvider and passes effort through ClaudeAgentOptions via _claude_reasoning_options. ClaudeLLMProvider.describe_image/_describe_image_sdk intentionally do not accept or pass reasoning_effort for vision image descriptions. The public vision route and VisionExtractRequest do not carry reasoning_effort. Claude terminal-agent spawning still uses provider_capabilities.py plus command_builder.py to emit Claude CLI --effort.

Local model catalog discovery contract from #18444: LM Studio admits a model only when its metadata explicitly classifies it as an LLM/language model; missing or embedding/rerank/audio-style classifications are excluded. Ollama candidates from /api/tags, /api/ps, the configured default, and the OpenAI-compatible fallback are selectable only after POST /api/show returns a capabilities list containing completion. For LM Studio/Ollama, the local:<endpoint> default alias is emitted only when the configured canonical model is in that capability-qualified set; successful discovery with zero eligible models returns an explicit error and no models. Generic openai-compatible discovery keeps its configured default for daemon feature routing, while web-chat exclusion is enforced by the provider catalog route.

Workflow discovery merges filesystem entries before DB rows. In src/gobby/workflows/loader_discovery.py, DB definitions retain precedence over equal-named filesystem definitions, while an already-discovered project-scoped DB entry must be protected from a later global DB row so project-over-global shadowing is independent of list_all row order. An incoming project row may replace either global source.

Tool-chat limit consolidation implemented in task #18839 / commit 398fa1eae (2026-07-24). The sole authored version-1 contract is crates/gcore/contracts/tool_loop_limits.v1.json with defaults max_turns=null/unlimited, max_tool_calls=24, max_bytes_per_tool_result=16384, tool_timeout_seconds=300, and loop_timeout_seconds=1200 under ai.generation.tool_loop. scripts/generate_tool_loop_limits.py produces src/gobby/_generated_tool_loop_limits.py and supports --check for drift. Rust ToolExecutor is Send+Sync and Arc-backed; each tool runs on a bounded worker for min(tool timeout, remaining loop budget), per-tool timeout returns a capped error and continues, overall timeout stops the loop, and model transport retries are deadline-aware. gcode/gwiki use thread-safe read-only executors and the same limits for direct/daemon routes. Python accepts only an optional complete limits override; duplicate top-level max_turns and hardcoded caps are removed. Codex enforcement uses app-server dynamic tools/raw turn events with native tools disabled; Droid uses stream-JSON-RPC plus an isolated bearer-protected loopback MCP server. Missing required protocol capabilities raise CapabilityUnavailableError. The generated module lives at gobby package root (not gobby.ai) to avoid config.app -> config.ai -> gobby.ai circular initialization.

Build lifecycle automation is split across focused modules under src/gobby/build/: lifecycle.py owns build() orchestration, stage_manifest.py resolves manifests and automated leaf categories, target_branch.py handles target branch validation/cascade, validation.py owns option/artifact validators, project_controls.py owns build_stop/build_resume, and service.py is a compatibility facade for the public gobby.build.service imports.

Gobby strict 36-character UUID validation for resolver exact-match guards lives in `gobby.utils.uuid_validation.is_full_uuid`. `gobby.storage.session_resolution.is_session_uuid` intentionally remains broader for session UUID literals and should not be treated as equivalent to the strict helper.

Gobby gobby-agents send_message uses target-based routing: send_message(from_session, target, content, target_id=None, ...). Valid targets are session (target_id session ref), agent (agent run id), project (project id/name), build (build run id, build input ref, or root task ref), and all (no target_id). The legacy to_session and send_to_all inputs are intentionally unsupported.

Epic review must diff the plan artifact against its expansion-time git version, not the disk copy. Plan files in .gobby/plans/ can be overwritten by later unrelated work reusing the same plan_id/path (e.g. dream-stale-memory-reconciliation.md was rewritten by #18644 into a restore-reconciliation plan while epic #18612, expanded from commit f9f6970cf's 1610-line version, was still open). Reviewing #18612 against the disk copy would have produced a false total spec-compliance failure. Recover the review scope with: git log -- .gobby/plans/<plan>.md, then git show <expansion-commit>:.gobby/plans/<plan>.md.

Project testing convention: regression tests should not depend on transient live `.gobby/plans` files. Use clearly named static fixtures under `tests/fixtures/` for plan parser/expansion regression coverage; reserve live `.gobby/plans` for plan coverage CI and active plan state.

Droid CLI 0.146.0 has no documented no-history/no-recording flag for `droid exec`; Gobby suppresses Droid feature-generation session history by running each `DroidCLITextGenerateAdapter` request in a per-request temporary HOME/XDG tree and deleting it after success, failure, timeout, or subprocess setup failure. When `FACTORY_API_KEY` is absent, only non-history `~/.factory` auth/config support is seeded into the temp home; sessions, logs, temp, telemetry, cache/search, background task/process files, and history are excluded.

For attached tmux/CLI sessions, both `sessions.chat_mode` and `sessions.reasoning_effort` are stale. The chat_mode column defaults to 'plan' at row creation and is only updated from the web chat path (`update_chat_mode` in `src/gobby/storage/sessions/_field_update.py`); reasoning_effort is never updated by any path for tmux sessions. The freshest live values live in the `session_variables` table where workflow observers in `src/gobby/workflows/observers.py:451` write them when they parse transcript markers. Implication: any UI that displays an attached session's mode or reasoning effort cannot trust the `sessions` table columns alone — it must read `session_variables` or wait for a backend that writes back. This is why Drawbridge #148 hid the Plan|Act|YOLO picker in attached mode and dropped the Reasoning cell; sync work is filed under gobby-#14334.

Rule engine variable persistence architecture: The rule engine (RuleEngine.evaluate) mutates a variables dict in-place via set_variable effects, but the engine itself is stateless — it doesn't persist anything. The integration point is WorkflowHookHandler._evaluate_rules() in src/gobby/workflows/hooks.py, which loads variables from session_variables table (exclusively, as of v0.2.22 — the workflow_states.variables fallback was removed) and persists changes back after evaluation. Session variables are the single variable store for rules. WorkflowInstance.variables exists separately for per-workflow-instance state. Fixed in commit 0c563945.

Daemon restart now uses the legacy shutdown_source.json marker with an explicit intent field. stop intent cancels active agents with terminal_reason=daemon_stop; restart intent preserves tmux-backed active agent runs and skips child-process reap. Startup reconciliation lives in runner_lifecycle_agents._reconcile_agent_runs_after_restart and runs after tmux health before the lifecycle monitor/cron/pipeline recovery; it hydrates completion subscribers, refreshes live tmux pane PIDs, restarts tmux output readers, and cleans missing/dead tmux-backed active runs through the agent cleanup handler.

For Gobby/gwiki source lifecycle planning, gobby-cli will own the upstream JSON contracts for `gwiki sources --format json` and `gwiki remove-source --id <SOURCE_ID> --format json [--dry-run|--yes] [--keep-asset]`. Daemon/web should consume these only through `GwikiGateway`, add HTTP/MCP/web removal surfaces in `.gobby/plans/gwiki-daemon-web.md`, treat remove-source as an explicit write using CLI-returned `index_status`, and avoid adding source-removal work to `.gobby/plans/gwiki-daemon-ai-contract.md`.

`src/gobby/storage/sessions/_manager.py` is mixin composition plus `__init__` only, with separate mixins for bootstrap, CRUD, discovery, field updates, bulk updates, queries, lifecycle delegation, transcript processing, usage accounting, and terminal metadata. Public signature invariants in `tests/storage/test_sessions_import.py` are sensitive to exact `builtins.list[...]` annotations on `get_pending_transcript_sessions`, `get_sessions_since`, and `record_skills_used`; using plain `list[...]` breaks the compatibility test.

Agent tmux prompt automation is centralized in src/gobby/agents/terminal_prompt_monitor.py. AgentLifecycleMonitor delegates trust, loop, and approval prompt handling in that precedence order. Approval prompt auto-enter only sends Enter for detected spawned-agent tmux prompts and is gated by TmuxConfig.auto_enter_approval_prompts.

For Gobby frontend docs audits, the current product UI design authority is `.impeccable.md`; deployed runtime tokens are in `web/src/styles/tokens.css`, Tailwind semantic aliases are in `web/src/styles/tailwind-theme.css`, the app-level Tailwind entrypoint is `web/src/styles/index.css`, and theme/settings behavior is in `web/src/hooks/useSettings.ts`. The palette uses OKLCH values with dark as `:root` and light under `[data-theme="light"]`.

Scope note: `.impeccable.md` LOCKS the brand accent (hue 125 values) and the neutral-tint RULE (tint toward hue 125 at chroma 0.005-0.008, no pure #000/#fff). It does NOT lock the per-theme neutral RAMP lightness values/steps. So retuning the `:root` (dark) or `[data-theme="light"]` bg/border/text ladder in tokens.css is a legitimate change WITHOUT an `impeccable teach` update, as long as the tint rule and accent stay intact and WCAG 2.2 AA holds. Example: task #14714 (commit 81a3a1b60) reworked the light ramp (--bg-primary 99%->97% warm paper, even steps, --text-muted 51%->48% for AA on the deepest surface) with no contract edit. Verify AA empirically via chrome-devtools sRGB readback against computed tokens, not by eyeballing OKLCH L%.

Gobby's Qwen transcript parser intentionally supports only the current JSONL envelope `{type, message:{role, parts}}`; legacy aggregate/session shapes are removed. It expands thought text, visible text, functionCall, and functionResponse parts into sequential normalized records, assigns usage once per assistant envelope, suppresses `ui_telemetry` and `file_history_snapshot`, and preserves genuinely unknown record types/subtypes as unknown blocks. Established by tasks #16046 and #18352 in commit 0293d9925.

Provider inherit resolution: SessionSource values mostly match provider names directly. Only 3 divergent cases need normalization: claude_sdk -> claude, claude_sdk_web_chat -> claude, antigravity -> claude. Everything else (claude, gemini, codex, cursor, windsurf, copilot) passes through as-is. Don't create identity maps — just normalize the exceptions. For mode:self agents, provider inherit stays unresolved since no process is spawned.

Before executing any wiki-research spike, dedup-check for a prior identical run: look for wiki/outputs/<slug>-run-report.md, grep wiki/log.md for research_completed/research_run_completed lines, and search_tasks for the question keywords. Epic #17632's research spikes can duplicate already-run standalone tasks — #17628 was a verbatim duplicate of #17590 (same title/description/criteria); the run report, topic page, and investigation tasks (#17591, #17592) already existed, so the correct action was verify + close with a finding, not re-run (re-running would re-ingest sources and recreate the -2 duplicate-page problem cleaned in #17630).

Task #17266 decomposed `src/gobby/ai/registry.py` by extracting daemon capability binding construction into `src/gobby/ai/registry_builder.py`. `gobby.ai.registry` remains the public facade for enums, binding/status classes, `build_daemon_ai_capability_registry`, `PROVIDER_INSTALL_PROBE_TTL_SECONDS`, and `_whisper_runtime_available`. The facade passes those patch points into the builder so tests and monkeypatches under `gobby.ai.registry` keep working while source files stay under 1,000 lines.

In the Gobby project, save persistent memories via `gobby-memory.create_memory`, NOT the native Claude auto-memory system at `/Users/josh/.claude/projects/-Users-josh-Projects-gobby/memory/`. Hooks will block reads/writes to that directory. The UserPromptSubmit hook explicitly says: 'If the user told you something worth remembering across sessions, save it with create_memory on gobby-memory.' The native `Skill` tool is similarly off-limits — skills are managed via gobby-skills MCP (search_skills / get_skill). Applies only to this project; other projects use the default Claude auto-memory system.

Agent Definition Architecture (post-migration, Feb 2026):

The old AgentDefinition model (29 fields, in agents/definitions.py) has been DELETED along with WorkflowSpec, SkillProfileConfig, AgentDefinitionLoader, AgentDefinitionInfo, and AgentSource.

The single source of truth is now AgentDefinitionBody (15 fields, in workflows/definitions.py) stored in workflow_definitions table with workflow_type='agent'. Key schema:
- AgentDefinitionBody: name, description, role, goal, personality, instructions, provider, model, mode, isolation, base_branch, timeout, max_turns, workflows (AgentWorkflows), enabled
- AgentWorkflows: pipeline (str|None), rules (list[str]), variables (dict)

Loading pattern: Use LocalWorkflowDefinitionManager.list_all(workflow_type='agent') then AgentDefinitionBody.model_validate_json(row.definition_json). No intermediate conversion.

Key code locations:
- Model: src/gobby/workflows/definitions.py (AgentDefinitionBody, AgentWorkflows)
- Sync: src/gobby/agents/sync.py (YAML → DB sync at startup)
- Factory: src/gobby/mcp_proxy/tools/spawn_agent/_factory.py (_load_agent_body)
- Routes: src/gobby/servers/routes/agents.py (CRUD + import/export)
- Bundled agents: src/gobby/install/shared/agents/ (5 YAML files)
- Old agents: src/gobby/install/shared/agents/deprecated/

Runner (agents/runner.py) no longer loads agent definitions — the factory handles all definition merging before spawn.

Frontend attention reconciliation uses the roster cursor contract: subscribe to `agent_event` first, buffer `attention_changed` events while `/api/attention/roster` is in flight, discard same-epoch events at or below the snapshot seq, apply later events in sequence order, and refetch when the epoch changes. Aggregate blocked state by roster `entry_id` into session counts so clearing one run cannot clear a session that still has another blocked entry.

In the Gobby daemon worktree MCP tools, list_worktrees should resolve project context the same way get_worktree_stats does. For cross-project coordinator calls, accepting project_path and passing it through resolve_project_context prevents list output from diverging from stats/get_worktree_by_task visibility when the wrapper/session context points elsewhere.

For Gobby build coordination, do not manually tick `build_task` to advance lifecycle unless the user explicitly asks or a bug fix requires a controlled rerun. A root task can sit in `active_no_run` for normal reviewer spawn/worktree/code-index preflight; wait on dispatcher state with `get_build_status`, `explain_dispatch`, `list_running_agents`, and `wait_for_agent`. In the memory-recall-helper build, root #12898 advanced naturally through holistic QA and merge after waiting.

Workflow instance mutations use WorkflowInstanceMutation(session_id, workflow_name) with HubDatabase.transaction_immediate. Workflow-scoped variable merges and step-instance check-then-create paths in apply_persona and session activation share this lock so concurrent writes preserve both instance.variables and current_step.

Gobby hook contract/provider probe sessions should resolve to storage.projects.GLOBAL_PROJECT_ID (`_global`) rather than inheriting the daemon's current project or trying to resolve the temporary probe cwd. The probe cwd may still be preserved in raw provider payloads for fixture/contract fidelity.

As of task #18690, `tests/e2e/test_daemon_auth.py::test_ws_auth` validates standalone and HTTP `/ws` authentication. The direct ASGI `/ws` route rejects unauthenticated handshakes before accept, observed by real clients as HTTP 403; the former accept-then-close 4401 proxy behavior is obsolete. Frontend `useChat` connection creation is gated until auth loading completes and login succeeds. E2E daemons use `test_mode: true`, which bypasses production managed-service readiness while retaining isolated PostgreSQL and ports.

PromptLoader renders DB-backed prompts with Jinja StrictUndefined, preserves Jinja's built-in `default` filter (including the boolean third argument), and lets Jinja template errors propagate to callers. Its only custom Jinja filter is `untrusted`, backed by `delimit_untrusted_content`. Established by task #16254 / commit b065a9481.

Gobby stage-skip cleanup: runtime code should not read or write legacy `stage-:<name>` labels or `_skipped_stages`. Build/profile skip behavior is represented by task stage manifests (`task_stage_states`) and subtree cascade should initialize child manifests via `StageStatesManager.initialize_manifest`. Historical migration 234 remains the only place that replays `stage-:<name>`, `planning-round:N`, and `qa-attempts:N` labels; migration 237 removes `planning-round:N`/`qa-attempts:N` from stored task labels after replay.

runner_maintenance.py zombie cleanup pattern: The cleanup_zombie_messages_loop function expires undelivered inter-session messages to dead sessions. Key design points: (1) SQL must handle both ended_at < threshold AND ended_at IS NULL with started_at fallback, since crashed sessions never set ended_at. (2) The loop runs cleanup once immediately on startup before entering the sleep loop, so zombies from before a daemon restart don't wait a full interval. (3) The cleanup is extracted into a _expire_zombies() inner function to avoid duplication between the startup call and the loop body.

Build-triggered dispatcher ticks now take an explicit max_active_agents BuildOptions value and pass it to dispatcher.run_heartbeat. This fanout cap is separate from stage max_work_attempts, which remains a per-stage retry cap. Dispatcher spawn unavailability caused by missing daemon services is classified as heartbeat unavailability and must not append per-task spawn-failure audit markers or increment dispatch_failure_count.

## Provenance

- decision: confirmed

- repo: gobby

## Lesson
- principle: A shield loop that drains repeated caller cancellation must stop when the shielded task itself is done-cancelled and must establish required durable cleanup before propagating that inner cancellation.
- root_cause: The loop treated every CancelledError from asyncio.shield as a new cancellation of the caller, including the permanent CancelledError produced by re-awaiting an already-cancelled cleanup task.
- prevention: Catch inner cleanup cancellation inside the cleanup task to establish quarantine, then check cleanup_task.done() in the outer shield handler before retrying.

D5 gwiki research contract is documented in gobby-cli `docs/contracts/gwiki-research.md` (commit 6b5c5ba, task #15569). Design decision: `gwiki research` owns a standalone reason-act loop for mutating wiki research/audit notes and must not call `/api/agents/spawn` or expose daemon-dispatch flags (`--task-id`, `--agent-count`, `--resume`). Gobby enhancement stays outside gwiki through `--ai daemon`, cron, pipelines, and post-run agent review; gwiki keeps session.rs/checkpoint and compile note flow.

Config Resolution (DB-First, Two-Phase): Config is DB-first via config_store table (migration 98). YAML is import/export only. Phase 1 (runner.py:61): load_config() from yaml bootstraps database_path only. Phase 2 (runner.py:~95): After DB init, _maybe_import_yaml_to_db() one-time migrates yaml to DB, then load_config(config_store=...) loads from DB. Resolution: DB config_store > Pydantic defaults. $secret: and ${VAR} patterns resolved at load time via _resolve_config_values(). One-time import tracked by _meta.yaml_imported key. ConfigStore at src/gobby/storage/config_store.py with flatten_config()/unflatten_config(). deep_merge() in config/app.py. Gobby PostgreSQL client-pool sizing is pre-database bootstrap configuration: `postgres_pool` in bootstrap.yaml owns min_size=2, max_size=20, acquire_timeout_seconds=5.0, and open_timeout_seconds=30.0. Bootstrap validation requires positive finite values and min_size <= max_size. DaemonConfig carries this typed object into PostgresHubDatabase; config_store rows and legacy PGPOOL_* environment variables do not override it because the pool must open before config_store is readable.

Workflow variable evaluation architecture: `variables.get()` in session-lifecycle.yaml `when` expressions is architecturally correct. The `variables` dict is a merged dict combining workflow state variables AND session variables, with session_variables having override priority. The `session` object in eval context is a Session DB record (id, status, branch metadata), NOT a variables container. Do NOT replace variables.get() with session.* - this would break all workflows. The set_variable workflow action persists to workflow_states.variables, and the MCP set_variable tool persists to session_variables table. Both are loaded and merged before evaluation.

For MCP server listing responses in Gobby, `/api/mcp/servers` must not expose raw external server `env` or `headers` values. The safe public response keeps only values that are explicit `$secret:` references; raw tokens or header values are stripped from the unauthenticated list response. Implemented for task #17175 in `src/gobby/servers/routes/mcp/endpoints/server.py` with regression coverage in `tests/servers/test_mcp_routes.py`.

Task #14625 translates the memory knowledge graph implementation from Neo4j HTTP Cypher to FalkorDB: `MemoryManager` now wires `FalkorClient` via `databases.falkordb` when `requirepass` is set, `KnowledgeGraphService` and `CodeGraph` accept `falkor_client`, Falkor writes use `timestamp()` and `vecf32()`, and daemon source should contain no literal `apoc.` fragments under `src/gobby`.

Agent cancellation MCP tools should share `gobby.mcp_proxy.tools.agent_cancellation.stop_agent_run(...)` so each cancellation runs the same kill process, `terminalize_cancelled_agent_run(...)`, and terminal artifact cleanup path. `cancel_stale_helpers` and `stop_agent` both delegate there as of task #15205.

Codex terminal completed-turn recovery in IdleCheckHandler uses a redacted rollout snapshot: the last eight response_item summaries plus the latest event_msg task_started/task_complete marker. Expedited continuation requires an active run, stale Codex child session, no pane safety block, a fully parseable transcript, and task_complete older than the run's base idle timeout. A fresh task_complete suppresses intervention during the grace window; task_complete continuation precedes the reasoning watchdog and still counts toward max idle reprompts.

SECURITY FIX: ExitPlanMode timeout was fail-open (auto-approved after 600s), which allowed an agent to build a full auth system without user approval when combined with the PlanApprovalBar being hidden by an isStreaming guard. The root cause chain: (1) PlanApprovalBar hidden by !isStreaming guard (fixed in #9048), (2) 600s timeout auto-approved (fixed in #9049 to fail-closed with request_changes). Design principle: all permission timeouts in chat_session_permissions.py should fail-closed (deny/request_changes), never fail-open. Tool approval timeout already correctly failed closed (line 375: reject). The ExitPlanMode timeout was the exception.

Rule YAML and update payloads cross a shared boundary at split_rule_definition_data in src/gobby/workflows/definitions.py. It copies the input, hoists row metadata fields name/description/enabled/priority/tags, and validates the remaining dict with strict RuleDefinitionBody. Bundled sync, MCP update_rule, HTTP rule updates, and isolated bundled-rule fixtures use this boundary; explicit API metadata takes precedence over embedded metadata. Implemented in #18395 / 89ce7ed20.

Runner degradation invariant after #16609 and #18371: GobbyRunner initializes degraded_services as a set before runner_init phases. Initialization failures and unavailable configured dependencies add stable service names; runtime monitors report state through lifecycle callbacks that add the service on degradation and discard it on recovery. The admin /health and /status payloads expose degraded_services in sorted order and report degraded status whenever the set is non-empty; CLI status renders the entries. The stderr resource monitor uses stderr_capture_over_limit and leaves the live capture file intact because safe rotation requires coordinated descriptor reopening (#12010/#13910). Features absent by configuration are not recorded as degraded.

Transcript index sidecars include session_id in the persisted payload and load validation, so callers that know the session should pass session_id to load_index_sidecar/get_or_build_index to prevent cross-session cache reuse.

Gobby web frontend lives under /web/ (React + TypeScript + Vite). Components are in web/src/components/, hooks in web/src/hooks/, and styling is centralized under web/src/styles/. The web API proxy targets the local Gobby daemon HTTP service on port 60887; current daemon bind host is 0.0.0.0.

Gobby daemon live wake notifications for tmux-backed CLIs must paste the plain notification text and then send a separate raw tmux Enter key event. Do not rely on trailing newline text for Codex, Claude, Gemini, or other TUI CLIs; the wake dispatcher should pass submit=True for tmux paths and keep newline-bearing prompts only for SDK resume paths.
Take proper care with every task. Don't rush or try to burn through tasks. Rely on the Gobby daemon to manage context (compaction, session persistence). Quality over speed.

A Go CLI strangler fig migration feasibility study was completed and written to docs/research/go-cli-strangler-fig.md (#8893). CompletionEventRegistry is confined to one asyncio event-loop thread. notify() snapshots subscribers before awaiting wake callbacks, so callback-driven subscription changes apply only to later notifications. If cleanup removes a notified result before wait() resumes, wait() raises the public CompletionResultEvictedError instead of leaking a raw KeyError. Established by task #15959 / commit b356d7185.

When require-clean-tree-before-status blocks close_task because of files I haven't touched in this session (pre-existing handoff state, or concurrent-agent diffs landing during the session), escalate to the user instead of stashing. Why: stashing looks reversible but isn't safe in practice. The branch can evolve (other commits land on the same files) while the stash sits, leaving the stash obsolete or contradicting newer commits. Concrete case in epic #13989: stashed a session-handoff batch to clear the close gate; commits #14058 and #14055 then landed on the same files, making the stash partially obsolete with unsafe --theirs resolutions (would have stripped a WHERE id IS NOT NULL SQL guard in src/gobby/build/service.py). How to apply: surface immediately, options to present include escalate_task, asking the user to commit/discard/claim the unrelated work, or explicit user approval to stash with the understanding that branch evolution can render the stash unsafe to restore. Do not bury the decision in a final summary.

Live web-chat provider-selection integration contract from #18449 (commit 78e9f2568): ChatInputModelControls must open the catalog-aware ProviderPicker; a separate execution-provider-only select leaves local catalog groups unreachable. Gobby storage managers use HubDatabase. HubDatabase.transaction_immediate requires a typed LockTarget; production callers cannot open a lockless immediate transaction. Hub adapters reuse an ambient transaction for nested manager calls and enforce strictly increasing lock-target priorities to prevent AB/BA deadlocks. Outer BuildDryRunMutation uses priority 50 so nested task locks remain ordered; GitHubIssueTriageMutation uses 150 before TaskSeqAllocation at 200; IntegrationWorkspaceMutex uses 350. Existing targets include AgentCapAdmission, TaskSeqAllocation, DispatchMutexRow, TaskSubtreeCascade, TaskLifecycleMutation, session locks, and ChatAttachmentMutation.

Task review lifecycle tools are now stage-native: mark_task_needs_review, mark_task_review_approved, and mark_task_review_rejected resolve the current task_stage_states row and call StageStatesManager.submit_for_review, approve_review, and reject_review respectively. They leave task.status as a compatibility projection instead of writing legacy needs_review/review_approved/rejected statuses; non-review stages like test_arch/prd should use gobby-tasks-ops:complete_stage.

Context window usage calculation: The context window (e.g. 200k for Claude) is an INPUT limit. Output tokens do NOT occupy it. Correct formula: context_load = input_tokens + cache_creation_input_tokens + cache_read_input_tokens. Percentage = context_load / context_window. Output tokens should be shown separately in tooltips but never added to the numerator. The DB field usage_input_tokens stores the total (uncached + cache components), so when hydrating uncachedInputTokens for display, compute: total - cache_read - cache_creation.

ACP transcript tool_call_update statuses use pending/in_progress for intermediate updates and completed/failed for terminal updates. Grok transcript parsing should emit tool_result records only for the terminal completed/failed statuses; the shared typed-JSON parser carries the enclosing toolCalls entry's status into ParsedMessage.tool_result.

Progressive-discovery redesign decision (2026-07-22): preserve server inventory and per-tool schema leases across daemon restarts; reset only schema leases on genuine context loss (clear/compact or resume with pending_context_reset). Normal known-tool flow becomes call_tool when leased, or get_tool_schema then call_tool after context loss. list_tools is only for an unknown tool name; list_mcp_servers is only for explicit registry inspection. Keep strict schema-before-call enforcement to prevent guessed arguments. Also fix session_start ordering: clear-pending-context-reset-on-start currently runs at priority 5 before reset consumers (memory priority 5 by name; discovery/skill priority 80), and rule evaluation sees prior mutations, so cleanup must run after all consumers. Update active prompts, skills, agent definitions, AGENTS.md, and user/operator docs to teach the new contract.

`gobby install` VS Code-family terminal integration is consent-gated: `--ide-settings/--no-ide-settings` is tri-state, interactive unspecified prompts Yes only for detected IDEs needing changes, and non-interactive unspecified skips mutation. On POSIX, the installer preserves any existing custom `tmux` profile, otherwise creates one from `shutil.which("tmux")` with `args: ["new-session"]`, selects it as the platform default, adds `${sequence}` titles, and keeps Antigravity tabs visible.

In the Codex app-server adapter, streaming run_turn notifications should be scoped using the notification top-level threadId and the nested turn.id/turnId fields; unscoped shared turn/* and item/* handlers can cross-deliver events between concurrent turns.

As of commit 205bba761 (task #16280), MCP env/header persistence encrypts high-confidence credential slots in SecretStore and stores deterministic $secret refs. Managed secret identity includes persistence domain (database/file), project scope, server, field, and key; an ownership-hash description gates cleanup so operator-owned explicit refs are never deleted. Database upsert/update/remove operations are transactional, file saves use atomic replacement plus rollback compensation, and stale managed secrets are removed when slots are updated or deleted.

Autonomous progress/stuck detection state is DB-backed: hook PostToolUse traffic records loop_progress via ProgressTracker, task suggestions record task_selection_history via StuckDetector, and separate ProgressTracker/StuckDetector instances on the same HubDatabase can share that persisted state.

Artifact panel editing state architecture: isEditing and showSource state are owned by ArtifactPanel (parent), not by ArtifactCodeView/ArtifactTextView (children). The Edit/View and Source/Preview toggle buttons live in the ArtifactPanel header row as icon-sized buttons alongside Copy, Download, and Close. ArtifactCodeView and ArtifactTextView accept isEditing and showSource as props. This eliminates the full-width button bar that each child component previously rendered. Show Edit/View when onUpdateContent is defined (editable). Show Source/Preview only for read-only text artifacts (type=text, no onChange).

Design decision for task #14312: full project-scoped custom category registry is a post-0.4.0 platform feature, but #14312 should stay narrower and provide docs-category development review routing to a docs-reviewer/doc-reviewer without implementing arbitrary custom categories yet. GitHub triage webhook authentication must not disclose project existence or triage enabled state. In GitHubIssueTriageService.accept_webhook_delivery, verify the configured HMAC before checking enabled flags; unknown/deleted projects use an unverifiable sentinel HMAC key so the validation path still runs. Raise WebhookAuthenticationError for missing/invalid/unresolvable signatures and disabled/unknown projects, and map it to the single public 401 detail `GitHub webhook authentication failed`.

When adding scope columns to a DB table for the DB-first pattern (bundled/global/project), the create() method must auto-infer scope='project' when project_id is provided and scope is the default 'global'. Without this, existing callers that pass project_id without explicit scope will create records with scope='global', breaking the SQL scope precedence query (ORDER BY CASE scope WHEN 'project' THEN 1...).

Strategic direction behind epic #17425 (remote/shared Gobby stack over Tailscale). Josh wants Gobby's data model to anticipate four future angles (NOT in #17425's scope, but its seams must not block them): (1) work from any machine on his tailnet; (2) fleet management — control multiple Gobby daemons/stacks from a central interface; (3) monetization requiring a shared auth platform — e.g. a sold mobile app that connects to your daemons, or going closed-source and moving chunks into a Rust hub-and-spoke binary against hosted services; (4) local auth hardening sooner (servers/routes/auth.py is untested).

Key architectural facts discovered (2026-06-27): The Gobby daemon is effectively SINGLE-FILESYSTEM — hooks are processed server-side (servers/routes/mcp/hooks.py), so the daemon reads the client's cwd/transcript_path and runs agents/worktrees/git-commits on ITS OWN disk. So a remote machine pointed at a shared stack only works as a management/metadata plane; instrumented local coding from arbitrary machines needs a rearchitecture (ship transcript content not paths, path-independent project resolution, per-machine/remote agent execution) — deferred to follow-up epics.

Secrets were machine_id-coupled (storage/secrets.py derives the Fernet key from machine_id) — epic #17425 replaces this with envelope encryption (random DEK wrapped by a swappable KEK: default 0600 key-file like .secret_salt, opt-in scrypt-passphrase, future user/token). Gobby does NOT use OS keyring (database_url_ref was removed). Identity seam decision: owner_user_id lives on a new machines registry ONLY (user derivable session->machine->user), not scattered as user_id across tables. Client-dial endpoint contract lives in crates/gcore/src/daemon_url.rs (GOBBY_DAEMON_URL > GOBBY_PORT > bootstrap daemon_url > bind_host-derived > default; dial normalization) — in-repo since the former gobby-cli workspace merged into the gobby monorepo. Sentence collision fix in websocket/chat.py: The has_sent_text flag tracks whether any text was sent in the current turn, independent of accumulated_text flushes. The old check `if accumulated_text and not accumulated_text.endswith(...)` was always False because accumulated_text was already flushed to '' by ToolCallEvent handler before the separator check ran. Gobby embedding routing lesson: EmbeddingService must preserve EmbeddingsConfig.query_prefix through generate_embedding(s) into _apply_prefix, while the HTTP embeddings route intentionally rejects non-null provider/project_id with 400 because route-level provider/project routing is unsupported.

The daemon startup health check failure ('Daemon started but health check failed') is caused by the HTTP server (uvicorn) starting last in runner.py's run() method — after MCP connect_all (10s timeout), VectorStore init, and several other async steps. The health endpoint is at /admin/health (defined in servers/routes/admin.py). The CLI health check polls this endpoint from daemon.py. With 5000+ tasks and VectorStore rebuilds, startup can take 60+ seconds. The max_wait was increased from 15s to 120s. A future improvement would be starting uvicorn earlier in run() so the health endpoint is available before other initialization completes.

ACP web-chat '[object Object]' tool-error bug (task #15705): Gemini/ACP CLIs send `session/request_permission` JSON-RPC requests (params: sessionId, options[{optionId,kind}], toolCall) to the client (Gobby) for tools needing approval. Gobby's `handle_client_request` in src/gobby/adapters/acp_client_requests.py only handled `terminal/create` and returned JSON-RPC error -32601 ('Unknown client request method') for everything else. The Gemini CLI (Node) renders that rejected-permission error object to the model as the literal string '[object Object]', so every approval-gated tool (mcp_gobby_* MCP tools, and non-allowlisted shell commands like gcode/uv/file) fails, triggering a 75s+ runaway diagnostic loop with no plan. Safe/read-only shell (echo, ls, pwd, git status) auto-approves inside the CLI so it succeeds. Grok is immune because Gobby launches it with --always-approve so it never sends request_permission. Fix: implement `session/request_permission` in handle_client_request to auto-approve by selecting an allow-kind option (outcome {outcome:selected, optionId}); CLI-agnostic, also protects qwen. Reproduce via GeminiACPClient directly with a prompt that forces an MCP/gcode tool call.

WebhookExecutor security and response-limit contract: task #16829 / commit 0be30028c resolves each HTTP(S) target before connecting, rejects every non-global DNS address, pins validated results into aiohttp's connector, disables redirects, and uses capped RetryConfig backoff. As of task #18370 / commit c12672751, response capture reads at most 1 MiB plus one detection byte and returns a typed response_too_large failure on overflow with no partial success body. Diagnostics count decompressed bytes captured, expose Content-Length as total_bytes only under identity encoding, sanitize URL credentials/query/fragment, and include webhook_id for registry execution.

Frontend bundle policy: web/vite.config.ts sets chunkSizeWarningLimit to 1300 kB. Closed-by-default App modals (QuickCaptureTask, ResumeSessionModal, and SlashCommandModal) are lazy-loaded and only mounted while open so the main entry bundle remains below that ceiling.
