Current Gobby plan manifest category/TDD policy: approved implementation-plan expansion may emit only development-forward leaf categories (`code`, `config`, `docs`, `refactor`, `test`). Only `code` and `config` manifest entries are TDD-eligible. `research`, `planning`, and `manual` are valid for direct task creation outside expansion manifests, but Plan-Coverage Contract manifests and compiled expansion specs reject them so gobby build does not launch discovery-stage agents from approved plans.

mode_level architecture: Numeric autonomy level (0=Plan, 1=Act, 2=Full Auto) derived from chat_mode + plan_mode via compute_mode_level() in observers.py. plan_mode=True always forces level 0. mode_level is a workflow session variable synced in 4 places: (1) session-lifecycle.yaml on_after_tool for EnterPlanMode/ExitPlanMode, (2) _handle_set_mode() in chat.py on UI slider change, (3) detect_plan_mode_from_context() for system-reminder detection, (4) on_session_start/on_before_agent for init. Existing plan_mode boolean is kept for backward compat; _is_plan_mode() in _agent.py prefers mode_level when available.

Skill scope uniqueness is enforced by UNIQUE NULLS NOT DISTINCT (name, project_id, source), and soft-deleted skill rows remain part of that constraint. Scope-move destination collision checks must query with include_deleted=True and the exact destination source/project scope.

Implemented in gobby-#15359 (commit 8f2690076): web transcript-backed session detail now keeps a bounded frontend window of rendered transcript groups via `sessionTranscriptWindow.ts`. The hook opens tail-first, keeps at most `TRANSCRIPT_PAGE_SIZE * 5` groups, evicts the far edge on older/newer paging, exposes `hasNewer`/`loadNewer`/`isLoadingNewer`/`setTranscriptAtBottom`, and only appends live/refreshed tail rows when the loaded window is tail-contiguous and the viewer is at bottom; otherwise totals advance and downward scroll refetches.

Gobby shutdown intent writes two markers: persistent `shutdown_source.json` for status/last-shutdown attribution and consuming `shutdown_intent_active.json` for hook guards and signal handling. `read_shutdown_intent()` consumes only the active marker; `read_shutdown_source_record()` reads the persistent marker without consuming it; `/api/admin/status.last_shutdown` prefers the persistent marker and falls back to the active marker.

Admin status for FalkorDB should emit `memory.falkordb` from `get_falkordb_status(db=server.services.database, host/port/password from server.config.databases.falkordb)`. The `configured` flag is predicate-driven via `is_falkordb_enabled(config.databases)`, so it stays true after graph clients are cleared and operators see installed/unhealthy instead of not-configured.

YAML `>` folded scalar pitfall: Lines with MORE indentation than the first content line preserve the preceding newline instead of folding it to a space. This caused a critical bug in command-mcp-tool-restriction where `not in` on an extra-indented line produced `...)
  not in ...` — a SyntaxError in ast.parse(mode='eval'). Because _evaluate_condition in rule_engine.py uses fail_closed=True for block effects, the SyntaxError defaulted to blocking ALL tools unconditionally. Fix: (1) keep all continuation lines at same indent in YAML `>` blocks, (2) SafeExpressionEvaluator._normalize_expr() now collapses whitespace before parsing as defense-in-depth.

Confirmed review lessons from task #18674: (1) infrastructure-category validation outcomes persist as validation_status=error while ordinary verdict failures remain invalid and retain their own retry counters; (2) synchronous agent/skill database lookups in async dispatch paths must run through asyncio.to_thread; (3) Git failure classification uses specific environment markers for checkout/clone/fetch/worktree failures, while verification commands such as git diff --check, git diff --exit-code, and git apply --check are code evidence unless explicit test-failure evidence is present; (4) merge workers terminate only after record_merge_result persists success or failure, so merge_start errors remain in the merge stage through corrected retry and failure recording; (5) validation infrastructure backoff must use the authoritative escalate_task transition at the consecutive-failure threshold and return retryable=false, escalated=true, and the failure count without changing the original failure type/category/message; (6) PostgreSQL test orphan cleanup holds the shared advisory drop lock across schema scan and every DROP SCHEMA, releasing it in finally to serialize with xdist teardown.

The wiki MCP URL-ingest freshness boundary is `wiki_ingest(max_age_hours=...)` in `src/gobby/mcp_proxy/tools/wiki.py`, forwarded to `GwikiGateway.ingest_url` and emitted as `gwiki ingest-url --max-age-hours <n>`. The operational range is 0..=8760 via `MAX_URL_AGE_HOURS`; file `path`/`paths` combinations return a structured URL-only validation error, and the gateway rejects out-of-range values before spawning gwiki. `wiki_ingest` uses explicit `InternalToolRegistry.register` schema metadata so its JSON schema advertises minimum 0 and maximum 8760.

Quick-build dispatcher contract from #18637 (commit 060ccadda): when a stage pipeline that was already started by a bounded interactive build completes into a required-review state after the initial tick, schedule exactly one task-scoped continuation (`explicit_task_ids=(task_id,)`, `max_ticks=1`, `max_actions=1`). The continuation may select that task while `allow_automation=false`, but it must not re-enable persistent automation; normal dispatcher mutex, eligibility, and duplicate-review protections still apply.

Fix for debug_echo_context persisting after YAML change: Changing debug_echo_context from true to false in workflow YAML (e.g., claude-sdk-lifecycle.yaml) does NOT take effect for existing sessions because persisted workflow state variables take precedence over YAML defaults. Fix: use set_session_variable(name="debug_echo_context", value="false", session_id="#N") via gobby-workflows MCP server. Session variables (_session_variables_override) have highest precedence per evaluate_all_lifecycle_workflows. New sessions inherit the YAML default. The duplicate [DEBUG additionalContext] injection was caused by the debug echo re-injecting the same additionalContext as a system_message with prefix.

Task #18794 / commit 4a4368357 hardens `gobby test-types audit`: structurally valid mypy diagnostics resolving outside the project root are dropped individually, and exit 1 remains trustworthy when all such diagnostics are filtered; requested out-of-root targets remain rejected. Python discovery now uses `Path.walk()` and prunes `.git`, `.mypy_cache`, `.venv`, `__pycache__`, `dist`, `node_modules`, and `target` relative to the audit root. Shared test-quality/test-types baseline writes chmod the completed temporary file to `0o666 & ~umask` before atomic replace, with cleanup on chmod/replace failures. Validation: 124 focused tests passed, strict mypy passed 21 source files, Ruff and test-quality passed, and the repository test-types ratchet reported 0 new errors with the committed baseline unchanged.

Gobby pre-push `frontend_tests` runs the full `cd web && npm test` suite. Current Qwen provider-model labels intentionally strip trailing transport/source suffixes like `(qwen-oauth)` and `(openai)` via `parseQwenModelInfo`, so UI tests should assert sanitized labels such as `Coder Model` and `GPT 5`, not raw suffix text.

Task #18544 added the reusable terminal controls used by the activity-panel live-terminal integration. TerminalSessionPicker is a controlled Radix Select over JoinedTerminalSession keyed by `${socket}:${name}`; matched Gobby rows reuse ActivityRowStatusDot with `Session <status>` labels, while dead, agent-managed, and external state remains visible as text badges. TerminalKeysBar is the sole keyboard/touch input surface and emits composed text plus CR, Esc `\x1b`, Tab `\t`, Enter `\r`, arrows `\x1b[A`/`\x1b[B`, Ctrl+C `\x03`, and bare prompt digits 1/2/3 through sendInput. Commit 2fc0b3fa1.

Web UI font rule: mono/monospace font should ONLY be used for code editors and tool use blocks inside the web chat. Everything else (task refs, file paths, session refs, labels, navigation) uses the base sans-serif font. No font-mono on refs like #123, file paths in status bars, or any non-code UI elements.

LocalAgentRunManager derives active agent-run tool_calls_count and turns_used from linked session rows on read: child session stats win when a child session row exists, parent session stats are used only for active runs without a child session row, and persisted agent_runs counters remain authoritative for terminal runs. AgentRun.to_brief includes those counters so gobby-agents.list_running_agents exposes live activity.

Agents v3 sentinel convention: `inherit` is the universal sentinel meaning 'resolve from runtime context.' Used for provider (→ CLI source), model (→ CLI default), and base_branch (→ current git branch). One word, one concept, everywhere. Don't use `self` (already a mode value), `current` (was used for isolation and renamed to `none`), or identity maps. Also: don't create tasks before a plan is approved — finish the plan first, get approval, then expand.

User does not manually run local CI Docker workflows for Gobby; git hooks and agent-driven validation handle CI, so local CI-only Docker images are disposable unless actively being used for debugging.

Rule ownership convention: ad hoc single-file rule imports use the `user` tag, while bundled directory sync uses the `gobby` tag. Bundled orphan cleanup selects installed rules by the bundled sync tag, so user-tagged imports remain outside bundled ownership and cleanup.

In gcode codewiki module docs, rendered ModuleDoc.component_ids should describe only direct module member files. The module prompt path still uses prompt_component_ids_for_module to include transitive descendant component labels/IDs, but the Markdown Components section should not roll up descendants because high-level pages become unreadable.

Gobby web activity-panel row consistency convention (epic #16998 cleanup). ALL top-list row classes bind their height to ONE token: min-height: var(--activity-panel-row-height) (= 2.25rem / 36px, defined in web/src/styles/tokens.css). The four row classes are: .session-entry (sessions-tab.css), .activity-list-row (chat/styles/activity-panel.css — the shared canonical row used by migrated list tabs: agents, rules, memory, skills, stages, profiles, pipelines-defs, wiki, integrations, AND FileChanges/Changes), .activity-task-row (tasks/task-execution.css), and .pipeline-exec-row (chat/styles/pipelines-tab.css — Traces, Cron, Pipelines runs). SELECTED-state convention is uniform across all of them: background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 8%, transparent) (NOT a gray bg-muted tint, NOT a >1px side-stripe — banned by .impeccable.md BAN 1). Canonical row typography: title = .activity-row-title (var(--text-base)/14px, font-weight-medium, truncate); secondary = .activity-row-meta (var(--text-sm)/12px, normal, tabular-nums). When adding/auditing any activity tab, compose these classes rather than hand-rolling row height/selected/typography. Verified via CSSOM + live computed styles 2026-06-14.

For Gobby plan-file expansion only (no development), use `uv run gobby build --quick --planning-seed-state approved --no-merge <plan-file>`. Dry-run first to confirm the lifecycle is exactly `expansion`; without `--no-merge`, default isolation may append `merge`. The `["expansion"]`-only manifest from quick+approved applies only at first creation: an existing build root's persisted stage manifest is reused on re-invocation and survives `gobby build clean`. On both fresh and reuse paths, `--quick` runs one dispatcher tick then disarms automation for the whole task tree (set_automation_for_task_tree false), so a full-manifest root still stops after the current stage; resume later with plain `gobby build <plan-file>`.

ToolEventHandlerMixin.handle_after_tool consumes normalized write metadata (`canonical_tool_kind=write`, `canonical_repo_mutation=true`, and `canonical_file_paths`) for shell edit tracking. Each normalized path flows through the existing repo/internal/gitignore checks and SessionVariableManager.record_edited_file, which also invalidates verification evidence.

In gobby-cli, the unified Obsidian vault contract for gwiki/gcode uses `code/` for gcode-generated codewiki pages, `knowledge/` for synthesized knowledge pages, and `_meta/` for shared metadata. gcode codewiki emits shared frontmatter keys such as `source`, `provenance`, `generated_by: gcode-codewiki`, `trust`, and `freshness`. Do not add or preserve legacy `wiki/**` compatibility paths when changing gwiki or codewiki.

Web session activity filters are persisted per effective project under `gobby-sessions-filters:<project-id>` (with `:all` for no project), preventing task-reference filters from leaking across projects.

In Gobby's memory VectorStore, full rebuilds are intentionally non-destructive when the existing Qdrant collection has the configured embedding dimension: rebuild upserts regenerated vectors, then deletes stale point IDs after successful upserts. Collection delete/recreate is reserved for dimension mismatches and is serialized with collection lifecycle locking.

Managed native-binary version parsing is centralized in src/gobby/install/version_probe.py. probe_native_bin_version extracts the numeric semantic version from decorated `--version` output (for example `ghook 0.4.5 (build abc)` -> `0.4.5`), and distribution._probe_helper_version delegates to it while passing distribution.subprocess.run to preserve the module's test seam.

Pipeline execution discovery is now fully exposed: list_pipeline_executions and search_pipeline_executions MCP tools on gobby-workflows server, CLI subcommands (gobby pipelines executions, gobby pipelines search), HTTP endpoint (GET /api/pipelines/executions/search). Storage layer search_executions() uses LEFT JOIN step_executions with LIKE-based text search across pipeline names and step errors/outputs. The previous API gap (no list/search without knowing execution ID) is closed.

Merge tooling bug fix #14888: gobby-merge verify_in_worktree(final=true) must enforce a clean git worktree after the verification command succeeds. Previously final verification ignored the final flag and allowed merge campaigns to record success with staged/dirty files. Commit 70f841d7e adds a post-command `git status --porcelain` check and returns dirty file details on failure while leaving non-final verification permissive.

Qwen typed JSON transcripts may report usage as tokens:{input, output, cached, thoughts, tool, total}. In gobby.sessions.token_usage.typed_json_token_usage, input includes cached tokens and maps to input_tokens=max(0,input-cached); cached maps to cache_read_tokens; output+thoughts maps to output_tokens; tool is excluded because it is a subset of input.

Web chat routing exposes addSystemMessage through ChatState so synchronous routing failures can surface visible local feedback. useChatPageSessionRouting validates a web-chat target against conversations.sessions before parking the current chat or dismissing the mobile panel; missing targets append a local system message and leave UI/session state unchanged.

In gobby-cli gwiki session ingest, Droid/Factory CLI local transcripts are raw JSONL with a `session_start` record (`version`, `cwd`/`sessionTitle`, `hostId`) followed by `message` records containing `message.role` and typed `message.content` blocks. The Droid adapter should require `session_start` before claiming generic `message` rows, skip `visibility: "llm_only"` or `context-*` records, render `tool_use` / `tool_result` blocks, and use `GWIKI_DROID_ARCHIVE_FIXTURE` for env-gated real fixture validation.

LLMProvider base abstraction and bridge adapters were removed. Text capability routing now exposes native `ClaudeTextGenerateAdapter` and `LocalTextGenerateAdapter`; vision routing exposes `ClaudeVisionExtractAdapter` and `LocalVisionExtractAdapter`. Runtime code should use feature-routed AI capability adapters plus shared primitives like `LLMTextResult` and `LLMProviderCancellation`, not an `LLMProvider` ABC or generic LLMProvider bridge adapters.

Gobby build child-merge recovery: if a child task is stuck in merge because its source worktree metadata exists but the parent integration worktree DB row is missing, the intended repair is `gobby build <child-ref> --target-branch <target>`. The code now ensures/adopts the nearest parent integration workspace for child resume and workspace merge recovery instead of requiring a full epic rebuild.

FastAPI test patterns learned during coverage push:

1. isinstance with lazy imports: When route handlers do `from gobby.storage.database import LocalDatabase; isinstance(db, LocalDatabase)`, MagicMock fails. Fix: autouse fixture patching `gobby.storage.database.LocalDatabase` with `MagicMock` class so isinstance(MagicMock(), MagicMock) returns True.

2. Test directory naming conflicts: Never name a test directory after a Python package (e.g., tests/servers/routes/mcp/ clashes with the `mcp` package). Use `mcp_endpoints/` instead.

3. FastAPI dependency_overrides: Routes using Depends(get_server) need `app.dependency_overrides[get_server] = override_fn` instead of `create_X_router(mock_server)` pattern.

4. Exception re-wrapping: If a route catches HTTPException(503) inside a generic `except Exception`, it re-raises as 500. Check the actual handler logic when writing test assertions.

5. Installer backup-before-read order: copy2 (backup) runs before open (read), so making a file unreadable causes 'Failed to create backup' not 'Failed to read'.

Do not restart the gobby daemon during implementation or verification. The user frequently has agents running that depend on the daemon — restarting would disrupt active work. Run tests to verify, let the user restart at their convenience.

Interactive/delegated planning review rejection uses `mark_task_review_rejected(task_id, rejection_notes, round=None)`, which returns planning-review tasks to `open` and appends `## Adversary Findings — Round N`. This replaced an earlier, abandoned `changes_requested` task status. Follow-on work for interactive/delegated planning should use this review-rejected/open round-trip contract, not a new status enum.

ACP auth in Gobby follows ACP 1.0 initialize authMethods plus agentCapabilities.auth.logout. Store advertised auth methods on the ACP client/session, call authenticate with the selected methodId, and call logout only when auth.logout is advertised. This remains separate from Gobby Plan/Act/YOLO chat_mode; auth UI belongs in existing session/chat controls, not a new Activity Panel.

Claude watchdog transcripts use assistant, user, and system records. Safe recovery treats a valid system subtype=turn_duration record with nonnegative integer durationMs/messageCount and a valid timestamp as completed; every valid user record, including tool-result-shaped content, immediately supersedes any earlier completion as latest_turn_kind=started. Assistant isApiErrorMessage=true maps to diagnostic provider_error_kind=api_error and never to conclusive capacity. A structural audit on 2026-07-22 covered 349,093 assistant, 198,737 user, and 5,164 system records with zero legitimate-shape rejections under the reader contract. Keep all raw content/error values out of WatchdogTranscriptSnapshot.

Gobby build config loading and profile resolution live in src/gobby/config/build.py. load_build_config merges BuildConfig defaults, ~/.gobby/build.yaml, <project_root>/.gobby/build.yaml, then flag overrides, normalizing clones_dir to Path and merging profiles by profile name. resolve_profile supports quick, review, full, full-yolo, and auto mappings: plan_file -> review, leaf/default -> quick, epic with plan -> full, epic without plan -> ValueError.

Task #18727 (commit 80f12cd87) extended review-learning taxonomy. SourceKind now includes plan_review and task_validation; SOURCE_KIND_DOMAIN is the total fail-closed source-to-domain map and CODE_DOMAIN_EXCLUDED_TAGS centralizes plan exclusion. Every newly normalized lesson receives lesson-domain:<code|plan>; check_key/category findings get explicit enumeration tags. Reserved plan-review and epic-qa pattern namespaces validate class-scoped pattern_id components against explicit kebab-case check_key (and plan category), while ReviewLearningService preserves existing record signatures and honors explicit class-scoped finding_fingerprint values so multi-class lessons have independent occurrence streams.

Gobby Homebrew distribution mode is detected with `GOBBY_DISTRIBUTION=homebrew`. In that mode `gobby install` verifies `gcode`, `ghook`, and `gwiki` against `src/gobby/install/version_pins.py`, skips global npm installs and managed helper downloads. Helper resolution and Homebrew verification treat executable `~/.gobby/bin/<helper>` binaries that satisfy the managed pin as authoritative before falling back to Homebrew/PATH helpers.

Gobby identity model: the durable user boundary is user -> machine -> session. The `machines` registry owns optional `owner_user_id`; sessions/tasks/agents/memory should not grow scattered `user_id` columns. Session listing/filtering uses `machine_id`, and placeholder machine IDs like `unknown`, `unknown-machine`, `none`, and `null` are intentionally skipped instead of creating registry rows.

All read-modify-write operations on a session_variables row must use transaction_immediate(SessionVariableMutation(session_id=...)) so PostgreSQL advisory locking serializes compact-continuation helpers with SessionVariableManager writers. This includes first-write INSERT paths, which otherwise can race into a unique violation.

`gobby build restart --no-resume` treats stage cap escalations as build-owned reset state. `_is_build_owned_escalation` includes reasons ending in `_max_work_attempts`, `_max_review_rounds`, `_work_failed:max`, and `_review_failed:max`, so paused manifest resets clear cap escalations like `development_max_work_attempts`.

Dispatcher agent-slot caps are global across projects. In src/gobby/dispatch/dispatcher.py, both the early candidate-loop check and the final SpawnAgentAction admission check call count_active_agents(db) without project_id; final admission uses AgentCapAdmission(project_id=None), which maps to the global agent_cap_admission:* advisory-lock key. Project-scoped count_active_agents remains available for observability/fairness reporting. Regression test test_concurrent_project_heartbeats_share_global_agent_cap in tests/dispatch/test_dispatcher.py runs heartbeats for two projects and proves global pending/running runs stay at the configured cap. Implemented by #15958 in commit 69cfc34e183caabefb72fca762ec5dc3a5c90f18.

Gobby web voice capture diagnostics use local browser console events prefixed `[gobby:voice]`. `useVoiceCapture.ts` logs VAD readiness and speech lifecycle (`vad_waiting`, `vad_start`, `vad_ready`, `vad_speech_start`, `vad_speech_end`, `vad_misfire`, `vad_error`), PTT lifecycle, and voice audio send attempts/results with request IDs, sample rate, payload size, WebSocket state, and only a short conversation prefix. PTT capture normalizes high-rate audio to 16 kHz before WAV encoding and blocks payloads over `VOICE_AUDIO_MAX_PAYLOAD_BYTES`.

Expansion runs have no restart recovery worker. Task #16358 added LocalExpansionRunManager.cleanup_stale_runs, which atomically fails running/applying rows older than 30 minutes. Daemon startup invokes it through DatabaseExecutor, and start_expansion_run_impl invokes a parent-task-scoped sweep before active-run reuse so a row that becomes stale after startup cannot permanently block re-expansion.

FalkorDB entity-memory linkage: Entities in FalkorDB get a common _Entity label (via SET after MERGE to avoid mismatch). When memories are created, entities are linked to (:Memory {memory_id}) nodes via MENTIONED_IN relationships. This enables graph-augmented search: vector search finds entities, MENTIONED_IN links resolve to memory IDs, and graph traversal finds related memories. Backfill via rebuild_knowledge_graph MCP tool passes memory_id to add_to_graph().

Procedure to empirically capture a managed CLI's native plan-approval menu for Path B keystroke mapping (epic #15606 / #15647, per-CLI tasks #15727-#15732). Gobby's persistent tmux socket is /private/tmp/tmux-501/default; it has `destroy-unattached on` globally, which instantly reaps any detached session you create. To make a survivable capture session: (1) `tmux -S <sock> set-option -g destroy-unattached off`; (2) `tmux -S <sock> new-session -d -s plancap-<cli> -x 130 -y 45 -c /Users/josh/Projects/gobby`; (3) `tmux -S <sock> set-option -t plancap-<cli> destroy-unattached off` (per-session override survives the global being restored); (4) `tmux -S <sock> set-option -g destroy-unattached on` to restore gobby's behavior. Then send-keys to launch the CLI in plan mode and give it a REAL planning task (a trivial prompt makes Claude exit with no plan -> only a bare confirm menu; you need a genuine task so it writes a plan and renders the full menu). Capture with `tmux -S <sock> capture-pane -t plancap-<cli> -p`. Test the selection mechanic NON-destructively: digits/arrows to move the cursor and the feedback/keep-planning option, never the approve options (approving executes in the real repo). Kill the session when done. KEY Claude finding (v2.1.169): the native ExitPlanMode menu has TWO shapes with DIFFERENT activation -- full plan menu (plan written) navigates on digit + Enter activates (1=auto/yolo, 2=manual/act, 3=Ultraplan-web unused, 4=tell-Claude/request-changes); bare confirm menu (no plan: 'Claude wants to exit plan mode' 1.Yes/2.No) activates on the digit alone. So claude needs a pane-aware resolver, not a static keystroke map. The framework supports this via PlanKeystrokeRegistry.register_resolver/requires_pane/resolve_for_pane in src/gobby/adapters/plan_keystrokes.py. The user prefers launching a gobby-agents planner agent (a real managed terminal session) as the capture vehicle for the remaining CLIs.

ChatInput button layout fix (ChatInput.tsx): Replaced conditional streaming/non-streaming button blocks with a single stable container using 'flex gap-1 shrink-0'. Send button is always present (left), disabled when not streaming and no input. Stop button appears conditionally to the right during streaming. This prevents the bar from growing vertically when buttons appear/disappear. Send stays enabled during streaming to allow interrupt-with-message.

In Gobby Teams communications, `TeamsAdapter.verify_webhook` binds Bot Framework JWTs to the activity body by requiring decoded `serviceUrl` to be a HTTPS string equal to the activity `serviceUrl`. Mismatched replayed tokens are rejected before parsing stores ConversationReferences, preventing proactive sends to forged service URLs. Commit bf32ac121 for task #16011.

GitHubSyncService bidirectional issue sync uses LocalTaskManager.reconcile_task_state for external lifecycle changes: GitHub closed sets closed_at and closed_reason="github_sync", GitHub open clears close metadata, and push derives GitHub state with tasks.state_semantics.is_task_closed. Import and push route labels through the service's existing mapping helpers.

In Gobby communications, BaseChannelAdapter.initialize receives a synchronous secret_resolver callback. CommunicationsManager._init_adapter must resolve `$secret:` channel config refs with asyncio.to_thread before calling initialize, then serve both full `$secret:NAME` and bare `NAME` keys from an in-memory map; adapters such as Telegram may pass bare names after stripping the prefix.

During gobby build dogfood #15385/#15447, AgentLifecycleMonitor.refresh_active_run_dispatch_mutexes was changed to restore a dispatcher-held heartbeat mutex when an active task-bound agent run has no task_dispatch_mutex row. This prevents duplicate dispatch windows after a same-task helper clears a mutex while another active orchestrator/agent is still running.

Spawned tmux agents must persist child_session_id, pid, and tmux_session_name immediately after live-pane verification and before waiting for SessionStart registration. Otherwise registration timeouts can kill the pane while DB/MCP surfaces still report no terminal. Claude sandbox settings should omit optional proxy port keys when no proxy is configured; serializing httpProxyPort/socksProxyPort as JSON null triggers Claude /doctor settings warnings.

Force-graph ref-isolation pattern (2D reference implementation: web/src/components/activity/wiki/WikiForceGraph.tsx, #17764): react-force-graph re-applies props on parent re-render and destroys custom canvas objects, so graph components sit behind a memo wall whose equality checks only (dataRevision, theme, width, height, reducedMotion). Everything else crosses the wall through parent-owned MutableRefObjects: interaction state (hoverId, lowercased search) in an interactionRef read by nodeCanvasObject/linkColor accessors every frame, and callbacks in a handlersRef whose identity never changes. autoPauseRedraw={false} keeps force-graph's internal rAF repainting the accessors, so pointer-move causes zero React state updates (hover writes go through useRafCoalescedHandler). dataRevision is a composite string of requestKey + toggle bits + theme; token colors are baked into the scene once per build via resolveCssVar (pure builder in WikiGraphScene.ts takes an injectable resolver for tests). Gotchas: force-graph mutates link source/target from id strings into node objects at runtime (type endpoint extraction as unknown); the 2D package exposes no renderer()/pixelRatio API unlike the 3D exemplar; eslint react-hooks/immutability forbids render-time writes even to module-level '.current' objects in test mocks — capture props inside a useEffect. Backend graph include enum is {all, knowledge, code} (_GRAPH_INCLUDE_VALUES in src/gobby/servers/routes/wiki.py) — 'wiki' is not a value and 400s.

Project registration concurrency pattern: LocalProjectManager.ensure_exists uses INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (id) DO NOTHING and returns the stored Project, which is appropriate when callers only need existence. Routes that must distinguish a newly created row from a concurrent duplicate should use ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING RETURNING id; a returned row means success, while no row means fetch and return the existing project.

Default-agent prompt-facing role, goal, personality, and instructions are injected from the first UserPromptSubmit/before_agent hook, not during SessionStart. SessionStart activates agent variables/rules/skills. Full startup/context-loss starts set _agent_context_injected=false and _agent_context_rehydrate_pending=true so the next prompt rehydrates once, then clears the pending marker. Daemon restart/reregister_active_sessions must not reset prompt injection flags; stale _agent_context_injected=false on sessions with prior message_count/turn_count is repaired to true without emitting another preamble. Persona switches still use _agent_identity_reinject=true for a one-time reinject. Implemented in commit 3dfba4be7 for task #17468.

Inter-agent messaging overhaul plan (docs/plans/inter-agent-messaging.md): Clean break replacing 5 hierarchy-locked tools (send_to_parent, send_to_child, broadcast_to_children, poll_messages, mark_message_read on gobby-agents) with 3 new tools: send_message (P2P, any session in same project), send_command (ancestor-only, overrides child's workflow with __command__ sentinel and restricts tools), complete_command (restores workflow). Push delivery via EventEnricher injecting undelivered messages into response.context during PreToolUse/UserPromptSubmit hooks. Delivery acks auto-sent back to sender (delivery_ack for messages, command_ack for commands). ## Agents v3 Design Decisions (Epic #9085)

### Core Concepts
- **Selectors**: Compact string syntax for targeting rules by metadata — `tag:X`, `group:X`, `name:X`, `source:X`, `*`. Fnmatch globs. Include is OR, exclude wins on conflict. No boolean combinators in v3.
- **`extends`**: Single inheritance for agent definitions. Child overrides parent. Max depth 5, cycle detection. Uses Pydantic `model_fields_set` to detect explicit overrides vs defaults.
- **`inherit`**: Sentinel value for provider/model. Resolved from CLI source at session_start or spawn time via `_CLI_SOURCE_TO_PROVIDER` map.
- **`mode: self`**: "Persona, not process." Loads rules+variables onto current session without spawning. Already exists in spawn layer but not in `AgentDefinitionBody.mode` Literal. Being added as first-class + decoupled from requiring a workflow.
- **`default_agent`**: New `DaemonConfig` field (default: "default"). Deep loaded at session_start in `handle_session_start` — before rules evaluate. Writes `_agent_type`, `_active_rule_names`, preset variables to `session_variables`.
- **`_active_rule_names`**: New session variable. When set, rule engine filters to only these rule names (via `_filter_by_active_rules`). When None, all rules pass (backward compat).

### Key Architecture
- New files: `src/gobby/workflows/selectors.py`, `src/gobby/workflows/agent_resolver.py`
- Injection point: `src/gobby/hooks/event_handlers/_session.py` handle_session_start, after session registration, before rules evaluate
- Rule engine change: `_filter_by_active_rules` added after `_filter_by_agent_scope` in evaluate()
- Spawn evolution: `_modes.py` gets `_handle_self_persona` for workflow-less mode:self
- Agent sync already exists at `src/gobby/agents/sync.py`

### Phase 2: Variable Definitions
- First-class `workflow_type='variable'` in `workflow_definitions` table (no schema change)
- Replaces 14 session-defaults rules (all pure set_variable initializers guarded by `is None`)
- 6 conditional set_variable rules in other groups stay as rules
- User chose first-class variable registry over variables-as-rule-outputs

### User Preferences
- User wants `mode: self` (not terminal/headless) for the baseline agent concept
- User prefers config setting for default agent activation (not convention-based)
- User wants deep load pattern (like session ID) for agent activation at session_start
- Keep straightforward for agents v3 — no boolean combinators, no compound selectors

## Lesson
- principle: When a background thread hosts an asyncio event loop and consumers gate submissions on loop.is_running(), the readiness event must be set by a callback scheduled on the loop (loop.call_soon), not between loop creation and run_forever(); otherwise there is a window where the constructor has returned but the loop is not yet running.
- root_cause: Readiness was signaled at thread-setup time instead of loop-run time, creating a construct-then-submit race for immediate first use.
- prevention: Signal readiness via loop.call_soon(ready.set) immediately before run_forever(), and regression-test by gating run_forever entry and asserting a submission immediately after construction succeeds.

## Diagnostic
- title: Loop-hosting thread readiness must be signaled from inside the running loop
- message: WorkflowEvaluationRuntime._run_loop set its readiness threading.Event after storing the loop but before loop.run_forever() started, so __init__ could return while loop.is_running() was still False and run() spuriously rejected work with 'Workflow evaluation runtime is not running'.

gobby is routinely edited by multiple concurrent agent sessions sharing ONE working tree and ONE git index. Between your `git add` and `git commit`, another session's `git add`/`git add -A` can stage its files into the shared index, and a plain `git commit` would sweep that in-flight foreign work into your commit; another session may also land its own commit in the same window (observed 2026-06-03: ~20 foreign gwiki/gcore changes appeared mid-task; observed again 2026-07-10: a codex session's crates/ worker-pool work got swept into a #17201 commit despite staging only 12 own files). How to apply: (1) never `git add -A`/`git add .` — stage only your explicit paths; (2) before committing verify with `git diff --cached --stat` / `git show :<path>` that staged content is yours; (3) ALWAYS commit path-scoped with `git commit -m msg -- <your paths>` — the trailing pathspec restricts the commit to those paths regardless of what else is staged (note it errors with 'did not match any file(s) known to git' if a listed path is still untracked — `git add` it first); (4) after committing confirm `git show --stat HEAD` lists exactly your files; (5) recovery from a bad sweep: `git reset HEAD~1` (mixed) only rewinds the index — the other session's working-tree changes and untracked files stay intact — then re-add and recommit path-scoped; (6) do not try to own/fix another session's uncommitted mid-refactor (CLAUDE.md #8 is about errors you hit, not others' WIP) — leave it staged for its owner.

Gobby runs multiple concurrent agent sessions against the SAME working tree and git index. A bare `git commit` (or `git add -A`) will sweep another session's staged files into YOUR commit — observed 2026-06-09 when a docs/reviews scaffold commit (#15765) accidentally bundled another session's in-flight bundled-C-skill files (#15748). Mitigation: always commit with an explicit pathspec (`git commit <paths> -m ...`) and stage only your own files; never bare-commit the whole index. If you hit a `.git/index.lock` error, another session's git process is mid-commit — diagnose via `ps` for git processes + lock mtime and wait for it to clear; do NOT force-remove the lock (risks corrupting the other session's commit). Recovery if you already bundled foreign files: `git reset --soft HEAD~1` then `git commit <your-paths>` (pathspec commit leaves the other files staged for their owner).

gcode codewiki full regen cost & reuse model (learned during #894): a full regen is SEQUENTIAL at ~100s/page (each page = multi-call AI generate + verify), so the 601-page gobby-wiki/code vault is ~10-17h end-to-end — not a blocking in-session op. Cost is calls-per-page × pages, not per-call latency. reusable_page_keyed (crates/gcode/src/commands/codewiki/reuse.rs) reuses a page only when render_version == CODEWIKI_RENDER_VERSION (mod.rs) AND source-hash/ai_mode match, so ANY render-version bump globally invalidates reuse → a full from-scratch regen. --since <ref> only targets source-changed pages (+ digest-changed aggregates); it does NOTHING for a render-code-only change. Implication: for a render-only delta on a few curated pages, replicate the committed render behavior deterministically in place rather than re-generate hundreds of byte-identical pages. Vault is git-tracked; _meta/codewiki.json + .obsidian/* are gitignored and must never be staged. Don't infer daemon feature_low/mid/high model chains from a stale plan table — probe POST /api/llm/generate for the currently configured models instead of relying on a point-in-time snapshot.

gobby-cli source-edit workflow under Gobby hooks: PreToolUse hooks block the Read/Edit/Write tools on indexed .rs source (even bounded reads, and even scratchpad copies that keep the .rs extension), plus grep/rg, broad head/cat on project source, bare python (require-uv), and cat of JSON. The standard Edit/Write tools need a prior Read the hook denies, so they're unusable directly on .rs. WHY: the repo enforces 'prefer gcode for source reads' + required-skill/task gates. HOW: (1) read working-tree source via `git show HEAD:<path>` or gcode (outline/symbol/grep); small `head -n` is ok, broad head/cat on .rs is flagged. (2) To EDIT: cp the .rs into the scratchpad as a .txt (the hook keys on the .rs extension, so .txt copies Read/Edit freely), edit the .txt with the Edit tool, then cp it back over the .rs; verify with git diff + cargo build/clippy/nextest. (3) Move a large inline #[cfg(test)] module with `git show ...|sed -n 'a,bp'|sed 's/^    //'`. (4) Load gate skills up front via get_skill: code-index, task-creation, rust, development-discipline, json, task-transitions. (5) Create/claim a gobby-task before editing; finish with commit + close_task(commit_sha). Foreground `sleep` is blocked — wait via background Bash or Monitor.

Activity Sessions action semantics: Resume means continue a non-web session into a web chat via continueSessionInChat. Swap means make an existing session the visible main surface: web_chat swaps select the existing conversation, while terminal/non-web swaps view and observe the session.

Wiki scope/root resolution is async. Call resolve_wiki_scope/resolve_scope_identity with await; project root lookup is offloaded. Wiki cron registration is async and runs during runner_lifecycle_subsystems immediately before CronScheduler.start(), not during synchronous runner_init orchestration.

Agent-definition JSON read-modify-write handlers use `WorkflowDefinitionMutation(definition_id)` with `db.transaction_immediate(...)`. This typed lock serializes updates to one workflow definition across SQLite and PostgreSQL so concurrent route patches preserve both edits.

In the web app shell, cohesive App.tsx responsibilities are being extracted into focused hooks under web/src/components/app. Task #17251 established useAppProjectSelection for project/provider UI-settings persistence and project sync, useAppSessionActions for session delete/kill/expire/continue handlers, useAppToast for toast timer state, and usePersistedSessionsFilters for sessions filter localStorage persistence. App.tsx remains the orchestrator and preserves the ChatPage prop contract.

Dependency audit policy after #17866: project-wide uv auditing is configured under `[tool.uv.audit]`; no-fix advisories must use `ignore-until-fixed`, not a permanent blanket ignore, so OSV automatically reports them when a fix appears. CI and the monthly dependency audit run `uv audit --locked`. Chatterbox 0.1.7 exact-pins vulnerable ONNX/Transformers versions, so safe floors live in `tool.uv.override-dependencies`; direct/transitive compatible floors such as aiosmtplib and joserfc live in declarations/constraint-dependencies.

Coupling invariant: every command added to a gwiki CLI contract (crates/gwiki/contract/gwiki.contract.json) MUST also get an arm in gcode's hardcoded resolve_gwiki_handler map (crates/gcode/src/commands/codewiki/build_parts/features.rs), mapping command -> (handler_file, entry_symbol). Missing arms fail gcode's feature-catalog test every_entry_resolves_to_a_handler_file_that_exists_on_disk. This was missed twice: #17752 (`pages`, fixed in 553a70bc2) and #17753 (`page write`/`page delete`, fixed by the #17753 session after cross-session P2P coordination). Validation for any gwiki contract change should include `cargo test -p gobby-code --lib features`.

POST /api/config/import persists configuration and prompt overrides through managers backed by the same HubDatabase. Keep the full import inside an ambient config_store.db.transaction(); nested ConfigStore and LocalPromptManager transactions participate in that scope, so any prompt create/update failure rolls back the preceding config replacement.

Server list routes batch enrichment at the route layer: task owner refs resolve all session IDs with one sessions query; project lists load session activity and open-task counts with two grouped queries, then pass precomputed stats into response serialization. Focused query-count tests live in tests/servers/routes/test_tasks_routes.py and test_projects_routes.py.

Provider catalog and generation-endpoint contract after task #18804 / commit 314037d26 deliberately reverses #18447 for Responses endpoints only. Generic generation endpoints live at `ai.generation.endpoints.<name>` and use selectors `endpoint:<name>[/<model>]`; the old `ai.generation.local.*` path and `local:*` generation selectors are rejected without aliases. Endpoints with `wire_api=responses` are published under `provider=codex` with `execution_provider=codex` and execute through Codex CLI/app-server using a deterministic `gobby_endpoint_<name>` internal provider plus child-only API-key environment. Capability flags remain independently probe-gated, including vision-only degradation. Chat Completions endpoints remain their own catalog-only groups and are unavailable for web chat. LM Studio/Ollama Responses behavior from #18447 is not generalized to Chat Completions.

Task close zero-row outcomes are a three-way contract in storage: an absent task ID raises ValueError with an explicit not-found message; an existing task whose updated_at differs from expected_updated_at raises TaskStaleStateError; an already-closed task with no stale freshness conflict is idempotent. Established by task #18397 / commit 29ece53a5.

Codex CLI sends notify payloads with kebab-case field names (thread-id, turn-id, input-messages, last-assistant-message, cwd). The _normalize_input_data() function in hook_dispatcher.py now handles all three naming conventions (snake_case, camelCase, kebab-case). The CodexNotifyAdapter no longer falls back to os.getcwd() for missing cwd — it returns None instead, since the daemon's cwd is never the project directory. The codex_app_server config flag in DaemonConfig controls whether CodexAppServerClient is created in runner.py. CodexAdapter.EVENT_MAP includes thread/closed for session end events.

Plan approval keystrokes for static native menus are guarded through PlanKeystrokeRegistry menu matchers; attached approval captures live pane text and resolve_for_pane returns None when the expected menu is absent, causing PLAN_KEYSTROKES_UNMAPPED instead of sending blind digits.
For Gobby build coordination, daemon restarts are allowed when needed. Before restarting the daemon, broadcast to other agents so they expect the interruption.

Gobby no longer has a Python package at src/gobby/tools. The MCP tool description summarizer was moved to src/gobby/utils/tool_summarizer.py in task #13908; imports should use gobby.utils.tool_summarizer.

runner.py Phase 2 config reload bug: The second load_config() call (with config_store) didn't pass config_file, so when the DB config_store was empty (fresh installs, e2e tests), DaemonConfig(**{}) returned all defaults (daemon_port=60887, default DB path). Fix: pass self._config_file to both load_config calls, and in load_config fall back to YAML when config_store is empty.

`mark_task_review_rejected` accepts both `needs_review` and `in_progress` states. Interactive planning/adversary flows can auto-claim a review task before emitting a reject verdict, so rejection must still persist findings, clear ownership, and reopen the task.

Chat UI off-by-one bug after interrupt: When a user sends a new message while the previous response is streaming, the Claude SDK's response buffer isn't fully drained after interrupt(). The next receive_response() call returns stale events from the interrupted query, and _stream_chat_response tags them with the NEW request_id — so the frontend renders the old response as if it belongs to the new message. Fix: Added drain_pending_response() to ChatSession (chat_session.py) that consumes remaining events after interrupt, and call it in _cancel_active_chat (websocket/chat.py) after task cancellation.

Gobby memory lifecycle design: the `increment-parent-turn-seq` bundled rule increments `parent_turn_seq` on parent `turn_start` only when the session variable was already seeded, and it is intentionally not gated by `memory_recall_helper_enabled` so stale helper payloads cannot become fresh after the feature is toggled.
EmailAdapter rejects SMTP credential auth on ports other than 465 or 587 by default; set config_json["allow_plaintext_credentials"] = true only for explicit plaintext SMTP credential opt-in.

As of task #17798, the Web UI auth contract includes `credentialsConfigured`, mapped from `/api/auth/status` field `credentials_configured`. Status HTTP failures and network failures resolve fail-closed (`authRequired=true`, `authenticated=false`) while treating credential readiness as potentially configured to avoid false setup claims during outages. App passes the field to LoginPage; absent credentials replace the login form with the exact daemon-host command `gobby auth credentials`. Implemented in commit 9022b411b.

Gobby test/report policy: install httpx2 as a dev dependency so FastAPI/Starlette TestClient uses the non-deprecated client path; local pre-push pip-audit should mirror CI no-fix ignores including CVE-2025-3000 for torch, while Gradio should be upgraded when pip-audit reports a fixed line.

InternalToolRegistry schema generation (internal.py line 166) skips parameters starting with underscore. This is by design — _context is hidden from the schema. But it also means the daemon must be restarted after changing tool function signatures, since schemas are generated at import time.

Gobby repo artifact-path convention: plan artifacts live under `.gobby/plans/`, but `_artifact_paths()` must not hardcode `.gobby/plans/task-<id>-plan.md`. Since task #12741, front-half plan path resolution prefers persisted task/session/run state and accepts existing `.gobby/plans/task-<id>-*.md` files for legacy compatibility. `_artifact_paths()` still reserves `.gobby/test-architecture/task-<id>-test-architecture.md` for test-architecture artifacts. Generic untracked report output lives under `reports/` (for example `reports/coderabbit-1776775137.md`), and screenshots are intentionally untracked under `.gobby/screenshots/`. For a manual verification report like task #12122, prefer `reports/task-12122/verification-report.md` over `.gobby/plans/...` so the file is not misclassified as a plan artifact.

Unresolved tool failures are tracked in the reserved session variable `open_tool_errors` as a normalized, newest-10 list keyed by exact `(tool, target_key)`. `SessionVariableManager.upsert_open_tool_error` and `resolve_open_tool_errors` own atomic mutations. The public `ToolProxyService.call_tool` finalizer owns proxy-entry outcomes (and runs tracking off-loop); native `handle_after_tool` owns non-wrapper CLI events. Policy denials and invalid calls do not mutate state; failed pre-dispatch outcomes use caller identity; executed outcomes use final rewritten identity and exact success resolution. Public wrapper echo events must be skipped to avoid double counting.

RuleEngine condition evaluation unwraps `call_tool` / `mcp__gobby__call_tool` `tool_input` to the inner `arguments` payload inside `TemplatingMixin._build_eval_context`, then re-injects only `server_name` and `tool_name`. Rule YAML that inspects MCP call inputs must therefore read the unwrapped shape (for example `tool_input.get("task_id")`), not `tool_input.get("arguments")`.

CodeRabbit batch #17424 lessons for Gobby: ACP filesystem writes must treat temp-file unlink as best-effort cleanup so cleanup failures never mask the primary write OSError; synchronous hook shutdown should drain deferred memory recall futures against one shared monotonic deadline, not per-future 5s budgets; task MCP payloads must derive `ref` from the same `seq_num` value they return, including `to_dict()`-only seq_num rows; transcript title sync must re-raise psycopg.Error before advancing JSONL offsets or JSON mtime so DB outages retry; plain JSONL transcript processing should pass `record_observations=True`; Claude unknown assistant block flushing must preserve source order by emitting pending text before pending thinking; unmodeled-observation hash-version changes cannot be backfilled from persisted metadata, so purge existing observation rows in a numbered migration; ACP discovery warnings must not log raw response bodies.

Bundled agent `allowed_mcp_tools` entries with wildcards such as `gobby-tasks:*` intentionally allow exact MCP handler refs on the same server, for example `gobby-tasks:close_task` and `gobby-tasks:escalate_task`; contract tests should model that wildcard allowance rather than adding redundant exact YAML permissions.

E2E test env leak: protect_production_resources sets GOBBY_TEST_PROTECT=1 in the test process env. When e2e conftest spawns daemon subprocesses via os.environ.copy(), this flag leaks into the subprocess. The daemon's load_config safety switch then fires but GOBBY_DATABASE_PATH was already popped, causing inconsistent state. Fix: pop GOBBY_TEST_PROTECT and GOBBY_CONFIG_FILE from daemon subprocess env alongside GOBBY_DATABASE_PATH.

Testing caveat for schema-lease recording: session_variables has a foreign key to sessions, and record_schema_shown (src/gobby/mcp_proxy/services/schema_guidance.py) swallows FK failures at debug level. Tests asserting that an invalid-argument response records/retains the unlocked_tools lease must use a SessionManager-registered session ID; an arbitrary UUID makes the lease write silently no-op and the assertion passes vacuously.

The web useWebSocketEvent hook owns a module-level singleton WebSocket. Every socket callback must be guarded by the current connectionGeneration (and closed state), because effect cleanup resets closed for a replacement mount and late callbacks from the retired socket can otherwise clear the current socket, flip connected state, dispatch duplicate messages, or schedule zombie reconnects. Reconnect timers should call ensureConnection so an already-created current socket prevents a duplicate connection. Covered by task #15890 / commit 1f88754ec.

Codex worktree hook installation now uses gobby.cli.installers.codex.install_codex_project_hooks(project_path), which writes/merges <worktree>/.codex/hooks.json, trusts that project hooks file in ~/.codex/config.toml, and seeds Codex [projects] trust for the worktree path. create_worktree(provider="codex") should report hooks_installed=True when that project installer succeeds; it no longer relies on the old CODEX_NOTIFY_SCRIPT model.

useDetailDraft (web/src/components/activity/fields/useDetailDraft.ts) marks the draft clean only AFTER its onSave callback resolves. Any navigation triggered inside onSave (e.g. a WikiTabActions helper that navigates on success) runs while the registered dirty guard still reports dirty, so guardedRun pops a spurious 'discard unsaved changes' confirm. Pattern: onSave only persists and stashes the result path in a ref; the caller awaits save() and navigates after it returns true (draft is marked clean synchronously inside save() before it returns). WikiPageEditor.runSave/onSaved is the reference implementation.

Gwiki human-facing timestamps use the shared precision-aware parser in crates/gwiki/src/support/time.rs. ParsedTimestamp distinguishes Instant, DateOnly, DatePrefix (date plus original text), and Unparseable. Instant rendering accepts an injected FixedOffset, emits local `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM ±HH:MM`, and retains computed `unix-ms:<epoch>` in parentheses. DateOnly retains calendar precision; DatePrefix and Unparseable render their original text verbatim. Citation rendering is exposed as render_citations; citation, log.rs, and collect.rs log bodies use the shared formatter, while recap.rs alone converts DateOnly/DatePrefix to midnight UTC for ordering. Implemented for task #18578 at commits 9d1b579a6 and 7af59c95c.

Gobby plan parsing now stores source lines on PlanDocument via parse_plan, and semantic lint should reuse PlanDocument.source_lines for section body scans instead of rereading the plan file from disk.

MCP import synthesis now fetches GitHub repository/search context deterministically via GitHub HTTP APIs in `src/gobby/mcp_proxy/importer.py`, then calls `LLMService.call_feature(config.import_mcp_server, ...)`. The importer no longer uses `_claude_model_candidate`, `llm_service.get_provider("claude")`, `ClaudeLLMProvider`, or `generate_with_tools`; tests assert no legacy provider access.

Recall-signal logging schema v2 (#17115, commit bdbbe98aa): SearchDebugSnapshot and JSONL events include join metadata session_id, recall_request_id, and caller. MemoryRecallRunner generates one uuid4 recall_request_id per eligible recall run, passes session_id/recall_request_id/caller="memory.recall" into candidate search, and exposes recall_request_id on MemoryRecallResult. Non-recall callers are tagged by purpose while leaving session_id/recall_request_id null.

Task #18866 records the intended architecture scope: add the specific vllm-project/vllm inference server as a first-class Gobby runtime, including canonical vLLM deployments and the vllm-project/vllm-metal MLX backend for Apple Silicon, alongside existing LM Studio/Ollama/generic local generation endpoints. Support VLM multimodal workloads needed by UI-TARS where backend/model capabilities allow them, and integrate UI-TARS as a Gobby-bundled external MCP server managed like Context7 and Brave Search. vLLM is the serving product; VLM is a vision-language model class.

Codewiki compare mode (`gcode codewiki --compare-to GIT_REF[:META_PATH]`) is a read-only metadata consumer. It resolves the Git ref and repository-relative baseline path separately; omitted META_PATH defaults to `<out-relative>/_meta/codewiki.json`, while current metadata always comes from local `--out`. It compares only each doc's commit, commit_dirty, and source_hashes. Output uses top-level base/current commit metadata plus path-sorted added/removed/changed arrays; unstamped values serialize as null. Invalid explicit paths, bad refs, absent baseline metadata, malformed baseline metadata, and malformed current metadata have distinct errors. Implemented by task #18789 / commit 0dd39d15e.

Gobby does NOT use config.yaml files for runtime config — only for settings export/import. All runtime config goes through the config store (DB Layer 3) with $secret: resolution. Any code reading from config.yaml is dead code (exception: importers). No environment variable fallbacks for API keys — config store is the single source.

Daemon cron initialization invariant after #16770 / commit 84d8be5f5: CronJobStorage and CronExecutor are required dependencies for cron registration; their constructor failures stop that chain after logging the exact subsystem with traceback. SystemAutomationLoop initialization may fail independently while CronScheduler still initializes. CronScheduler or unexpected handler-registration failure clears runner.system_automation_loop so lifecycle startup cannot run automation against an unavailable scheduler/executor chain.

Transcript provider parsers may emit provider-shaped records, but rendering, windowing, indexing, stats, lifecycle processing, and title heuristics should consume records after `normalize_transcript_records(...)`. The current normalizer suppresses successful no-output Grok `hook_execution`, renders visible/non-success Grok hooks as system text, and parser dispatch suppresses Codex `tool_search_call`/`tool_search_output` plus Droid top-level `todo_state` metadata before parser-error logging.

As of commit a5380ad60 (task #16285), export_config_to_yaml writes owner-only YAML through a same-directory temporary file, flushes and fsyncs the completed file, atomically replaces the destination, then fsyncs the parent directory. Serialization or pre-replace failures remove the temp file and preserve the previous export byte-for-byte.

The gobby root CLI supports eager --hello and --goodbye flags in src/gobby/cli/__init__.py; they print 'Hello from Gobby!' and 'Goodbye from Gobby!' before config loading or subcommand dispatch. Focused coverage lives in tests/cli/test_cli.py under TestCLICommands.

Gwiki URL cache freshness is modeled separately from immutable capture identity: SourceRecord.fetched_at remains the original capture timestamp, while last_verified_at advances after successful unchanged URL ingest/refresh and fetch_provenance promotes from Stub to Fetched. URL batch cache lookup lives in ingest/url/cache.rs, uses one manifest snapshot, canonical location, checked unix-ms TTL math, and raw/asset existence; zero TTL always refetches. Only real HTML/non-HTML URL snapshot ingest originates Fetched; manifest dedup and refresh may promote it, while collect/manual/local constructors remain Stub. Pre-field manifest records deserialize as Stub with last_verified_at normalized to fetched_at.

Task #18713 implemented context-aware progressive MCP discovery in commit e0eed4dda. Contract: call leased known tools directly; for a known unleased tool call get_tool_schema then call_tool; for an unknown tool name use list_tools then get_tool_schema then call_tool; use list_mcp_servers only for unknown server or registry inspection; gobby-skills get_skill/list_skills/search_skills are schema-gate exempt and callable directly. Context clear/compact/resume resets only schema leases while PostgreSQL inventory/session variables persist across daemon reconstruction. Invalid arguments always include the current schema and retain the lease. Validation: 115 runtime/rule tests, 173 guidance/skill/compact tests, 356 adapter/hook/manifest tests, Ruff format/check, mypy on 11 source files, and test-quality audit of 551 tests all passed.

Voice-stack dependency compatibility (2026-07): TorchAudio 2.11's official release declares compatibility with PyTorch 2.11 and future PyTorch versions. Gobby therefore pins torch==2.13.0 with torchaudio==2.11.0 in [tool.uv].override-dependencies. PyTorch 2.13.0 fixes GHSA-rrmf-rvhw-rf47, so pyproject.toml has no audit ignore for that advisory. The pair was validated by a real import reporting torch 2.13.0 / torchaudio 2.11.0, exception-free `uv audit --frozen`, 37 focused Chatterbox voice tests, and package build. The existing setuptools>=83.0.0 override remains because exercised voice paths do not use removed pkg_resources APIs.

Architecture decision: Workflows are fundamentally event handlers and behavioral rules, not state machines. session-lifecycle.yaml (472 lines) bundled 7+ independent concerns that were decomposed into standalone rules (task #8795). RuleEngine evaluates standalone rules from the workflow_definitions table. Rules support 5 primitive effect types: block, set_variable, inject_context, mcp_call, and observe (observe was initially dropped but later reimplemented to append structured observations to the _observations session variable). The original plan to extend the legacy `rules` table was superseded — the rules table was removed entirely (migration 118) and all rule enforcement now goes through RuleEngine + workflow_definitions table.

Josh strongly prefers preserving complete raw system and cron output. Use structured outputs, summaries, pagination, references, and drill-down access instead of arbitrary truncation; any hard byte cap should exist only as a safety boundary with explicit overflow storage and retrieval.

Activity panel UI convention: toolbar/status bars should use shared CSS vars in `web/src/components/chat/styles/activity-panel.css` (`--activity-panel-bar-height`, `--activity-panel-control-height`) and shared `activity-panel-status-bar*` classes. Tasks activity stage filters use explicit selection: no stage boxes checked means no `stage` query params, and checking one or more stages sends those selected stage names. Review-rejected task filtering is a derived frontend filter for ready current stages with `review_round_count > 0`, because `reject_review` returns the stage state to `ready` rather than persisting a `review_rejected` stage state.

MCP call_tool argument validation in src/gobby/mcp_proxy/services/argument_validation.py intentionally enforces only top-level JSON Schema types. It supports string, number, integer, boolean, object, array, null, list-valued type, and recursive anyOf; booleans are excluded from numeric types and integral floats satisfy integer. Unsupported or untyped branches stay permissive, and enums, bounds, patterns, nested properties, and array items remain downstream concerns.

Task #15700 cleanup: ProviderModelCatalog no longer accepts a DaemonConfig/config constructor argument; runtime and tests should instantiate it with ProviderModelCatalog(cache_path=...) or ProviderModelCatalog(). The web plan-pending surface variant is now a persisted UI setting named planPendingVariant with allowed values 'info' and 'amber', defaulting to 'info', and render code should resolve colors via getPlanPendingColors(variant) rather than a module-level active variant constant.

Gobby build coordinator policy: bugs discovered while coordinating `gobby build` should get regression coverage at the E2E or build-level integration layer that exercises the autonomous build path, in addition to focused unit tests where useful.

Expansion prompt file context in `src/gobby/tasks/expansion/_compile.py::_build_file_context` treats task title, description, and validation criteria as untrusted path input. Accepted candidates must contain no `..` components, resolve under the canonical repository root (including symlink resolution), and be read through the already-validated resolved path.

Transcript rendering treats late tool-result owner emissions as updates to an existing RenderedMessage object. Full and window materializers should deduplicate those repeated object references by object identity, because distinct messages expanded from one raw transcript record can legitimately share the same rendered ID (for example Claude image and document blocks).

Web UI code splitting pattern: All non-default page components in App.tsx are lazy-loaded with React.lazy() and wrapped in Suspense inside the AppErrorBoundary. Vendor deps are split via manualChunks in vite.config.ts: codemirror, xterm, syntax-highlighter, markdown, d3. MemoryGraph (2D) and KnowledgeGraph (3D) are both lazy-loaded in MemoryPage.tsx. The lazy import pattern is: const Page = lazy(() => import('./components/Page').then(m => ({ default: m.Page }))). ChatPage stays eagerly loaded as the default tab.

Task #17267 decomposed `src/gobby/mcp_proxy/tools/tasks/_expansion.py` into a 17-line compatibility facade. MCP tool registration now lives in `_expansion_registry.py`; run/background orchestration, `ExpansionRunResult`, and `start_expansion_run_impl` live in `_expansion_runtime.py`. Keep `_background_run_tasks` and `_execute_run_background` re-exported from `_expansion.py`; `_expansion_registry` deliberately resolves `_execute_run_background` through the facade at call time so existing tests/callers patching `gobby.mcp_proxy.tools.tasks._expansion._execute_run_background` still affect resume behavior.

User preference for build-coordinator sessions: when coordinator cleanup or bug-fix work is broad, spawn subagents to parallelize investigation and implementation when useful, then have the coordinator verify and integrate the results before closing tasks.

Gobby daemon shutdown handling for uvicorn has layered shutdown noise control. `shutdown_daemon_services()` drains uvicorn HTTP connections before setting `server.should_exit`; as of task #15300 commit 7afa6149001b3d7dd13143db29dda3afca99aba9, it also cancels remaining live `server.server_state.tasks` with the `Gobby shutdown drain` message and waits briefly so daemon stop is bounded before uvicorn's own graceful timeout. `UvicornShutdownLogFilter` suppresses those Gobby drain cancellation records only while shutdown is active, while preserving the older graceful-timeout downgrade fallback from task #15289 commit f6a41cacb.

Gemini CLI sends MCP tool names with single underscores (mcp_gobby_call_tool) while Claude/Windsurf use double underscores (mcp__gobby__call_tool). The normalization layer in hooks/normalization.py handles this conversion (added in #10326). The GeminiAdapter.TOOL_MAP also maps bare tool names (call_tool, list_tools, etc.) to canonical double-underscore format. Step workflow tool whitelists should use double-underscore format — normalization handles the rest.

SessionLifecycleManager._process_pending_transcripts must decide short-session LLM skipping from the session turn_count refreshed after _process_session_transcript persists parsed transcript stats. digest_markdown remains the synthesis input and missing-transcript availability check; its heading count is not authoritative session state. Implemented by #16489 in commit 2d9768ecb.

Since task #18818 / commit 24ef776e2, oversized inline handoff summaries use deterministic section-aware budgeting. `split_markdown_sections` is fence-aware for ```/~~~ and preserves a preamble plus casefolded `##` sections; `allocate_section_budget` guarantees the first `Next Steps` and `Current State` occurrences before optional sections, treats later duplicates as unknown-priority sections, and emits trim/drop titles. `_bound_handoff_summary` falls back byte-for-byte to the prior head cut when neither mandatory title is recognized, and otherwise reserves a bounded breadcrumb whose omission list truncates titles to 40 chars and caps at 10 entries.

As of task #18897 (commit 455d6413b), daemon-selected memory recalls use a mandatory single-call retrieval contract. The dispatcher stores ranked references in session variable `memory_recall_deliveries`; hook enrichment no longer injects or acknowledges reference instructions. `gobby-memory.get_recall_memories(recall_request_id)` resolves the ambient session, enforces oldest-pending order, returns every available selected memory body unchanged with rank/search metadata, reports missing IDs, and marks the request complete only after retrieval. Installed memory-lifecycle rules block every other tool and `turn_end` while a valid pending recall exists. The tool is exempt from schema discovery so the gate can be satisfied in one MCP call.

Task list session column is task-ownership-only. In src/gobby/cli/tasks/_utils.py, format_task_list/_build_rendered_row derive the displayed #session from task owner_session_id (claimed_by_session_id via state semantics) or assignee fallback; they do not consult session_tasks for display. Active agent sessions without claimed tasks therefore do not appear on task rows, even if they are active or linked elsewhere.

gwiki librarian boundary after #18433 (commit 447ed0828): `librarian.rs` owns the public Options/report/artifact/SemanticProbe models, `run`, `render_text`, runtime probing/orchestration, deterministic hygiene classification, and lifecycle promotion. `librarian/semantic.rs` owns semantic availability/failure reporting, near-duplicate discovery and exclusions (reviewed distinct pairs, redirects, session/source digests, folder contexts), semantic queries, and unresolved-link clustering. `librarian/proposals.rs` owns suggested task/diff construction plus librarian artifact paths and JSON/text persistence. `librarian/tests.rs` owns the full behavior suite and semantic test backends. Keep internal callers pointed at the owning modules; do not add forwarding wrappers or compatibility re-exports.

Native helper policy: Gobby resolves executable managed helpers in ~/.gobby/bin before PATH, including GOBBY_DISTRIBUTION=homebrew. Managed install/status/updater logic for gcode, ghook, and gwiki must first probe the real local binary version and skip downloads or downgrades when installed_version >= MANAGED_BIN_VERSION_PINS[name]. GitHub releases are only a source for missing or stale helpers, not something the daemon should query before accepting an already-pinned local binary.

Architecture decision: For web UI chat sessions that lack SessionStart hooks, use a 'headless-lifecycle.yaml' workflow (separate from session-lifecycle.yaml) that moves all session_start initialization into on_before_agent with a _session_initialized guard variable. Backend (ChatMixin) handles session DB registration, lifecycle activation, and /clear. SDK hooks bridge to the workflow engine via callbacks. Plan at docs/plans/web-chat-lifecycle.md.

`task_artifacts` rows are created lazily. To serialize merge-style updates safely in PostgreSQL, first `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`, then `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` inside the same transaction so first-write races also lock a real row. Counter increments such as `expansion_attempts` should use a single `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE SET counter = table.counter + 1 RETURNING counter` statement.

Codex OSS local web chat routing in Gobby uses separate Codex app-server backend clients per configured local endpoint for provider=lmstudio or provider=ollama. Those endpoint-keyed clients start with Codex config overrides model_provider="oss" and oss_provider="lmstudio" or "ollama"; the normal Codex web chat path continues to use the shared default Codex app-server client. Spawned Codex agents use --oss --local-provider <provider> -m <resolved-model> for local selectors.

BASELINE_SCHEMA must be kept in sync with BASELINE_VERSION. When bumping BASELINE_VERSION, audit ALL migrations between the old and new version for: (1) ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN statements — add columns to the baseline table definition, (2) CREATE TABLE statements — add new tables to baseline, (3) INSERT statements for seed data — add to baseline. The migration guard for existing databases should check against _MIN_MIGRATION_VERSION (the first migration in the MIGRATIONS list), NOT BASELINE_VERSION. These serve different purposes: BASELINE_VERSION controls fresh DB schema, _MIN_MIGRATION_VERSION controls the upgrade cutoff for existing DBs.

Gobby lifecycle manifest semantics changed in task #14248: generic task creation through storage/MCP/HTTP is metadata-only and does not seed task_stage_states. Lifecycle rows are now created by explicit entry points such as LocalTaskManager.initialize_task_manifest, gobby-tasks-ops initialize_task_manifest, and build/expansion/review-anchor flows. Expansion and epic build descendants derive child manifests from the parent resolved manifest, copying matching caps and limiting child scopes to development, optional holistic_qa for epics, and inherited pr/merge. Historical manifest cleanup is scoped through LifecycleRepair / `gobby tasks repair-lifecycle` and dry-runs by default.

CodeWiki persistence and nightly-boundary invariants (#18190/#18483/#18486; commits c7681dfb5, 95a71920f, a4fcd798f, 5e44a7b0e): generated pages whose links depend on computed targets must invalidate over the complete emitted link set, and deterministic docs vulnerable to stale retained bodies must use a `content-sensitive:<sha256>` key. For content-sensitive docs, reuse is allowed only when the staged body is byte-equal to freshly rendered content; fresh metadata alone must never bless a stale body. `code/_ownership.md` hashes its actual rendered ownership content, so deleted sources and cluster renames rewrite stale file/module links before fail-closed publication validates targets. Separately, ordinary `--scope` intentionally preserves out-of-scope docs and returns before global/curated/ownership emitters; nightly configured scopes must pass `--complete-scope`, filtering input to configured roots while using a global prune/generation boundary so retained global pages cannot escape refresh. Production proof on 2026-07-18: cron run b0ccd499-3883-421b-accd-3d6aac46ef24 completed with 2,997 tracked docs, 44 changed docs (10 files, 6 modules), zero degraded file pages, ownership key `content-sensitive:8cde144c...`, no stale `usefulness.py` link, successful atomic publication, and successful post-publish indexing.

Task #14257 converted `src/gobby/hooks/event_handlers/_session_start.py` into a same-name package. `__init__.py` is the compatibility boundary exporting `SessionStartMixin`, `AgentActivationResult`, `SUMMARY_GENERATION_TIMEOUT_S`, and the package-level patch targets `Path`, `schedule_tmux_window_rename`, and `consume_and_schedule_compact_self_continuation`; implementation now lives in `types.py`, `transcripts.py`, `agents.py`, `handoff.py`, and `flow.py`.

Web chat SDK resume architecture: ChatSession.resume_session_id is passed to ClaudeAgentOptions.resume + continue_conversation=True. SDK session IDs come from two sources: (1) sessions.external_id — web chat updates this to SDK session ID after first ResultMessage (chat.py:1214), (2) agent_runs.sdk_session_id — autonomous agents store this via update_sdk_session_id(). The _handle_continue_in_chat handler in session_control.py resolves the SDK session ID, kills any running agent (terminal/autonomous) via registry.kill(close_terminal=True), then creates a ChatSession with resume. Falls back to history injection if no SDK session ID available. Frontend /resume command opens ResumeSessionModal which calls continueSessionInChat.

memory_recall_with_synthesis was rewritten to fix staleness. Previously it replayed _synthesized_memory_context from the previous turn (Phase 2 stored it for next turn). Now it searches using the current prompt_text enriched with session.digest_markdown.
