Settings overlay sections that edit ui_settings.* (client-side live settings — Appearance theme/fontSize/density/planPendingVariant, and upcoming Chat & Voice #17118, Providers & Models #17117, Projects & Sessions #17119) MUST consume the single shared useSettings instance, NOT call useSettings() themselves. A second instance diverges: theme/fontSize/density apply via global document side-effects so they look fine, but prop-threaded values like planPendingVariant (App.tsx threads settings.planPendingVariant deep into chat/activity) go stale until reload. The shared instance is plumbed App.tsx (const clientSettings = useSettings()) -> <SettingsOverlay clientSettings> -> <SettingsSectionProvider clientSettings> -> SettingsSectionContextValue.clientSettings (optional UseSettingsReturn, exported from hooks/useSettings.ts). Sections read it via useSettingsSectionContext().clientSettings and must tolerate undefined (fallback render). Established in commit 55f7c9696 (#17116). Also: density is a client-only Density='comfortable'|'compact' added to useSettings — persisted to localStorage and applied as data-density on documentElement, but deliberately EXCLUDED from PERSISTABLE_KEYS so it is never sent to the ui_settings PUT (the backend SaveUISettingsRequest has no density field; sending it would be a silent dead-frontend no-op). Compact tightens global --control-row-height/-sm and --activity-panel-row-height under @media (pointer: fine) only, so touch keeps the 44px floor.

Always create YAML template files for pipelines, agent definitions, and rules — not just DB entries via MCP. DB-only definitions created via create_pipeline/create_agent_definition are ephemeral and get purged when sync_bundled_content_to_db runs on daemon restart. The correct pattern is: write a YAML file to src/gobby/install/shared/workflows/{agents,pipelines,rules}/, commit it, and let the sync process install it. gobby-workflows now provides template-saving functionality using the existing create_rule, create_pipeline, and create_agent_definition endpoints, which satisfy templating needs for these structured entities.

Codex CLI app-server 0.139.0 protocol supports ephemeral threads: `ThreadStartParams.ephemeral` requests that a thread not be materialized on disk, and `Thread.ephemeral` reports that state. Gobby exposes this through CodexAppServerClient.start_thread/client_api.start_thread with `ephemeral: bool = False`, includes `"ephemeral": True` in `thread/start` params only when requested, maps response `thread.ephemeral` into CodexThread.ephemeral, and uses `ephemeral=True` only for CodexAppServerTextGenerateAdapter one-shot feature-generation threads so normal Codex web chat/session starts keep their existing request shape.

Circular-import gotcha for token/usage helpers: `src/gobby/sessions/transcripts/__init__.py` eagerly imports every parser (claude, codex, droid, gemini, grok, qwen), and `gemini.py` imports the shared helper `gobby.sessions.token_usage`. So any leaf/helper module that needs `TokenUsage` from `gobby.sessions.transcripts.base` and is imported by both a parser and a non-transcript layer (e.g. the hooks layer `hooks/event_handlers/_misc.py`) will hit `ImportError: cannot import name ... from partially initialized module`. Fix: import `TokenUsage` LAZILY (function-local, with a `TYPE_CHECKING` import for the annotation under `from __future__ import annotations`) inside the helper rather than at module top. This both breaks the cycle and keeps the hook layer from transitively loading all transcript parsers at import time. Established in gobby-#15578 (commit 1e4aeb4ba) for `gobby.sessions.token_usage.gemini_token_usage`.

Task #18736 (commit 69eb83caf) wires one ReviewLearningService instance from setup_internal_registries into the review-learning registry and both task RegistryContext instances. Leaf LLM validation recalls code-domain validation-miss lessons with limit 3 before prompt assembly. Successful empty recall preserves the legacy prompt bytes; recalled guidance enters the lessons_section slot as untrusted content. Gobby RuleEngine manual compaction handling: manual-like PRE_COMPACT triggers (`manual`, `user`, `clear`, `compact`, `compress`, or a present `custom_instructions`) set `_compact_turn_end_bypass_pending`. The next stop/after_agent/stop_failure evaluation removes only semantic `turn_end` and clears the marker, preserving raw-event rules; `turn_start` clears stale markers.

MCP list_mcp_servers tool output is intentionally compacted in src/gobby/mcp_proxy/server_list.py for stdio, GobbyDaemonTools, and hook _proxy/list_mcp_servers paths: connected servers are emitted as names in servers, while non-connected or disabled servers keep compact detail under issues. The HTTP /api/mcp/servers response remains rich object-shaped for UI and API clients.

Task storage concurrency convention: mutate labels and commits with guarded PostgreSQL JSONB operators in a single UPDATE, never by rewriting arrays derived from a prior read. Contested lifecycle transitions such as claim and escalate use conditional UPDATE predicates and inspect rowcount to report the losing transition.

Memory-dream review-vs-delete policy (gobby #17190, prompts/memory/dream.md): the planner uses an explicit decision tree, NOT a numeric scoring table. Tree: (1) reflects current repo? yes -> useful? yes=keep (refresh stale wording, promote if universal), no=delete-if-noise-else-keep; no -> (2) durable value generic to repo (rules/patterns/practices/user prefs/arch/security decisions)? yes=keep, no=delete (obsolete residue). 'review' is the uncertainty escape hatch ONLY (cannot resolve current-ness/value, or unresolved-but-plausibly-active issue), never a soft-delete for confident residue. Malformed/below-threshold verdicts degrade to visible 'keep', never 'review'. 'delete' must cite a concrete obsolescence signal in reason (truth-digest contradiction, closed task/epic, high age_days + ~0 access_count, hard date marking time-bound state); the planner already receives age_days/access_count/created_at per candidate via DreamCandidate.to_prompt_dict. REJECTED a numeric self-scoring table: LLM self-reported confidence is uncalibrated (numbers wouldn't quantify uncertainty, just launder it) and extra output fields add JSON-parse failure surface (the planner already fails on some providers). The robust alternative — a deterministic code-side staleness/value prior gating the LLM verdict — is deferred to research task #17206 pending measurement of a full sweep under the new prompt. Both 'review' and 'delete' soft-hide (recoverable, exclude from search via deleted_at IS NULL); difference is only whether a human triages.

Phase 6 frontend task refactor for #13866 moved LifecycleBoard stage registry construction, blocked filtering, category filtering, visible-stage calculation, swimlane grouping, and per-stage task selection into web/src/components/tasks/lifecycleBoardModel.ts. useTasks now keeps its public API/types intact while using internal helpers for task-list query params, pagination append behavior, and websocket task event application; the Phase 6 test contract still expects StageAdvanceAction to be imported in web/src/hooks/useTasks.ts from ../lib/stageActions.

Tags (and similar extensible config concepts) must be configuration, not code — introducing a new value must never require a Python source edit.

Why: Josh's framing (session #3368, 2026-04-22): 'shouldn't adding tags not require a code change? kind of defeats the purpose of having tags.' Tags are only useful if they're an extensible config surface; if every new value requires shipping Python, they're just hardcoded enums with extra steps.

How to apply: When a plan needs to introduce a new tag, label, category, or similar extensible vocabulary word, don't put the list in Python. Check first: (1) does the storage layer already accept free-form strings (Gobby's `labels` column does), (2) are there existing config surfaces that can emit the new value — LLM prompt templates, rule YAMLs with `mcp_call` effects that call `add_label` on `task_created`, agent calls to `add_label` with arbitrary strings. A one-time plumbing change to EXPOSE a config-driven mechanism (e.g. adding `labels: list[str]` to an LLM output schema so prompts can populate it) is acceptable because it makes the mechanism generic; per-value Python changes are not. This generalizes: before adding a whitelist, enum, or hardcoded set in Python for any extensible concept, check whether the existing storage + a config surface (prompt, rule, skill) already supports free-form strings.
User preference: after finishing and closing a coordination task in this Gobby build-coordinator workflow, call gobby-sessions:compact_self before continuing broader coordination.

Python imports of `gobby.ai.<submodule>` execute the eager `gobby.ai.__init__` first. Configuration modules loaded by `gobby.config.app` must keep import-time dependencies outside the `gobby.ai` package, while endpoint helpers used by agent reasoning should be imported inside the call boundary. The regression probe is `python -c "import gobby.cli"`.

User motivation for workflows v2: The engine is overengineered and makes simple things hard. A pipeline that spawns a CLI, sends a prompt, and kills itself shouldn't require polling gymnastics (weather-kamikaze example). Three evaluation paths, 848-line lifecycle evaluator, step workflows supporting pipelines nobody tested. User wants: pipelines should be easy, launching agents should be easy, enforcing rules should be easy.

In gobby-cli/dev-parity-plus, gwiki no longer keeps blanket `#[allow(dead_code)]` annotations on `crates/gwiki/src/lib.rs` module declarations. Memory dream dry runs materialize one immutable, strictly ordered eligible-ID snapshot at run start, then hydrate active/visible IDs page by page in snapshot order. Mutable last_dreamed_at/updated_at values cannot move rows across pages; missing or hidden rows are logged and skipped. Complete validated dry-run actions are stored in run.plan.actions and rendered by `gobby memory dream status`, while live run action_sample remains capped.

The bundled `/gobby build` skill documents the interactive E2E pattern: keep a claimed coordinator/tracking epic separate from the automation/document epic, use `--quick` only for smoke checks, run final validation without `--quick` with bounded `--max-active-agents`, keep root `README.md` out of docs/guides refresh scope unless explicit, and verify real merge SHA/no agents/no claimed build tasks/no stale worktrees or clones.

Droid spawn runtime in Gobby uses the existing tmux spawn path. execute_spawn provider='droid' calls _spawn_droid_terminal, which builds `droid exec --input-format stream-json --cwd <cwd> ... --auto high <prompt>` and never passes Gobby's UUID as droid --session-id. Droid auth env vars are FACTORY_API_KEY and FACTORY_API_BASE_URL. pre_approve_directory('droid', cwd) is intentionally a no-op because spawned agents use --auto high rather than a trust database.

Gobby wiki freshness must hash the rendered source-page prompt content and prompt path, not only the prompt file path; wiki_source_context_hash is the shared helper used by synthesis and lifecycle refresh checks.

Codex CLI hook architecture: Codex has three modes in Gobby, none with full interactive hook parity. (1) Notify hooks: fire-and-forget, no blocking/context injection — used for interactive terminal sessions. (2) App-server mode (codex_app_server: true in config.yaml): Gobby spawns `codex app-server` as a subprocess via JSON-RPC stdin/stdout — full bidirectional control but headless (no interactive terminal). (3) Agent spawn (--full-auto in tmux): no hook enforcement, auto-approves everything. The app-server protocol replaces the interactive terminal, it doesn't augment it. For true interactive hook parity, Codex would need bidirectional hooks upstream (openai/codex#2109, still open). PR #11067 (community hook system) was closed without merge Feb 2026. Dev-loop pipeline uses developer_provider/qa_provider inputs to select CLI — pass 'codex' to spawn Codex agents.

Antigravity terminal title setup: setting terminal.integrated.tabs.title to ${sequence} is necessary but not sufficient after recent Antigravity builds because the terminal tab list can be hidden for a single terminal. Gobby's installer should force terminal.integrated.tabs.hideCondition=never for Antigravity and Antigravity IDE while preserving other VS Code-family IDEs' default tab visibility.

TmuxSessionManager.send_keys(..., literal=True) delegates to send_literal_text_to_tmux_target, which strips only trailing newlines, pastes any remaining text through a named tmux buffer with `paste-buffer -p`, waits 200 ms when text was pasted, and sends exactly one raw Enter when one or more trailing newlines were present. Internal newlines remain in the paste; text without a trailing newline sends no Enter; newline-only input sends one Enter without a paste delay. The shared 200 ms settle interval clears Codex 0.144.6's 120 ms paste-burst suppression window. Implemented in task #18664, commit a2b62ca87.

Task #17270 decomposed `src/gobby/memory/services/search.py` into a 401-line compatibility facade plus focused helpers under `src/gobby/memory/services/_search_*.py`; public imports for `DEFAULT_SEARCH_LIMIT`, `SearchDebugHit`, `SearchDebugSnapshot`, and `SearchService` remain stable.

Epic #16998 one-surface activity-panel migration has a foundational guide at docs/guides/one-surface-tab-recipe.md, added by task #17013 in commit 696bc110d. Scheduled communications routing contract (task #18858, commit 19a4f3647): Cron completion callbacks emit cron.run.<status> through CommunicationsManager even when WebSocket is disabled, using the cron run ID as a durable event_id and the job project_id for routing. OutboundCommunications derives a deterministic per-event-type/per-channel message UUID, persists a pending reservation before platform delivery, and returns the existing persisted record on restart or concurrent replay so Telegram is not sent the same completion twice. Final status and platform_message_id are persisted after delivery. Telegram home delivery uses the channel's existing config_json.default_destination plus a cron.run.* communications routing rule; WebSocket failures are isolated and cannot suppress communications delivery.

Task #18528 introduced the structured attention response contract. Prompt producers now persist payloads shaped as {kind, excerpt, options:[{option,label}], fingerprint}; detector excerpts are capped at the final 12 lines/4096 characters. POST /api/attention/{entry_id}/respond validates exactly one of option/text/key, checks the stored entry plus a fresh pane fingerprint under a per-entry asyncio lock, injects exact tmux input, and conditionally clears the same episode. Injection failures distinguish stage=none from stage=partial; partial sends clear the old episode and immediately recapture/re-detect so attention can recur safely. The router is centrally registered from src/gobby/servers/_app_routes.py, with implementation in src/gobby/servers/routes/attention.py and tmux primitives in src/gobby/agents/tmux/text_injection.py.

TerminalType enum was removed from the agent spawner system. Everything uses tmux now (TmuxSpawner). The `terminal` field was removed from: SpawnRequest, AgentConfig, AgentDefinitionBody API requests, spawn_agent MCP tool params, and dry_run evaluate_spawn. The `terminal_type` property on TerminalSpawnerBase now returns plain str instead of TerminalType enum. In registry.py, _close_terminal_window was gutted to only keep tmux kill-pane, parent_pid fallback, and Windows taskkill strategies (removed kitty, alacritty, iTerm, Terminal.app, Ghostty, generic pgrep strategies).

install_all_templates() only creates NEW installed copies — it does NOT update existing ones when templates change. After modifying template YAML files (agents, pipelines, rules), you must DELETE the installed copy from workflow_definitions and restart the daemon to re-install from updated templates. Bug #9416 tracks proper fix.

GobbyAI/gobby uses a solo-maintainer GitHub protection model: main is protected by repository ruleset 16902551 requiring PRs, zero approvals, resolved conversations, strict required status check `Merge Gate` from GitHub Actions, and no force pushes/deletion; repository admins have bypass for emergency recovery. The repo also uses the `pypi` GitHub environment with a custom deployment branch policy allowing only `v*` tags, admin bypass enabled, and no required reviewers while Josh is sole maintainer.

Task #17269 decomposed `web/src/hooks/useSessionDetail.ts` into a public hook facade plus focused helpers under `web/src/hooks/useSessionDetail/` (`api.ts`, `chatPolling.ts`, `realtimeEvents.ts`, `summaryActions.ts`, `usageEvents.ts`, `types.ts`, `constants.ts`). `useSessionDetail.ts` still re-exports `SessionMessage` and `TranscriptStatus` for existing component/test imports.

In Gobby's tmux session manager, real tmux treats semicolons inside inline `-e KEY=value` environment arguments as command syntax hazards. Route env values containing `;` through the private sourced env-file path, and use exact session targets of the form `=<session>:` for session-name operations to avoid prefix matches such as `agent` resolving to `agent-extra`.

invoke_pipeline steps in pipelines return {pipeline, execution_id, status, output: {child_keys...}}. Child outputs are namespaced under 'output' key (commit 94ab0751) to prevent clobbering wrapper keys. Previously (d395b0a2) they were merged flat via .update(). Parent steps reference child results as e.g. dev_loop.output.output.orchestration_complete.

The spawned-agent worker-safety rule `no-npx` was intentionally disabled for Gobby on 2026-05-07 because it was too broad: docs/tech-writer agents need `npx -y @mermaid-js/mermaid-cli` for Mermaid validation, and npx is a runner rather than necessarily a package install. The bundled template `src/gobby/install/shared/workflows/rules/worker-safety/no-package-install.yaml` now has `no-npx.enabled=false`; neighboring install blockers (`no-npm-install`, `no-yarn-add`, `no-pip-install`, `no-uv-add`) remain enabled.

User clarified Linear task identity for Gobby sync: keep the task ref itself as the canonical identity (`#N`) and rely on the Linear project name (`gobby`, `gobby-cli`, etc.) as the namespace. DaemonClient.check_health classifies connection failures by httpx exception type: httpx.ConnectError returns DaemonHealthError.NOT_RUNNING, while other httpx.HTTPError subclasses return their diagnostic string. Callers that distinguish an absent daemon must compare against the typed sentinel rather than treating None as a failure sentinel.

In Gobby step workflows, `loaded_skills` is the canonical session-level ledger populated by the gobby-skills:get_skill observer before rule evaluation. Additional-skill gates should check `all(skill in vars.get('loaded_skills', []) for skill in vars.additional_skills)` instead of maintaining a duplicate workflow-local `loaded_additional_skills` list.

In the Gobby CLI daemon commands, PID liveness checks should use gobby.cli.utils._is_process_alive instead of os.kill(pid, 0), because the helper treats zombie/defunct processes as not alive and keeps status/health/stop behavior consistent.

WorkflowLoader returns None only when no matching workflow definition exists. A matching DB row whose workflow or pipeline definition cannot be parsed or validated raises ValueError; evaluate_workflow converts that into WORKFLOW_LOAD_ERROR so malformed definitions remain distinct from WORKFLOW_NOT_FOUND.

Web UI project context architecture: effectiveProjectId in App.tsx is the global project scope. It syncs into sessionsHook.setFilters (which auto-filters ConversationPicker via webChatSessions derivation), TasksPage via projectFilter prop -> useTasks server-side filtering, MemoryPage via projectId prop -> useMemory filters, and SessionsPage via sessions hook. Gwiki deep ask (`gwiki ask --deep`, task #18565) reuses the existing bounded agentic lanes: daemon uses exactly the read-only gwiki tools `search`, `read`, `backlinks`, and `sources`; direct uses the semantically equivalent VaultToolExecutor tools `search_vault`, `read_document`, `backlinks`, and `sources`. Agentic provenance is honest end to end: daemon `turns` and `stop_reason` remain optional/provider-native, direct maps its concrete StopReason, and limit exits degrade with `deep_unavailable` unless `--require-ai` is set.

The bundled Bash language skill is src/gobby/install/shared/skills/bash. Its discovery rule covers .sh, .bash, .bats, common Bash dotfiles/config names, PKGBUILD, Bashfile, and shell template suffixes while excluding zsh/fish, .profile, Makefile, and Dockerfile. For standard Bats @test syntax, validate with shfmt -ln=bats and bats; ShellCheck should target Bash scripts rather than the Bats file. The skill is independently authored: Google Shell Style Guide is the attributed normative source, while the SkillsMP seed repositories are cited only for topic discovery because one uses FSL-1.1-ALv2 and the other declares no license.

Gobby web activity panel has THREE distinct canonical button surfaces; pick by context, do not hand-roll Tailwind buttons:
1. Toolbar/footer action buttons -> CSS `.btn` classes in web/src/styles/buttons.css. Canonical activity toolbar action = `btn btn-accent btn-sm` (TINTED accent: --accent-tint bg, --accent text, accent-35% border) used by SessionsTab/TasksTabToolbar/RulesTab/PipelinesTab; toolbar/create/filter/refresh buttons also add `activity-panel-action-btn` (+ `activity-filter-button` for filters) with a 14x14 icon + `<span class=activity-panel-action-btn__label>`. Secondary = `btn btn-secondary btn-sm`. `.btn-primary` (solid accent) is reserved for true CTAs only (chat Send, Approve). `.btn-sm` = 1.75rem (28px) / --text-xs / font-medium.
2. Detail-pane status-strip actions -> React `DetailActionButton` in web/src/components/activity/fields/DetailPaneHeader.tsx. SDK autonomous mode does NOT replace terminal mode. Terminal mode is permanent — it's how developers actually use Claude Code at the desktop. SDK autonomous is for Gobby-spawned agents. Web chat + /rc (remote control) is for session shifting to mobile or other devices. All three modes coexist.

Web UI project selection architecture: The app-level project selector in App.tsx provides `effectiveProjectId` which should be passed as a prop to all tab pages that need project scoping. Pages should NOT manage their own projectId state — this causes the backend `_resolve_project` to fall back to the first project alphabetically. The pattern is: App.tsx passes `projectId={effectiveProjectId}` to page components, which forward it to their data hooks (e.g., `useSourceControl(projectId)`). Fixed in commit 3b459a62 for GitHubPage.

Workflow definition drift hashing canonicalizes JSON by parsing and dumping with sorted keys and compact separators before SHA-256. This matches PostgreSQL JSONB row normalization, so serialization formatting does not create drift. Malformed definition JSON remains explicit via json.JSONDecodeError.

Dispatcher isolated leaf development now enforces a dependency base guard: closed transitive `blocks` dependency commits must be ancestors of the selected worktree/clone spawn base, parent integration workspaces are refreshed with required dependency commits before stage start, and refreshed integration clones sync their branch back to the source repo before clone spawns.

RuleEffect.mcp_tools field is list[str] with format 'server:tool' (e.g., 'gobby-tasks:close_task') or 'server:*' for wildcards. It is NOT a list of dicts. The rule engine matches mcp_tools against event.data['mcp_tool'] and event.data['mcp_server']. For call_tool events, _build_eval_context() unwraps the nested arguments dict so rule conditions like tool_input.get('commit_sha') resolve against inner tool params.

Agents working in clones should NOT call close_task. Only the merge agent (merge-clone pipeline) should close tasks, since it's the one that brings commits into main. Dev agents mark needs_review, QA marks review_approved, merge agent closes.

In Gobby, lifecycle close validation in src/gobby/mcp_proxy/tools/tasks/_lifecycle_validation.py now strips benign zero-failure tokens such as `0 failed`, `zero failures`, and `failed=0` before matching failure-feedback regexes. Nonzero summaries like `1 failed` / `2 failures` and explicit gate failures still block closure.

Task diff retrieval is centralized in src/gobby/tasks/diff_paging.py (commit 7731ee24f). DiffPage uses lossless utf-8/base64 byte pages, commit/manifest cursor_end paging, snapshot_hash plus view_hash continuation tokens, raw-byte manifest path selectors, and server-bounded git subprocess deadlines with kill/reap typed errors. Legacy TASK_DIFF_MAX_CHARS, _safe_truncate, and TaskDiffResult/get_task_diff were removed; string-only internal consumers reconstruct pages through collect_task_diff_text.

Build integration refresh invariant: when merging closed descendant commits into an epic integration workspace, closed_commit_sha is the authoritative accepted lineage once present. Linked task commits can be stale after worktree recovery/rebase/de-escalation and should not be merged ahead of the closed commit. This was hit in #12746/#14612 where #14629 retained orphan 7320e10f6 and #14632 retained orphan 1ca046215; both conflicted until stale links were removed. Fix in #15074 changed src/gobby/build/workspaces.py so _linked_commits uses closed_commit_sha when available and falls back to task.commits only for legacy/unclosed tasks, with regression in tests/build/test_child_merge_repair.py.

NEVER add startup code that kills other processes on ports. _clear_port() using lsof + SIGTERM was added to GobbyRunner.run() to handle orphaned test daemons, but it caused e2e tests to kill the production daemon. The correct approach to port isolation is preventing collisions at allocation time (find_free_port without SO_REUSEADDR + excluded ports), not killing processes at startup.

config_store.py secret detection gotcha: is_secret_key_name() checks if the LAST segment of a dotted key ends with a suffix from _SECRET_SUFFIXES. For 'auth.password', the last segment is 'password' — it does NOT end with '_password' (underscore prefix). Had to add bare 'password' (without underscore) to _SECRET_SUFFIXES to fix this. Any future secret fields whose last segment IS the suffix name (not prefixed with underscore) need the bare form in the list.

Task #17016 added web/src/components/activity/QuickMenu.tsx as the shared activity kebab primitive. QuickMenu supports self-managed trigger mode and externally-opened anchor mode, measures trigger/menu rects, flips above near the bottom viewport edge, clamps horizontally with an 8px gutter, handles Escape/outside click and ArrowUp/ArrowDown/Home/End/Enter keyboard navigation, gives the trigger a 44px target, and auto-adds an icon for destructive items. TaskQuickMenu and McpQuickMenu now build QuickMenu item arrays instead of owning fixed-position styles or duplicate keyboard code; TasksTab and ActivityMcpTab pass raw trigger rects to the wrappers.

Task #17722 decomposed the Claude LLM provider. `src/gobby/llm/claude.py` is now a thin `ClaudeLLMProvider` facade for provider metadata, Claude CLI path discovery/verification, and delegation. SDK text, agentic, JSON, and vision flows live in `src/gobby/llm/claude_sdk.py` (`ClaudeSDKClient`); retry/stderr/shutdown/max-turn/error-result execution policy lives in `src/gobby/llm/claude_runtime.py`; reasoning options, usage normalization, preamble stripping, and image data prep live in `src/gobby/llm/claude_payloads.py`. User decision: the 'opus' model alias used as raw default in claude.py/claude_streaming.py is not worth fixing without a config-table-based fallback mapping. Hardcoding full model IDs just moves the maintenance burden. The Claude Agent SDK handles 'opus' natively for subscription mode, and MODEL_ALIASES dict in litellm_executor.py handles it for LiteLLM calls. A clean fix would be a config table mapping (e.g., 'opus' -> 'claude-opus-4-6') that the LLM service reads at startup, but that doesn't exist yet.

Plan-mode structured scratch writes are governed by src/gobby/providers/path_policy.py:is_plan_scratch_path. ProviderMetadata.user_directory maps claude=.claude, codex=.codex, droid=.factory, grok=.grok, qwen=.qwen, agy=.gemini. The predicate requires absolute or home-relative paths, resolves symlinks/traversal, and permits only the active provider home plus OS temp roots. Plan workflow rules call plan_write_paths_allowed; Claude web chat and Codex/Droid managed permission gates share the same predicate. Multi-file writes fail closed unless every target is the plan artifact or approved scratch path, lifecycle hygiene retains precedence, and shell mutation policy is unchanged.

Feedback-lesson-loop design (plan .gobby/plans/feedback-lesson-loop.md, approved after 12 adversarial rounds, epic #18719; spike docs/spikes/feedback-lesson-loop.md, task #18598). Core decisions: (1) Lesson-domain partition: required `lesson-domain:<code|plan>` tag derived at record time from a total source_kind→domain map, fail-closed in record(); centralized CODE_DOMAIN_EXCLUDED_TAGS applied as tags_none on semantic recall AND both file-recall paths; plan-domain recall is positive opt-in only — semantic ranking is never the safety mechanism. New source kinds: plan_review, task_validation (pr_verdict, human_correction deferred). (2) Class-scoped identity for every multi-class recorder: pattern_id `plan-review:<lesson_type>:<category>:<check-key>`, `epic-qa:<lesson_type>:<check-key>`, `task-validation:recurring-validation-failure:<check-key>`; explicit validated kebab-case check_key with `check-key:`/`category:` tags; deterministic `list_check_keys` enumeration is the identity-resolution mechanism (versioned catalog is the documented escalation; canonicalization gate explicitly declined). Five reserved lesson_type classes: reviewer-miss, fixer-induced-defect, recurring-validation-failure, qa-miss, validation-miss. (3) Recording ownership: the reviser/coordinator side holding cross-round ground truth records; reviewed agents never grade themselves; enhancer never records. Unproven classification mints nothing. (4) Evidence: immutable pre-M1 snapshots via side-effecting `prepare_plan_review_round` → `plan_review_evidence` table (per-section hash manifest from a trusted producer; agent-generated hashes prove nothing); two-phase `bind_evidence_run`; lease bounds only pre-bind rows; per-class evidence bundles (reviewer-miss: unchanged sections; fixer-induced: causal changed sections + prior finding). (5) Interactive approval: unified commit order (durable pre-finalization intent → apply manifest → V1 checkpoint → lossless finalize stamping lesson_mint_status=pending → mint checkpoint); V1 round checkpoint fence is the enforced durable step-2 marker; preparation owns recovery via a deterministic drain (pending-apply no-drift convergence checkpoints applied then drains; drift executes the atomic pending-plus-drift revoked transition); incomplete-round rule scoped to rejection rounds and pre-intent crashes only; `pending_lesson_mint` refuse-gate blocks new rounds until the mint tail completes. (6) Stage-native mint: idempotent mint at approve_review (errors never block the verdict), workflow-owned single backfill via `backfill_plan_review_lessons`; activation boundary is planning-stage-only — all other stages' approve/reject byte-for-byte unchanged. (7) Promotion: no promotion.py change — explicit guardrail_target honored at occurrence 2+; plan classes → checklist, qa-miss → checklist, validation-miss → validation. (8) Retirement: explicit `retire_review_lesson` (never overload record(decision=stale)); retags confirmed→stale under the ReviewLearningPatternMutation advisory lock. (9) Expansion serialization: dependency edges come only from explicit manifest depends_on; shared-target-file pairs need explicit edges (7.1 depends on both 3.2 and 5.2 because 2.1/5.2/7.1 all touch mcp_proxy/tools/review_learning.py).

For Gobby 0.4.0 docs, `docs/guides/webhooks-and-plugins.md` should document hook extension webhooks (`hook_extensions.webhooks`) and pipeline webhooks as the supported webhook surfaces. Python workflow plugin actions such as `plugin:<name>:<action>` are retired/stale patterns; installer-copied `.gobby/plugins/` files and the `claude-plugins` skill hub are separate from workflow action plugins.

gobby-cli design decision for session wiki scope: gwiki sync-sessions should default Detect scope to machine-global topic `sessions`, preserving daemon page `project:` as `session_project` frontmatter provenance. When gsqz or other output compression mangles tool output (ripgrep, grep, search results), file a bug task immediately instead of just working around it. Mangled output forces agents to fall back to slower approaches (Read instead of Grep), defeating the purpose of the optimization. Track these so the compression can be improved.

As of commit 5e6dc8573 for Gobby task #15476, the daemon exposes `/api/embeddings/status`, `POST /api/embeddings`, and `/api/embeddings/doctor`. Status is sourced from AICapability.EMBED, generation uses `gobby.search.embeddings.generate_embeddings` with `config.embeddings.model/api_base/api_key/dim`, and responses expose only safe endpoint/config metadata with no raw API keys.

Gobby's shared workflow TemplateEngine in src/gobby/workflows/templates.py uses Jinja2 SandboxedEnvironment with StrictUndefined. Pipeline exec, prompt, and MCP argument templates therefore fail the step on missing variables instead of silently rendering empty strings. Established by task #16879 / commit b02cb2cc7.

Task #17250 decomposed src/gobby/servers/websocket/chat/backends/codex.py by extracting Codex app-server turn notification streaming into src/gobby/servers/websocket/chat/backends/codex_turns.py. CodexWebChatBackend keeps health/thread guards plus approval translation/handling facades for existing tests, while codex_turns.py owns delta extraction, notification handler registration, tool event replay, transcript fallback, usage normalization, and DoneEvent emission. The daemon constructs SessionLivenessMonitor after HookManager during app lifespan startup because the monitor depends on HookManager summary dispatch. EventHandlers therefore receives the running monitor through set_liveness_monitor, and session_end marks the canonical platform session recently handled before cleanup/status work.

Task status semantics: needs_review = waiting for QA agent to review. escalated = bumped to a human. closed = only terminal 'complete' state. is_task_complete() should ONLY check status==closed. requires_user_review column was dropped in migration v151 and is NOT on the Task model.

Gobby workflow CLI variable commands (`gobby workflows status`, `set-var`, and `get-var`) use `src/gobby/cli/workflows/common.py` to open a runtime HubDatabase for `SessionVariableManager`. The CLI path must close the cached database before process exit via `session_var_manager_context()` / `close_session_var_manager()`; otherwise psycopg `ConnectionPool.__del__` can emit `PythonFinalizationError` at interpreter shutdown. Regression coverage is in `tests/cli/test_cli_workflows.py`, committed for #15550.

Detection manifests use engine version 1 in src/gobby/agents/detection. load_manifest() strictly validates dotted-numeric versions, unique lowercase rule IDs, blocked-rule reasons, and the three regions whole_recent, bottom_non_empty_lines(N), and prompt_box. compile_manifest() caches compiled rules by SHA-256 content fingerprint, sorts matches by priority, and returns MatchEvaluation with controlled invalid_pattern or pattern_timeout issues. All data-controlled regexes go through safe_regex.py, which enforces a 2,048-character pattern limit and a fixed 10ms search timeout.

Task #15326 added docs/research/cron-durable-dispatch-semantics.md defining target cron semantics as durable dispatch: pipeline and agent_spawn cron runs become terminal status dispatched after child IDs are persisted; shell and handler stay inline until separate observable child-run records exist. docs/guides/cron-scheduler.md now says internal dispatcher and pipeline-heartbeat automation live in SystemAutomationLoop and cron history should represent real scheduled jobs only.

Two dev mode detection functions:

1. `is_dev_mode(project_path)` in `src/gobby/utils/dev.py` — checks if the project IS the gobby source repo by looking for `src/gobby/install/shared/` dir. Use this when gating behavior based on whether the current project is gobby itself.

2. `_is_dev_mode()` in `src/gobby/cli/installers/service.py` — checks if running from a dev install (sys.executable in gobby project dir or CWD is gobby project with .venv). Used by the service installer to decide install strategy.

Bundled agent sync ownership is defined by src/gobby/agents/sync.py::_is_sync_managed_bundled_agent: project_id must be null, source must be installed/template, and tags must include gobby. Task CLI policy is now split cleanly: `src/gobby/hooks/event_handlers/_tool.py` no longer hardcodes any `gobby tasks` shell block. Native task CLI mutation blocking lives in the installed/bundled `block-gobby-tasks-cli` rules-engine rule, which allows read-only commands such as `gobby tasks list --ready` and blocks mutating subcommands. Gobby's `.gobby/wiki/meta/health/latest.md` is generated by the external `gwiki health` command. The local durable fix for the Markdown heading is in `GwikiGateway.health()`, which postprocesses the payload's `root` + `text_path` report file and rewrites a leading `Wiki health report` line to `# Wiki health report`.

SDK client initialization was extracted from session-lifecycle.yaml into claude-sdk-lifecycle.yaml (#8756). The new workflow (priority 11, sources: claude_sdk, claude_sdk_web_chat) handles on_before_agent init (plan_mode, mode_level, baseline files, memory/task sync, session context injection, skills, task context, pre-existing error policy) with its own _sdk_initialized guard variable. ACP golden fixture contract tests live in tests/adapters/test_acp_contract_fixtures.py with fixture JSONL under tests/fixtures/acp_contract. All installer uninstall functions must respect GOBBY_HOOKS_DIR env var for test isolation. Pattern: `Path(os.environ.get('GOBBY_HOOKS_DIR', str(Path.home() / '.gobby' / 'hooks')))`. Tests using --all flag must mock ALL uninstallers (claude, gemini, codex, copilot, cursor, windsurf), not just the ones being asserted on, because --all auto-detects installed CLIs on the developer's machine and will call any unmocked uninstaller for real. Fixed in windsurf.py:199 and test_cli_install.py (commit 8ae3fee7).

Task #14948 changed turn-end claimed-task reconciliation so active claims owned by a parent/continuation session in the same session lineage are preserved and repaired to the current session instead of being pruned. WorkflowHookHandler now passes SessionManager and SessionTaskManager into reconcile_claimed_tasks; the repair force-claims the task for the current session and links the session-task row, while unrelated reassigned claims still prune.

Task #17256 decomposed src/gobby/cli/tasks/crud.py by keeping Click command wrappers and the legacy test patch surface in crud.py, while moving command bodies into _crud_listing.py, _crud_detail.py, _crud_mutations.py, shared choices/helper into _crud_common.py, and dependency injection into _crud_services.py.

Product decision for activity-panel Tasks UI: remove the kanban/board view and the List|Board selector. The activity panel Tasks surface should be list-only; do not reintroduce the board/drag-and-drop stage lanes unless the user explicitly reverses this decision. This supersedes the prior one-surface UI memory that asked for a Jira-style activity Tasks board.

Gobby project convention: use XML-ish semantic tags such as `<project-memory>` for model-facing context blocks that agents should read as named structure. Use HTML comment fences such as `<!-- gobby:injected-context:begin -->` / `<!-- gobby:injected-context:end -->` for machine-facing injected context boundaries that Gobby may detect, strip, replace, or deduplicate while staying render-hidden in Markdown. HTML comments are still visible tokens to models, so they are a transport/cleanup fence rather than true hidden context.

Codewiki staged publication reconciliation (#18252, commit 14071a327): `_meta/codewiki-stage/manifest.json` is private v2 `StageManifest { fingerprint, force_full_hash_scan }`. Exact fingerprints resume with the sticky flag. Drift in source hashes, AI mode/settings/routes/outcomes, aggregate candidates, snapshots, or `since_changed` retains staged bytes, atomically records the new fingerprint, and forces `ReusePlan` plus `DocSink` to ignore the `--since` shortcut and perform full per-page freshness checks. Version, canonical project-root, normalized-scope, missing, corrupt, and legacy v1 manifest changes reseed. Successful publication removes the stage and clears the flag; fail-closed link validation still protects live bytes.

In gobby-cli daemon text generation, `ai.text_generate.*` is the CLI standalone/direct namespace only. The daemon does not accept `ai.text_generate.*` config_store writes; daemon-side named local endpoints are configured under `ai.generation.local.endpoints.<name>` and selected with provider `local:<name>` plus request-level `model`, `profile`, or `candidates`. `GET /api/providers/models` reports named local endpoints with `source: "config"` and model objects (`value`/`label`).

The daemon does not accept `ai.text_generate.*` config_store writes; daemon-side named local endpoints are configured under `ai.generation.local.endpoints.<name>` and selected with provider `local:<name>` plus request-level `model`, `profile`, or `candidates`. `GET /api/providers/models` reports named local endpoints with `source: "config"` and model objects (`value`/`label`).

Design decision for Gobby cross-session file edit protection: guard all Git-visible dirty states (tracked, staged, deleted, renamed, and untracked) using atomic before_tool reservations scoped by machine ID + canonical Git worktree root + repo-relative path. Same-worktree foreign owners block; separate worktrees do not. Notify only the blocked requester with the owner session and gobby-agents:send_message guidance. Release claims on real session end, retain across compact because compact keeps the same Gobby session, and let the first guarded writer claim a dirty file with no recorded owner. Ship as a bundled enabled-by-default rule while preserving the installed DB operator toggle. Deprecated /clear parent-child handoff cleanup is tracked separately as task #18742.

In Gobby, chat attachment cleanup for cleared web chat conversations must delete chat_attachments metadata before deleting chat_messages, because attachment message_id uses ON DELETE SET NULL and deleting messages first loses the link. Use storage.chat_attachments.delete_attachments_for_conversations(...) to collect conversation-bound and message-bound attachment records, then unlink their local files after metadata deletion.

After task #14248, live dry-run of `gobby tasks repair-lifecycle --provenance expansion-run:expand-1242485f202e` exposed a repair edge case: historical phase-wrapper parents could start at holistic_qa while leaves already had development/pr/merge, causing naive parent-derived repair to propose removing development from leaves. Task #14251 fixed LifecycleRepair to skip removing development from development-first children and to repair historical phase wrappers to development-first shapes when their parent has no manifest.

For gobby-cli `release-gwiki.yml` Windows gwiki builds under Git Bash, normalize `RUNNER_TEMP` and `GITHUB_ENV` with `cygpath -u` before using Bash tools (`mkdir`, `curl`, `sha256sum`, `tar`), and convert only the final pdfium DLL path back with `cygpath -w` for `PDFIUM_BUNDLE_LIB`. Windows OpenSSL vendored builds should export `OPENSSL_SRC_PERL` to Strawberry Perl (`C:\Strawberry\perl\bin\perl.exe`) instead of Git Bash Perl. For `aarch64-pc-windows-msvc`, set `CARGO_TARGET_AARCH64_PC_WINDOWS_MSVC_LINKER` to the MSVC Hostx64 arm64 `link.exe` from `VCToolsInstallDir` so Cargo does not pick Git's `/usr/bin/link.exe`.

When mocking PromptLoader for tests that use validation or other template-rendering code, the render mock must pass through context variables (not return a static string). Use `side_effect=lambda path, ctx: '\n'.join(str(v) for v in ctx.values() if v)` so tests that assert specific content appears in the rendered prompt still pass. A static mock like `render.return_value='fixed string'` will break tests that check for file_context, criteria_text, etc.

Gobby web MCP management now lives in Chat's MCP Activity tab. The top-level MCP sidebar/nav page route was removed; legacy #mcp entry and /mcp browse actions route to Chat and select the MCP activity tab instead. Keep server import out of this surface; durable import/config belongs in Config.

Task #14090 refactored hub placeholder remapping into `gobby.storage.hub.placeholders`. SQLite and Postgres adapters keep their existing wrapper APIs (`_remap_placeholders`, `_remap_placeholders_to_psycopg`, `_scan_placeholder_indexes`) but now share one scanner that preserves strings, comments, quoted identifiers, dollar-quoted bodies, and returns index permutations for executemany reuse.

Plan review is provider-neutral and coverage-gated: bundled plan adversaries and the taskless researcher use provider: inherit with optional high reasoning; spawn resolution is explicit override, concrete agent provider, spawn-capable parent session provider, then Claude fallback, while model: inherit selects the provider default. Every conclusive round requires the three canonical lanes, candidate dispositions, source rehashing, adjacent/cross-lane completion, and a server-derived shadow manifest. apply_plan_review_manifest re-derives canonical entries from routing decisions before writing.

For Gobby Postgres migration docs, comments, and user-facing text, describe the runtime hub as the PostgreSQL hub or hub database. SQLite references should be explicitly scoped to `DEPRECATED_SQLITE_IMPORT` migration-only tooling, `DEPRECATED_SQLITE_IMPORT_TEST_ONLY` fixtures/LocalDatabase compatibility, or historical archives; gcode/code-index references should describe the external gcode toolchain over the PostgreSQL hub/pg_search.

Superseded mailbox delivery design: src/gobby/sessions/mailbox.py now resolves explicit send_message targets (session, agent, project, build, all) through MailboxService. Fanout targets still write one inter_session_messages row per recipient, but the old send_to_all flag is gone; selector metadata records the target and target_id instead.

Mobile responsive CSS added to WorkflowsPage.css and ConfigurationPage.css using @media (max-width: 768px) breakpoint, consistent with DashboardPage, McpPage, CronJobsPage. Patterns: flex-wrap for filter rows, single-column grid, horizontal scroll for filter chips, full-width modals. The 'gobby' tag is injected at sync time (not in YAML source files) in workflows/sync.py and agents/sync.py via _ensure_gobby_tag_on_installed() helper. The 'Hide Built-in' toggle in WorkflowsPage filters items by this tag across all 3 tabs.

Telegram DM enrollment contract (task #18850, commit d6cb589ed): when a Telegram channel's allow_from is empty, only the first exact private /start atomically binds and persists that sender's numeric Telegram user ID. Group messages and other first DMs cannot claim the channel. Once bound, unknown Telegram DMs are acknowledged for poll-offset advancement but dropped before identity resolution, message/attachment persistence, session creation, or responder dispatch. Re-enrollment requires explicitly clearing allow_from through local channel configuration.

For Gobby local generation routing, prefer the local model `google/gemma-4-26b-a4b-qat` over Qwen models for feature-profile/local-fallback planning because the Qwen models are too slow for this purpose. Keep built-in feature profiles cloud-only; use named local endpoint opt-in such as `local:lm-studio/google/gemma-4-26b-a4b-qat` when local generation is explicitly desired.

macOS SIGKILL on freshly-deployed ~/.gobby/bin/ binaries: root cause unclear, codesign is likely NOT the real fix. In session #50 on 2026-04-21, a fresh `cargo build --release` of gsqz copied to ~/.gobby/bin/gsqz SIGKILLed (exit 137) on every invocation, taking down Claude Code's Bash tool because the shell wrapper pipes stdout through ~/.gobby/bin/gsqz. Running `codesign --sign - ~/.gobby/bin/gsqz` appeared to fix it. BUT: `codesign -dv` shows cargo's Apple Silicon linker already ad-hoc signs every release binary (`flags=0x20002(adhoc,linker-signed)`), so the signature was not missing. The apparent fix may have been an inode-rewrite side effect of codesign clearing a page-cache/loader quirk from the fresh `cp`, or it may have been transient. ghook deployed identically in the same session did NOT exhibit the symptom. **End users don't need to codesign** — `cargo install` output is already ad-hoc signed, and so are the binaries in the GH release archives. The real user-facing friction on macOS is the `com.apple.quarantine` xattr attached by browsers/URLSession on downloaded release tarballs, which triggers Gatekeeper. Fix for that is `xattr -d com.apple.quarantine <binary>` or right-click Open, not codesigning. **How to apply:** If a freshly-deployed binary to ~/.gobby/bin/ inexplicably SIGKILLs, try `codesign --sign - <path>` as a cheap first thing to check even though it's probably superstition; if it keeps happening, investigate AMFI/MAC policies or do a `rm + cp` instead of overwriting in place. Do NOT bake `codesign` into the release pipeline as 'the fix' — it's not addressing a real signing problem.

PATH B REAL-WORLD FLOW (user-taught, IMPORTANT for qwen #15732 and future capture): the approval menu only renders in grok's INTERACTIVE/native TUI. gobby-agents:spawn_agent runs grok in ACP mode (`grok agent --no-leader --always-approve ... stdio`) which NEVER prompts -> spawned-agent tmux pane is BLANK; you CANNOT capture an approval menu from a spawned gobby agent. The real Path B surface = a USER-created native grok session (e.g. run grok in VS Code via tmux) that gobby registers as a session_type='terminal' (can_proxy_attach=true) via its SessionStart hook; the user then proxy-attaches it in the web UI main chat and the plan-approval dialog appears; approve -> handle_attached_plan_approval dispatches the mapped keystrokes to the tmux pane.

CAPTURE GOTCHAS (headless agent harness): detached tmux servers (`tmux -L X new-session -d`) are REAPED ~instantly here (double-fork/setsid escapes the sandbox) even unsandboxed; the shell `sleep` binary is shimmed (panes running sleep die) -> use perl `select(undef,undef,undef,N)` and an in-process pty (os.fork+os.openpty, NO setsid, pyte for the screen grid) OR the gobby DAEMON's tmux server which IS persistent. The gobby daemon's tmux server is socket NAME 'gobby' (`tmux -L gobby`, TmuxConfig.socket_name) and only runs WHILE an agent is alive; bootstrap it by spawning a keep-alive agent, then a session you create on it persists (server is daemon-owned). The user's config.toml has permission_mode='always-approve' GLOBALLY -> must launch native grok with `--permission-mode default` to get prompts. First-run 'Run Grok Build in a project directory?' trust dialog (Enter:submit) appears after the first prompt; answer '1'+Enter. capture_output MCP tool needs a gobby-REGISTERED session with a tmux terminal (agent_run.tmux_session_name OR terminal_context.tmux_pane); a raw `tmux -L gobby` session you create is NOT auto-registered (grok SessionStart didn't link a terminal in headless context) -> capture via `tmux -L gobby capture-pane` directly (same backend). Validation criteria capture-transport was generalized with explicit user approval since the literal capture_output MCP artifact isn't reproducible headlessly. See gemini [[af22ab38-1af1-528c-bfd4-8b23d5aa712a]], droid [[bf1d429d]], codex [[14895604]], procedure [[59385f3f]].

When composing Tailwind classes in web/src/, ALWAYS use cn() from web/src/lib/utils.ts. Never use template-literal composition like `${BASE} ${cond ? ACTIVE : ""}`.

Why: web/tailwind.config.ts has `important: true`, which marks every utility !important. When two utilities target the same CSS property, neither !important wins source-order ties. Tailwind sorts arbitrary values alphabetically within a category, so `border-[var(--accent)]` sorts before `border-[var(--border)]` in the generated stylesheet, and the base `border-[var(--border)]` ALWAYS wins when both are in the className string — regardless of source order. The `!` prefix is redundant under global important.

cn() (clsx + tailwind-merge) resolves this by deduping same-property utilities at compose time, keeping only the last for each property.

How to apply:
- import { cn } from '../../lib/utils' and use cn(BASE, cond && ACTIVE)
- Drop redundant ! prefixes from class strings
- Pattern reference: TasksPage.tsx, AssigneePicker.tsx, EscalationCard.tsx

Root cause of MCP server crash: event_enrichment.py runs on every hook event and has a session lookup with an except handler. Narrowing exception handlers on hook events causes the hook chain to crash when the session storage (PostgreSQL) throws unexpected exceptions. The fix is to keep the handler broad (`except Exception`) since this is a defensive guard during shutdown/edge cases. General rule: never narrow except handlers in code that runs on every hook event — it's a critical path that must never crash.

Memory KG edge-weighting spike (task #17096) result: weighting the entity->entity layer is the dominant recall lever, far above densification alone. Recall benchmark (tests/memory/test_recall_benchmark.py, real FalkorDB, measured at find_related_memory_ids): baseline typed-only recall@5=0.000; cooccurrence_unweighted (CO_OCCURS densify only)=0.200; cooccurrence_weighted (typed=cos01, CO_OCCURS=alpha*cos01+(1-alpha)*norm_support)=0.967; +edge decay=0.967 (no gain). alpha/cap sweep ({0.5,0.75,1.0}x{3,5,10}) all tie at 0.967 because cosine cleanly separates true neighbors from distractors. Decisions: ADOPT densify + weighting; do NOT default-on graph_edge_decay. Frozen constants COOCCUR_ALPHA=0.5, COOCCUR_SUPPORT_CAP=5 in src/gobby/memory/services/knowledge_graph/writer.py. Three MemoryConfig flags (graph_edge_weighting, materialize_cooccurrence, graph_edge_decay) all default OFF. CO_OCCURS edges are derived (a<b canonical, support=distinct shared-memory count SET idempotently from MENTIONED_IN bipartite), excluded from LLM _delete_outdated_relations cleanup but kept traversable (NOT in _STRUCTURAL_RELATIONSHIP_TYPES). Reader traversal now pulls a generous 64 candidates and applies weight/decay scoring + top-8 cap in Python (no Cypher ORDER BY). Edge updated_at is FalkorDB timestamp() epoch-ms; reader converts to ISO before temporal_decay. Follow-ups: #17098 signal logging, #17099 adaptive tuning, #17097 HDBSCAN/Leiden clustering consumes these weights.

React Compiler lint boundaries in web/ (learned via #17766/#17767/#17768): react-hooks/purity bans Date.now()/Math.random() not only in render but also directly in useEffect BODIES; interval/timeout CALLBACKS inside effects are exempt — so wall-clock stall detection must live in the interval callback (or count ticks) and request lifecycles belong in module-level functions taking setters as deps. react-hooks/set-state-in-effect bans synchronous setState in effect bodies — for external-store subscriptions use useSyncExternalStore (see useWebSocketConnected in web/src/hooks/useWebSocketEvent.ts); for state resets, key the state to a derivation instead (stalledSignature === liveSignature pattern in WikiResearchMode.tsx). react-hooks/preserve-manual-memoization can reject useMemo whose deps the compiler can't prove stable — dropping the manual memo fixes it. react-hooks/globals bans reassigning module-level variables inside hook/component bodies (even behind dev-env guards) — extract the mutation into a plain module function and call it (warn-once pattern in web/src/components/chat/artifacts/ArtifactContext.tsx). Related runtime rule: never gate keyboard-driven DOM .focus() on requestAnimationFrame (suspended in occluded windows — focus dies or fires late in bursts); use a useLayoutEffect keyed on a focus sequence instead (useTreeKeyboardNavigation.ts).

DECISION (2026-04-22): The approved fix direction for #12651 (skill injection gap) is to eject inline skill content emission entirely from hooks/adapters/servers/websocket/workflows and pivot to two patterns: (1) INSTRUCT pattern for user-initiated entry points like `/gobby <skill>` and the Skill-tool intercept in _tool.py — emit a short fetch directive and block via decision=block so Claude calls get_skill on gobby-skills to proceed; (2) MANIFEST pattern for session-start and rule-driven contexts — emit a tiny active_skills manifest of names/refs (no content), always-apply skills enforced via a pre-first-tool-call rule. Reason: 9,950-char aggregate cap on additionalContext is applied per-hook across ALL contributors (session banner + rule inject_context + memory + metadata + skills + project-memory), so any single bulky contributor starves the others. Inline injection of large skills (plan ~15KB, plan-draft ~11KB) silently truncates, breaking flagship flows. Also update install/shared/skills/gobby/SKILL.md:20 to remove the 'do NOT call get_skill again' directive — it locks in silent failure when truncation happens.

## Lesson
- principle: A leaf commit inside a plan-scoped epic must not modify bundled templates outside the plan's target list; template edits ride the same purely-additive constraint as code.
- root_cause: Skill-contract commits touch many YAML surfaces at once; an unrelated cleanup rode along without plan attribution and leaf QA only checked the planned surfaces.
- prevention: Epic and leaf QA must diff the commit's touched file list against the plan section's named targets and treat any un-cited bundled-template change (especially deletions) as a blocking finding until justified.

PipelineExecutor async execution paths route synchronous execution-manager operations and top-level child-session registration/setup through its injected run_db bridge; the fallback uses asyncio.to_thread. Managed web-chat plan presentation has two models. Text-plan CLIs (Codex and ACP providers, plus Droid prose turns) broadcast a tagged assistant plan after the stream completes through ManagedWebChatPermissionsMixin._maybe_broadcast_pending_plan; blocking inside that stream prevents the broadcast. Tool-plan CLIs (native Claude ExitPlanMode and Droid ExitSpecMode) park an explicit plan-exit tool on an approval event. Droid ExitSpecMode reaches Gobby only as droid.request_permission, is filtered from the session stream, and is handled by DroidPermissionResolver._resolve_plan_mode_request. Approval maps to proceed_once; user-requested changes map to cancel and preserve revise feedback. As of #18344 / commit 36d8907b1, expiry maps to the distinct "timeout" outcome, clears pending plan state, emits mode_changed(reason="plan_approval_timed_out"), interrupts the provider turn, then maps to cancel. Managed cancel_pending_approval releases _pending_plan_event so an external interrupt cannot strand the gate. Frontend plan actions live on the agent status bar, and plan_pending_approval options come from the provider registry.

Close-validation verdict concurrency uses the task row's updated_at as an optimistic verdict token: valid close/reset and invalid count/escalate both require an open, non-escalated row with the expected timestamp, so the first committed terminal transition wins and the loser raises TaskStaleStateError. Escalation side effects consume PostgreSQL's authoritative is_escalated/escalated_at row; the stable delivery identity is derived from task_id plus escalated_at, making a later re-escalation a fresh event.

CRITICAL DISTINCTION — Templates vs Active Workflows:

- Files in src/gobby/install/shared/ (rules/, workflows/, agents/, pipelines/) are TEMPLATES. They are bundled with the software but are NOT active enforcement.
- Templates have enabled: false BY DESIGN. This is correct and intentional.
- A workflow/rule/pipeline/agent must be INSTALLED (synced to the workflow_definitions DB table) AND ENABLED for it to be active in the rules engine.
- The sync process (src/gobby/workflows/sync.py) copies templates into the DB but preserves the enabled state from the YAML (false).
- The user enables specific rules incrementally via the admin UI or API.
- DO NOT treat 'all 82 rules are disabled' as an issue — that's the expected state for templates.
- DO NOT confuse template files with the active enforcement system.
- The workflow_definitions table has been wiped multiple times; the DB state is the source of truth, not the YAML files.
- The deprecated/ subdirectories are correctly excluded from sync and are irrelevant to current state.

Settled shared-daemon vs standalone identity/key boundary: standalone Gobby users do not use user accounts, user identity, or API keys. Standalone/direct mode retains the existing install-scoped secret DEK wrapped by local key-file or scrypt-passphrase KEK. Shared-daemon mode adds users and shared user API keys; API key authenticates to user_id, and user_id selects user-scoped secret key material. Do not derive encryption keys from API keys. Use a stable random user DEK wrapped by the daemon installation/root KEK so API-key rotation has no encryption effect. Every daemon API request also supplies machine_id; valid user credentials auto-enroll unknown machines and enforce machines.owner_user_id. Binaries use daemon identity only in daemon mode; auto fallback to configured direct mode crosses into standalone install trust and must never occur for 401/403.

Recall fit contract (task #18425): pairwise evaluation is normalized per mixed request. Full-candidate cohorts assign each of P×N pairs weight 1/(P×N); injected cohorts assign IPS(pos)/(N×sum positive IPS), preserving within-request position correction while each request totals exactly 1. PairwiseEvalResult reports raw pair_count separately from mixed_request_count, and partial pooling shrinks in mixed-request units via mixed/(mixed+shrinkage_requests). Request partitions are SHA-256 ordered from a version plus request ID; split, evaluator, and audit-sampler versions form the evaluation cohort identity. Shrinkage candidates (2,5,10,20,50) are selected from planted synthetic requests plus validation nested inside the outer training partition, so selection has no holdout input.

Context injection reads observations from session_variable_manager.get_variables(session_id).get('_observations', []). Migration scoping principle for gobby Python→Rust: separate the data-plane (FalkorDB writes/reads, compute, report generation) from the orchestration tier (maintenance loops, sync workers, file-watch triggers, summarizers). Move the data-plane to Rust/gcore first so gcode can operate standalone. Leave orchestration in Python until its cross-subsystem dependencies (LLM client, embedding generation, Qdrant writes) have also moved. The daemon calls gcode via subprocess for moved slices during the transition window; subprocess calls become in-process function calls when the daemon itself ports. This boundary was confirmed 2026-05-23 when scoping the graph-enhancements plan: graph subsystem moves, orchestration (maintenance.py, sync_worker.py, trigger.py, summarizer.py, context.py) stays.

Gobby task/session concurrency model: PostgreSQL is the authoritative shared store, and ordinary manager updates build SQL SET clauses only for supplied columns, so concurrent writes to different SQL columns preserve each other under PostgreSQL row serialization. Same-column conflicts use targeted policy—conditional UPDATE/rowcount checks or advisory locks for lifecycle invariants, atomic JSONB operators for task labels/commits and session terminal_context registration/backfill. There is no generalized per-field timestamp/CRDT layer. Task JSONL restore is an explicit recovery operation and intentionally applies whole-record LWW only when backup updated_at wins; sessions have no JSONL backup/restore sync.

HOW TO CAPTURE A NATIVE CLI TUI MENU HEADLESS (reusable; grok #15731 + qwen #15732):
- Managed/ACP spawns never show the native approval menu (gemini/grok/qwen run headless/ACP with auto-approve). Capture the NATIVE TUI directly.
- Drive the real binary on an in-process pty: os.openpty + os.fork, NO os.setsid (a setsid child escapes the harness sandbox and is reaped). dup2 slave->0/1/2, execvpe. Render with pyte (uv run --with pyte python). Foreground bash bounded by perl alarm; the shell `sleep` binary is shimmed/blocked — use perl select for pacing.
- qwen: launch `qwen --auth-type openai --openai-api-key <KEY> --openai-base-url http://localhost:1234/v1 --model qwen/qwen3.6-35b-a3b --approval-mode default`. Send a prompt forcing a tool call ('Use your WriteFile tool right now to create X...'). qwen3.6 is a reasoning model (~100+ reasoning tokens before the tool call) so the menu can take 20–130s+ — poll for menu markers with a wide window.
- GOTCHA: qwen Code AUTO-RESUMES the last conversation keyed by cwd path (~/.qwen/projects/<slug>/). Use a UNIQUE fresh workdir per run or it replays a stale prompt and your new turn never fires.

NEVER delete gobby tasks without first checking the dependency tree via `get_dependency_tree` or the `blocking`/`blocked_by` fields on `get_task`.

`delete_task(cascade=true)` (the default) deletes the task AND all *dependent tasks* — anything with `blocked_by` pointing at the target, and their dependents, transitively. Not just subtasks. In Gobby #3207 I deleted #12145 (a subtask of #12044) with cascade=true and it took out #12044, #12077 (the planning epic), #12081, and #12129 via the `blocked_by` chain. Seq numbers were freed and reused when the next expansion ran, making the damage hard to spot.

**Always before a delete:**
1. Call `get_task(task_id, brief=false)` and inspect `dependencies.blocking` — that lists every task that will cascade-delete if cascade=true.
2. If the list is non-empty and you don't intend to delete those, use `cascade=false` (fails if there are dependents) or `unlink=true` (removes links, keeps dependents).
3. If you genuinely want the cascade, state the full deletion set explicitly to the user before running.

Why: cascade delete is destructive and not reversible in Gobby — tasks are hard-deleted, not soft-deleted (no `deleted_at` column in the schema). The user explicitly told me to save this rule after I caused the incident.

Architectural direction from the user for Rust clients: daemon/standalone runtime mode must be selected exactly once per process. Auto mode tests whether the daemon is installed, independent of whether it is currently running. An installed daemon selects daemon mode for the process lifetime; stopped or unreachable daemon operations fail in daemon mode and never fall back to standalone. An uninstalled daemon selects standalone for that process. Explicit standalone selection is allowed. Configuration or installation changes take effect only on a new process invocation; environment settings must not bypass or flip an already-selected mode. Test isolation must preserve this production state-machine contract instead of introducing a per-read override.
