Also means live verification of hook-path recall changes requires a real user prompt, not a probe agent.

Headless UI verification recipe for the Gobby web app (worked end-to-end in #17768): (1) Auth — mint a short-lived session by inserting sha256(token) into the Postgres `auth_sessions` table (DSN from ~/.gobby/bootstrap.yaml `database_url`), then set `document.cookie gobby_session=<token>`. (2) Browser — the chrome-devtools MCP drives 'Chrome for Testing' from ~/.cache/puppeteer-browsers/, but its window ops (resize_page, emulate, take_screenshot) hang forever on occluded/minimized windows and wedge the whole MCP queue; recovery is `kill <chrome-devtools-mcp pid>` (gobby respawns it on next call). For screenshots/viewports/color-scheme/reduced-motion use playwright-core (available in web/node_modules — import by absolute path .../playwright-core/index.mjs) launching the same Chrome for Testing binary with headless:true. (3) Data scoping — wiki API calls resolve project scope per request; pin `?project=<id>` via a context.addInitScript fetch wrapper to test against a populated vault. (4) rAF is suspended in occluded windows: any rAF-gated focus/animation code silently does nothing there — this is also why DOM-focus assertions fail live but pass in jsdom (jsdom rAF is setTimeout-backed).

Context-window architecture decision (#18631): Gobby no longer has a generic static model context-window table or sentinel fallback. Resolution precedence is explicit override, provider-reported value, provider-owned catalog, the DB-backed model_metadata registry, then a typed unknown result (value None/source "unknown") with one warning per normalized model. Sessions must pass their concrete HubDatabase and configured override dict into resolution rather than relying on global app context. model_metadata is refreshed from OpenRouter every 24 hours with the common bounded async DB primitive; empty/failed fetches retain cache, writes use one deadline and one transaction, and shutdown cancellation is reaped with a 7-second drain bound. Provider JSON serializes unknown as context_length null/source unknown; frontend accepts only override, provider_reported, provider_catalog, registry, and unknown.

In the code_index subsystem, sync completion and summary persistence must be guarded by the snapshot content_hash: CodeIndexStorage.mark_vectors_synced, mark_graph_synced, and update_symbol_summary only update rows when the current row's content_hash matches the caller's snapshot hash.

On 2026-05-31 during the gobby-cli #354 build dogfood run, coordination task #15432 fixed a half-stopped daemon failure mode: `gobby status` now reports a degraded daemon when a PID exists but `/api/admin/status` is unavailable, and `gobby.mcp_proxy.stdio.DaemonProxy.call_tool` now runs a short HTTP preflight and returns structured `DAEMON_UNAVAILABLE` errors for connection/read timeouts. Commit c25dcf5e0.

Linear sync for Gobby should register tasks under a Linear project named after the Gobby project/repo. Linear issue titles should use the local Gobby task ref prefix (for example `#14277: Title`) while local Gobby task titles remain unprefixed; imports/pulls strip the ref prefix and link existing tasks by seq_num when possible. The current bundled `mcp-linear` server lacks team/project/list_issues/delete tools, so Gobby uses a small Linear GraphQL fallback via the stored `linear_api_key` for discovery, project creation, project-scoped issue create/list/update/delete.

The setup wizard distinguishes persisted in-progress state from finished state with `SetupState.completed_at`: in-progress re-runs enter `Welcome` so its resume/start-fresh choice is reachable, while a non-null initial `completed_at` renders a side-effect-free completion summary. Resuming advances from `completed_step_id`; starting fresh clears that ID before advancing.

Planning skill instructions now direct normal plan-authoring validation to `uv run gobby plans validate <plan-file>` (with optional `--project` when cwd cannot resolve context). `gobby tasks expand validate-plan` is documented only for task-expansion workflows/debugging. The plan-review and plan-adversary instructions also classify `target-coverage`, conservative `table-row-decomposition`, and index-proven `consumer-sweep` as mechanical validator failures rather than qualitative findings.

Dispatcher no-run mutex cleanup must respect lease_until. In #15212, duplicate #12898 build agents were caused by sweep_orphan_no_run_dispatch_mutexes and build resume cleanup deleting dispatcher-owned run_id=NULL mutexes after a 30s updated_at grace even though spawn preflight/worktree+gcode setup can exceed that. The fix in commit 7c50730af preserves live lease_until values and only recovers expired or lease-less stale no-run mutexes.

Native gcode integration tests that generate a temporary GOBBY_HOME and Fernet .secret_kek must point gcode and Python storage at a unique PostgreSQL test schema. Keeping the schema isolated ensures the generated KEK wraps the same schema-local DEK and avoids collisions with secret_key_material rows from the shared database.

Codex transcript-synthesized MCP tool results can arrive as outer envelopes like {content, structuredContent, isError}. Workflow enforcement expects the semantic payload at top-level tool_output, so normalization must unwrap structuredContent (or parse JSON text content) before step routing inspects success/error.
MCP default installer repairs should not overwrite existing args containing $secret: references, and optional-secret SecretStore database handles must be closed after optional arg processing.

Provider design decision for Gobby daemon: generation providers should be capability-based. Any supported CLI provider can participate in text/vision generation when daemon-side adapters exist, and `local` means an OpenAI-compatible HTTP endpoint such as LM Studio, Ollama, or vLLM configured with explicit api_base/model/api_key, aligned with embedding endpoint policy.

Bundled-content integrity verification in src/gobby/sync/integrity.py is complete only when every scoped Git query returns a string. run_git_command returning None after Git repository detection means the integrity check is unavailable (checked=False with an error), which activates the sync CLI's existing block-all fail-closed path; an empty string means the query succeeded with no matching files.

PostgreSQL hub row normalization intentionally serializes psycopg dict/list JSONB values to compact JSON text because storage model decoders consume serialized JSON for both JSONB and text columns. Returning driver-native structures only in PostgresHubDatabase._normalize_value breaks live task, chat, metrics, workflow, and related decoders; changing this boundary requires a coordinated storage-model migration.

Chatterbox voice availability/status probes must remain metadata-only: use the shared _module_is_available/find_spec path and reference-file checks, and defer chatterbox.tts_turbo plus Torch-backed automatic device detection to ChatterboxTurboProvider._ensure_model's asyncio.to_thread loader. /api/voice/status must never synchronously import the Chatterbox/Torch runtime.

Config variable resolution has a two-phase design due to chicken-and-egg: config must load before DB init (to get db_path), but SecretStore needs the DB. Phase 1: expand_env_vars() with env vars only. Phase 2: after DB init in runner.py, reload config with secret_store.get as secret_resolver. Resolution order: secrets store > env vars > default > warn. The expand_env_vars function in config/app.py accepts an optional secret_resolver: Callable[[str], str | None] parameter.

Bundled Rust skill upgrade (#15758): Rust should use seven reference files by judgment: configuration, ownership, types, error-handling, testing, async, and performance. The configuration reference is required because Cargo workspace/package boundaries, feature flags, rust-toolchain/MSRV, rustfmt/clippy policy, and .cargo/config.toml materially affect safe Rust edits. The Rust discovery rule should trigger on .rs plus precise Rust project/config files: Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, rust-toolchain, rust-toolchain.toml, rustfmt.toml, .rustfmt.toml, clippy.toml, .clippy.toml, .cargo/config, and .cargo/config.toml; avoid broad TOML matching.

After changing ~/.gobby/config.yaml (e.g., switching memory backend), the gobby daemon must be restarted with 'uv run gobby restart' to pick up the new configuration. Config changes are not hot-reloaded.

In gobby-cli/gwiki, shared-code Falkor enrichment limits are configured by gwiki.shared_code.call_edge_limit and gwiki.shared_code.import_edge_limit. Defaults are 200, resolved from config_store before ~/.gobby/gcore.yaml with no env or CLI override, and queries use a limit+1 sentinel to report truncation components like code_call_edges>{limit} and code_import_edges>{limit}.

Digest title ownership policy: non-empty session titles with title_source="native" are authoritative for digest synthesis and should not be replaced by LLM title candidates. Native transcript ingestion may still replace empty, provisional, heuristic, or prior native titles; manual and LLM-owned titles remain protected from native ingestion.

Gobby logging boundary after task #13910: `logging.dir/runtime.log` is the single append-only sink for raw daemon stdout/stderr across direct launch, launchd, systemd, and Windows. Direct launch passes one shared file handle to both Popen streams. Python logging handlers must never target runtime.log; rotating application logs such as gobby.log and gobby-error.log remain separate. `forward_subprocess_stderr()` sends captured gcode/gwiki diagnostics to daemon stderr once, and the gcode gateway must not force `--quiet`, preserving JSON on stdout.

Gobby task expansion validation deliberately rejects compiled leaf tasks where category='planning' and task_type='task', while the manual category remains valid for direct user-created CRUD tasks. Regression coverage lives in tests/tasks/test_expansion.py around compiled-spec planning leaf rejection.

Gobby's built-in validation command detection must recognize `playwright test` under the JavaScript/TypeScript test matcher. Without that matcher, a passing Playwright gate lacks trusted exit-code correlation and task completion can be blocked even when the browser suite passes.

Post-0.5.0 monetization/client-server direction, SETTLED 2026-07-22 (extends the epic #17425 strategy memory; plan file /Users/josh/.claude/plans/just-thinking-about-the-federated-fox.md). Architecture: control plane vs data plane, NOT hosted daemon — the daemon stays on the user's machine (single-filesystem: hooks processed server-side, daemon reads client transcripts/repos off its own disk); gobby.ai hosts a closed-source control plane (accounts, per-user API keys, entitlements, multi-machine sync, teams, fleet, mobile relay). Business model: SOLO FREE, CONNECTED PAID — everything single-user/single-machine free forever; paid is the multi-* layer. Positioning comp: OpenHands (sell the platform layer, not the agent). Self-hosting the control plane: free Docker image, never policed; the paywall holds because Pro entitlements are Ed25519-signed tokens only gobby.ai can mint, verified offline inside closed-source Rust binaries that CONTAIN the paid capabilities (distributed via existing ~/.gobby/bin/ channel; a closed checker gating open code is decorative). Hosted-daemon SaaS explicitly rejected as a first move. LICENSE: relicensed from Apache-2.0 to FSL-1.1-ALv2 (Functional Source License 1.1, auto-converts to Apache 2.0 per release after 2 years) in task #18706 while Josh was still sole author; licensor 'Josh Wilhelmi'; pyproject uses 'LicenseRef-FSL-1.1-ALv2' because packaging 25.0's SPDX snapshot lacks the id, crates use bare 'FSL-1.1-ALv2' (cargo accepts); GitHub's licensee does NOT detect FSL (shows 'Other' — same for Sentry), badges carry the message; already-published Apache versions (e.g. gobby-code on crates.io) remain Apache. External contributions now require a CLA (stated in CONTRIBUTING.md; tooling not yet wired). Deferred future epics in rough order: users/accounts table backing machines.owner_user_id + per-user API keys; daemon-to-control-plane link (machine registration, entitlement fetch); sync; teams; fleet; mobile relay. Do not say 'open source' unqualified — Gobby is Fair Source.

gobby-cli #838 fixed Rust duplicate type symbols from tree-sitter `impl_item` captures. Parser flow now runs `collapse_rust_impl_symbols` after `link_parents` and before call extraction: Rust impl captures are treated as transient parents, child methods are reparented to the same-file canonical struct/enum/trait/type symbol with `Type::method` qualified names, and impl pseudo-symbols are removed before indexing/call resolution. Coverage: parser test `rust_impl_blocks_do_not_emit_duplicate_type_symbols_and_parent_methods` and graph_standalone Rust tuple-struct construction test `index_resolves_cross_file_rust_tuple_struct_construction`.
PUT /api/rules/bulk-toggle preserves the existing status/count response fields and also reports per-rule update failures in a failures list plus partial=true when any matching rule failed to update.

Adding a gwiki CLI contract command is a 7-place update: (1) crates/gwiki/src/contract.rs entry + contract_version bump, (2) pinned crates/gwiki/contract/gwiki.contract.json (regenerate via `cargo run -p gobby-wiki --bin gwiki -- contract --format json`), (3) vendored tests/contracts/gwiki.contract.json (byte-identical copy), (4) version asserts in crates/gwiki/tests/cli_contract.rs and tests/test_cli_contracts.py, (5) docs/contracts/gwiki-cli.md changelog, (6) a handler arm in gcode's resolve_gwiki_handler map (crates/gcode/src/commands/codewiki/build_parts/features.rs) or `cargo test -p gobby-code --lib features` fails, (7) release rebuild + reinstall of ~/.gobby/bin/gwiki. The gcode contract has the same pinned (crates/gcode/contract/) + vendored (tests/contracts/) dual-copy rule. Missed step 6 shipped twice (#17752 pages, my #17753 first attempt caught by session #7921); missed vendored sync shipped in c92e52613 (#17810). Contract command names with spaces (e.g. "page write") denote nested subcommands.

In Gobby's agent live-activity overlay, `AgentRun.parent_session_id` is typed as `str` while `child_session_id` is optional. Protocols that model `AgentRun` should expose session IDs as read-only `@property` members and keep `tool_calls_count`/`turns_used` as mutable `int` fields; otherwise strict mypy treats `AgentRun` as incompatible and may infer `overlay_live_activity` as returning `None`. Use overloads for `overlay_live_activity(run, transcript_reader)` so non-null callers get a non-null run back.

Verification evidence has concurrent writers: MCP record_verification_evidence and hook validation observers. To prevent lost evidence, both paths must use SessionVariableManager.append_to_bounded_list_variable so the bounded append and verification_evidence_recorded update share one immediate database transaction; making only the MCP tool atomic still permits a stale hook merge to overwrite it.

JSONL sync architecture: All task/memory sync rules are now in workflows/rules/sync/ tagged with 'sync'. Agent definitions use rule_selectors with exclude: ['tag:sync'] to prevent JSONL contamination in worktrees. Git hooks (pre-commit, post-commit, post-merge, post-checkout) also skip sync when GOBBY_AGENT_RUN_ID env var is set. Six redundant session-level sync rules were removed (commits 9e62a45 & 38a0d29), leaving only commit-hook-triggered exports.

In Gobby sandbox docs, distinguish Gemini/Qwen spawned-agent sandboxing from ACP web-chat startup: spawned Gemini/Qwen sessions use `-s` with `SEATBELT_PROFILE`, while Gemini/Qwen ACP web-chat backends receive the daemon sandbox config but start without full-process Seatbelt flags because those flags blocked ACP startup on macOS. See `src/gobby/servers/websocket/chat/backends/acp.py` and `docs/guides/sandbox-compatibility.md`.

Web chat managed backend sessions should let asyncio cancellation and programming exceptions propagate to ChatStreamingMixin._stream_chat_response, which emits interrupted=True for cancellation and classifies ordinary failures as chat_error. Backend-local recovery should catch only expected operational failures; async-generator cleanup should suppress Exception rather than BaseException so cancellation propagates.

GET /api/tasks stage filtering is implemented through LocalTaskManager.list_tasks/count_tasks SQL EXISTS filters (`stages` plus `stage_state`), so SQL applies pagination and the count query mirrors all active list filters.

Integration research (2026-07-24): current Open Interpreter supports native stdio MCP via `interpreter mcp-server`, exposing session start/continue tools (`codex`, `codex-reply`) for coding-agent delegation; it does not expose raw desktop screenshot/click controls through that MCP surface. UI-TARS Desktop's visual computer-use engine is available through `@ui-tars/sdk` plus `@ui-tars/operator-nut-js`; its monorepo ships separate MCP servers for browser, commands, filesystem, and search, while the desktop GUI operator itself has no official MCP server. For Gobby, Open Interpreter is config-only; UI-TARS needs a thin stdio MCP adapter. Gobby already has Playwright and Chrome DevTools MCP servers configured, so UI-TARS is valuable specifically for arbitrary desktop GUI apps.

Project convention from Josh: do not add legacy compatibility paths or fallbacks in Gobby. Current pre-0.5.0 work should use the active contract directly; CodeRabbit suggestions that add legacy behavior should be rejected unless the user explicitly asks otherwise.

ProjectsPage reuses activity FilesTab with layout='responsive-split'. Shared ResizeHandle supports horizontalAnchor defaulting to 'right'; FilesTab desktop split passes horizontalAnchor='left' so dragging right and ArrowRight expand the left file tree pane without changing existing right-anchored panels.

In the web chat UI, sessionRef has two sources: (1) chat.sessionRef from useChat, set only via WebSocket events (session_info or chat_stream done chunk), which can be null before the first message exchange; (2) GobbySession.seq_num from useSessions, available as soon as sessions are fetched from the API. When displaying session identity (e.g. #42), always fall back to seq_num from the sessions list when chat.sessionRef is null. The GobbySession.ref field is a short UUID prefix, NOT the #N format.

Unified CLI Launcher v3 architectural decisions (unified-cli-launcher.md):

1. Source identity redesign: `source` = bare provider only (claude, gemini, codex). New `session_type` column (terminal, web_chat) replaces the *_web_chat/*_sdk source suffixes. _normalize_provider() deleted entirely — source IS the provider.

2. Provider purge: Cursor, Windsurf, Copilot, and Antigravity removed in Phase 0. Only claude/gemini/codex survive.

3. Web chat = universal session viewer/controller: Any session (terminal or web-initiated) can be swapped into the web chat window from the activity panel. Sessions are durable processes — they continue running when switched away, recover via CLI resume (--resume/--session-id) on daemon crash, with transcript/summary_markdown as fallback.

4. Canonical identifiers: sessions.id (UUID) is server-side canonical. conversation_id is client-side WebSocket correlation. external_id is CLI-native for resume/transcript.

5. Codex review fixes: child session pre-creation stays (agent_run_id, depth, env vars depend on it); only CLI-native ID preflight capture dies. pending_approvals table generalizes pending_plan_path. Agent definitions get session_types field alongside sources.

Auto-heal progressive discovery rules: The 3 blocking rules (require-servers-listed, require-server-listed-for-schema, require-schema-before-call) were converted to auto-healing rules. Key design: RuleEffect has inject_result and block_on_failure fields for mcp_call effects. HookManager._dispatch_mcp_calls returns captured results. _proxy server name routes to ToolProxyService methods (list_servers, list_tools, get_tool_schema) directly, bypassing call_tool dispatch which only routes to sub-servers. _evaluate_workflow_rules processes results: inject_result adds context for the agent, block_on_failure stops the chain and blocks if a prerequisite fails. Tracking rules (track-servers-listed, track-listed-servers, track-schema-lookup) remain unchanged and coexist with auto-heal.

For task #17062, daemon one-shot Codex text generation now reuses a daemon-owned TextGenerationService. GobbyRunner and ServiceContainer carry text_generation_service, runner.codex_client is late-bound into build_daemon_text_generation_service via codex_client_provider, and /api/llm/generate reads server.services.text_generation_service instead of constructing a per-request service. CodexAppServerTextGenerateAdapter borrows the shared connected app-server client without start/stop, archives one-shot threads best-effort, and falls back once to an owned client when no connected shared client is available or the borrowed client loses connection.

Wrapper timeout clamping remains relevant to genuinely blocking WAIT_TOOL_NAMES such as wait_for_output and wait_for_summary. Task #18604 / commit a6b6bede5 made the wait_for_agent MCP handler immediate subscribe-and-return, so callers no longer pass a timeout or rely on wrapper ceilings for that tool; transport classification cleanup is tracked separately in the event-driven wait epic.

Postgres hub cutover convention: runtime CLI and daemon setup paths should open hub storage through gobby.storage.hub.runtime.open_runtime_hub_database/runtime_hub_database and SecretStore/ConfigStore on the HubDatabase protocol. LocalDatabase is legacy SQLite support and should remain off runtime paths except explicit migrate-from-sqlite/import compatibility.

Gobby's split between logical project identity and code-index identity:

- LOGICAL project identity is parent-scoped. Tasks, workflows, approvals, and memory route via parent_project_path / parent_project_id (and the .gobby/project.json `id` field, which in isolated roots equals the parent's id by design).
- CODE-INDEX identity (gcode's `project_id` for code_symbols / code_indexed_files / code_content_chunks rows) is filesystem-root-scoped for isolated roots. gcode resolves it as UUID5(CODE_INDEX_UUID_NAMESPACE 'c0de1de0-0000-4000-8000-000000000000', canonical_root_path).

An 'isolated root' is a Gobby clone (agents/isolation.py) or a Gobby worktree (mcp_proxy/tools/worktrees/_create.py). Both flow through ensure_project_json_for_isolation in src/gobby/utils/project_context.py, which copies the parent's .gobby/project.json verbatim and adds parent_project_path (and, after this change, parent_project_id).

Git detection alone cannot distinguish a clone from a main repo — clones have their own .git directory and look identical to a main checkout. The reliable isolation signal for gcode is the parent_project_path / parent_project_id marker in .gobby/project.json. Git linked-worktree detection (canonical(git_dir) != canonical(git_common_dir)) is a fallback for non-Gobby-created worktrees.

Branch switches inside one root keep the same code-index id (root path unchanged); gcode's lazy freshness + orphan sweep handle content drift. Different roots get different ids automatically.
Gobby has fully migrated to PostgreSQL; runtime and test code should treat SQLite usage as stale unless it is historical migration/documentation compatibility.

Handoff tools consolidation (commit 91b58384): 6 MCP tools consolidated to 2 on gobby-sessions.

Old tools (removed): generate_handoff, extract_handoff_context, create_handoff, pickup.
New tools: set_handoff_context, get_handoff_context.

set_handoff_context has two modes:
1. Agent-authored fast path: pass `content` param → writes summary_markdown, sets handoff_ready, optionally sends P2P via `to_session`
2. Automated fallback: omit content → TranscriptAnalyzer (compact=True) and/or LLM (full=True)

get_handoff_context merges old get + pickup: finds by session_id, project_id/source, or most recent handoff_ready. Prefers summary_markdown over compact_markdown. Supports link_child_session_id.

Workflow action handlers (generate_handoff, extract_handoff_context in workflows/actions.py) are SEPARATE from MCP tools and were NOT changed.

Key files: _handoff.py, _factory.py, _actions.py, registries.py, 3 YAML rule templates.

Gobby daemon local generation endpoint config supports ai.generation.local.endpoints.<name>.provider with values openai-compatible, lmstudio, and ollama. The default is openai-compatible. provider=lmstudio uses LM Studio native /api/v1 chat/model endpoints; provider=ollama uses Ollama native /api/chat and /api/ps with keep_alive model lifecycle; generic OpenAI-compatible endpoints use the OpenAI SDK path. Gobby install/setup does not manage a local-generation launcher helper.

Task escalation is now represented by the first-class `tasks.is_escalated` column in the Phase 5 task-state migration. `Task.from_row` reads that column into `Task.is_escalated`, `state_semantics` projections should read the dataclass flag instead of inferring from `escalated_at` or legacy `status`, and storage transition guards should test `task.is_escalated` directly while legacy helper names remain compatibility aliases until their removal phase.

Communications inbound dedup contract: InboundCommunications.handle_messages checks (channel_name, platform_message_id) before identity resolution and storage. Duplicate envelopes remain in the returned handled list so PollingManager acknowledges the current delivery, while storage and comms.message_received fan-out occur only for newly persisted messages. Adapter-owned durable config uses BaseChannelAdapter.set_config_update_callback; lifecycle merges patches into the live ChannelConfig and persists through LocalCommunicationsStore. Telegram restores config_json.poll_offset during initialize and checkpoints every contiguous offset advance. Implemented in task #17890, commit 6847dc2bf.

Gobby session registration should never return synthetic platform session IDs after persistence failures. Commit 778557ad6 (#15050) made SessionManager.register_session recover an existing canonical persisted session by external_id/source/project when possible, and otherwise return no platform id so hooks do not inject stale wrapper IDs. Session-start only stores _platform_session_id when truthy, and session responses omit the Gobby Session ID banner without a real session.

Task #15174 simplified completion gates: verification-before-completion was removed as a bundled skill/rule dependency, task-transitions is now the canonical completion/readiness skill, and lifecycle readiness is derived with completion_evidence_ready(variables). Successful validation evidence after the last reset satisfies readiness; failed validation_command evidence blocks until a later validation_command succeeds; manual evidence can satisfy readiness only when no failed validation command is pending. The errors_resolved session variable contract and require-error-triage-before-status rule are retired.

Before Gobby 0.5.0, the supported production daemon topology is a local Docker Compose stack containing PostgreSQL, Qdrant, and FalkorDB. `gobby start` uses a two-phase Compose boot: start and health-wait PostgreSQL first so hub-backed Qdrant/FalkorDB configuration can be read, then start all three profiles with detached mode, orphan cleanup, and Compose health waiting. The runner independently gates HTTP binding on PostgreSQL SELECT 1, Qdrant health, and authenticated FalkorDB PING. Qdrant/FalkorDB degradation after startup remains nonfatal and is exposed through health/status rather than a shutdown monitor. Bootstrap database URLs must target localhost or another loopback address.

ConfigStore owns the config_store.is_secret invariant: set() and set_many() derive it from canonical $secret:<natural_name> references and include it in both insert and conflict-update paths. Import/template code with external secret-marker metadata must call ConfigStore.mark_secret_keys() using canonical storage keys instead of issuing route-local SQL.

In gobby-cli gcode, DSN-gated PostgreSQL tests should use the #618/#714 pattern: `crates/gcode/build.rs` emits `cfg(gcode_postgres_tests)` when `GCODE_POSTGRES_TEST_DATABASE_URL` is present, and each PG-backed test has `#[cfg_attr(not(gcode_postgres_tests), ignore = "requires GCODE_POSTGRES_TEST_DATABASE_URL")]`. When an ignored PG test is explicitly run, its DSN/connect/schema helper should fail loudly with `expect`, not silently `return`. For nextest serialization, every PG-backed gcode test should live under a `serial_db` module path so `.config/nextest.toml`'s `test(::serial_db::) | test(serial_db::)` filter catches it.

In gobby-cli gcode, DSN-gated PostgreSQL tests should use the #618/#714 pattern: `crates/gcode/build.rs` emits `cfg(gcode_postgres_tests)` when `GCODE_POSTGRES_TEST_DATABASE_URL` is present, and each PG-backed test has `#[cfg_attr(not(gcode_postgres_tests), ignore = "requires GCODE_POSTGRES_TEST_DATABASE_URL")]`. When an ignored PG test is explicitly run, its DSN/connect/schema helper should fail loudly with `expect`, not silently `return`. For nextest serialization, every PG-backed gcode test should live under a `serial_db` module path so `.config/nextest.toml`'s `test(::serial_db::) | test(serial_db::)` filter catches it.

Communications HTTP/CLI contract: GET /api/comms/channels returns a bare JSON list, so comms status, channels list, and channels remove must consume response.json() directly. POST /api/comms/send accepts channel_name/content plus optional session_id and metadata, forwards all four to CommunicationsManager.send_message, and serializes the returned CommsMessage including id/status. Completed in task #17892, commit c9e808e9d.

In gobby web, task #17027 removed the legacy Workflows Agents sub-tab and deleted the workflows/AgentsTab.* family/tests. Agent configuration and actions now live under the Activity Agents tab introduced by #17026; future agent UI changes should target web/src/components/activity/AgentsTab.* rather than workflows/AgentsTab.
In the Gobby repo, the retired local-launcher and shell-output compressor helper integrations have been removed. Do not preserve or reintroduce their installer/status/rule/UI references.

Gobby dispatcher tests: run_heartbeat is serialized by a module-level asyncio.Lock, so concurrency tests should run competing run_heartbeat calls in the same event loop. Running them via separate asyncio.run() calls in worker threads can hang because asyncio.Lock is not a cross-thread synchronization primitive.

Task #17228 decomposed src/gobby/config/app.py by extracting config loading helpers into src/gobby/config/_loading.py. app.py remains the public facade for load_config, load_yaml, apply_cli_overrides, deep_merge, expand_env_vars, and export_config_to_yaml via imports and __all__. Environment-expansion warning tests should patch gobby.config._loading.logger because the helper implementation now lives there.

Codex app-server v2 uses the `effort` field on `turn/start` for per-turn reasoning overrides. The Codex CLI/config knob remains `model_reasoning_effort` (and `plan_mode_reasoning_effort`) for config-level defaults; web-chat turn requests should not send `reasoningEffort`.

consecutive-tool-block in rule_engine.py treated ALL MCP calls as the same tool because it compared event.data.tool_name which is always 'mcp__gobby__call_tool'. FIXED in commit dfe71d70: _get_tool_identity() helper extracts 'server:tool' from tool_input for MCP calls. Also resets consecutive-tool-block counters on step transitions (in _process_step_after_tool) so failures from implement don't bleed into terminate.

SO_REUSEADDR port collision root cause: When find_free_port() uses SO_REUSEADDR, the OS can assign a port (e.g. 60887) to localhost even if production daemon is bound on 0.0.0.0:60887 — they're treated as non-conflicting addresses. The verification bind also passes with SO_REUSEADDR. Fix: remove SO_REUSEADDR from both sockets and add a 0.0.0.0 verification bind. Also exclude known gobby ports (60887/60888) as defense-in-depth. File: tests/e2e/conftest.py:find_free_port().

As of #16111 / commit e1654902594c0c4bbef6a16f6a195e9967968524, operator-supplied endpoint/base URL config fields share src/gobby/config/url_validation.py. HTTP endpoints require http/https plus an explicit host and valid port; MCP websocket transport uses the same validator with ws/wss. Optional URL fields preserve None, and CommunicationsConfig preserves an empty webhook_base_url as its explicit unset sentinel.

In WorkflowHookHandler._run_observers, context compact guidance must run on the semantic turn-start branch after detect_plan_mode_from_context. This ordering lets detect_context_compact_guidance suppress nudges for plan-mode turns, while populating context_compact_guidance_message before the enabled nudge-compact-on-context-pressure rule evaluates.

Epic #13175 Docs/A1/A10 added Plan-Coverage Contract documentation surfaces in commit 5d33b101a: CLAUDE.md, docs/contracts/plan-coverage.md, plan/plan-draft/plan-review/expand skills, planner/plan-adversary/expansion-qa agent prompts, and focused docs/skill/workflow tests. The contract pins the canonical plan heading regex, kind enum, acceptance item shape, typed deferral object, structured covers labels, bootstrap ledger, .grandfathered rules, CLI synopsis, evidence kinds, and table-row decomposition rule.

SystemAutomationLoop project-dispatch shutdown safety after #16389: schedule_project_dispatch rejects requests while _running is false, and _schedule_project_dispatch_on_loop repeats the same guard because stop() can run after call_soon_threadsafe enqueues the callback but before that callback executes. Both boundaries are required to prevent post-stop asyncio tasks and DB dispatch work. Covered by commit 6603de092412e5561a8cf7fcab74a3c36ba54b45.

In gobby-cli/gwiki, session transcript file ingest starts at `SourceKind::Session` (`session`) and `.jsonl` detection in `crates/gwiki/src/ingest/file/source.rs`. File dispatch routes this to `crates/gwiki/src/ingest/session.rs`, which unwraps JSONL archive envelopes shaped `{type,timestamp,payload}`, dispatches through the `SessionTranscriptAdapter` trait, supports a generic fixture/common adapter for `session` / `gobby.session` / `gobby.session.v1`, registers the original bytes as a source manifest entry with `SourceKind::Session`, and writes derived raw markdown with session metadata via `write_raw_markdown`. Future CLI-specific transcript adapters should extend the adapter list rather than changing `.jsonl` routing.

As of task #18344 / commit 36d8907b1, web-chat plan approval expiry is an explicit terminal turn outcome. Native ExitPlanMode and managed Droid ExitSpecMode use the distinct decision "timeout", clear pending backend plan state, broadcast mode_changed with reason "plan_approval_timed_out" so the frontend dismisses the card, and invoke the session's provider-specific interrupt. Managed cancel_pending_approval also releases _pending_plan_event, and native interrupt releases all pending interactions.

In Gobby, cancelling or stopping an active build reviewer/worker must wake the build dispatcher after terminal cleanup releases runtime state. Commit 4fe490169 (#15161) added schedule_dispatcher_tick_for_project/task in gobby.build.dispatch_tick, delegates MCP task handoff ticks through that shared scheduler, and calls schedule_dispatcher_tick_for_task from AgentCleanupHandler.terminalize_cancelled_run after post_terminal_cleanup. Regression coverage is tests/e2e/test_build_dispatcher_autonomy.py::test_cancelled_reviewer_wakes_dispatcher_for_replacement_without_build_resume.

Codewiki module dependency diagrams are deterministic graph projections: roll up both Import and Call edges to module nodes, canonicalize with BTreeSet before two-hop BFS and the 20-edge cap, gate the fence with is_valid_mermaid, and record one ModuleDependency DiagramOutcome per module page. Graph edges intentionally stay outside module reuse keys. RENDER_VERSION_MODULE remains 20 until the call-sequence renderer lands, when both sections will advance together.

TerminalView's safe @wterm/dom integration contract: load a fresh Ghostty core per TerminalView attempt, render WTerm in a fresh child mount node, and destroy synchronously in useLayoutEffect cleanup even while init() is pending. The detached per-instance node contains @wterm/dom's possible late internal destroy so it cannot erase a StrictMode successor. Guard every init/onData/onResize continuation with disposed state, disable/untab/blur WTerm's textarea after init for a display-only surface, transpose onResize(cols, rows) to rows/cols behind a cancelable 200 ms debounce, and forward onData only as VT protocol responses. Commit a4d09e37e implements this in web/src/components/activity/terminal/TerminalView.tsx.

Gobby's MCP delete_clone tool deletes clone files before deleting the clone storage row. If filesystem deletion fails, the original clone row is left untouched so the clone_id and task/artifact references remain resolvable; it no longer deletes the row and recreates it with a fresh ID.

Workflows v2 architecture: Rules replace lifecycle workflows with 4 primitive effect types: block (reason), set_variable (variable+value), inject_context (template), mcp_call (server+tool+arguments). No execute_action, no observe. All hardcoded ActionExecutor actions decompose into these primitives. MCP tools ARE the plugin/extension mechanism — plugin system (hooks/plugins.py, 829 lines) removed entirely. Plan at docs/plans/workflows-v2.md, task #8795.

In gobby-cli, SQLite is retired as a runtime store. PostgreSQL/pg_search is the runtime persistence and keyword search backend across the repo (per the hub PostgreSQL architecture); gcode should not retain SQLite as a runtime store, and SQLite remains only for one-shot migration/import tooling (e.g. gobby postgres migrate-from-sqlite).

Gobby canonical context pressure now uses session snapshot fields `context_used_tokens` and `context_usage_ratio` with `context_window`; cumulative `usage_*` fields remain historical/cost counters. Web chat context-usage helpers live in `web/src/hooks/useChat/contextUsage.ts` and are re-exported from `useChat/core.ts` to keep core under the 1,000-line source limit.

Gobby task state buckets are now persisted in tasks.state_bucket via migration 244 and baseline schema triggers. Hub/admin aggregate queries should use tasks.state_bucket instead of recomputing the stage CASE join; triggers on tasks closed/escalated fields and task_stage_states state/position keep it current.

In gobby-cli, code graph read behavior is split with `crates/gcode/src/graph/code_graph/read.rs` as a thin facade. Child modules live under `crates/gcode/src/graph/code_graph/read/`: `support.rs` contains shared Cypher fragments, graph result row mapping, clamping, count extraction, and blast-row dedupe; `relationship_queries.rs` contains caller/usage/import/blast Cypher query builders; `payload_queries.rs` contains graph payload Cypher query builders for project/file/symbol/blast views; `graph_payloads.rs` builds `GraphPayload` values for project overview, file graph, symbol neighbors, and blast radius; `relationships.rs` exposes count/find/import/blast read APIs returning `GraphResult` lists or IDs. The parent `code_graph.rs` still re-exports the public read API and imports three test-only query helpers through the facade.

Gobby agent failed-run recovery: before releasing task ownership or rolling back a stage for a terminal agent run, recovery must verify the process/tmux session is dead, take over the run-linked task_dispatch_mutex with holder 'recovery', call stage_states.fail_stage with by_session_id='recovery', then reacquire the recovery mutex before release_task_claim because fail_stage releases its own RuntimeDispatchMutex context.

In Gobby workflow_definitions, source values 'installed' and 'template' are Gobby-owned definitions. Source values like 'custom' and 'project' represent user/project-authored definitions, so template refresh or reinstall flows should preserve them unless explicitly operating on user-owned content.

Memory search scoring policy: `similarity` is semantic confidence only (raw semantic score after source boost and temporal decay), while `ranking_score` is the hybrid retrieval rank used for ordering across semantic, graph, and FTS results. Hook-based auto recall uses `min_score=0.7`; manual memory search applies no default `min_score` and only filters when the caller explicitly passes one.

Plan coverage source separation: `--task-tree db` must read task data from PostgreSQL/LocalTaskManager, not `.gobby/tasks.jsonl`; CI revalidation should use `--task-tree matrix-file`; JSONL is export/sync material and only explicit jsonl mode should read JSONL.

In gobby-cli, gwiki local file ingest is split so crates/gwiki/src/ingest/file.rs stays the facade for StdinSnapshot, LocalFileIngestResult, ingest_path, ingest_path_without_index re-export, ingest_stdin, and the TEXT_INLINE_LIMIT_BYTES policy. Local kind dispatch lives in crates/gwiki/src/ingest/file/dispatch.rs; generic borrowed-file ingest in generic.rs; raw markdown rendering in render.rs; replay metadata updates in replay.rs; source-kind classification, source locations, asset threshold checks, and source-file reads in source.rs; degradation summary formatting in degradation.rs; behavior tests in tests.rs. Keep future file-ingest behavior tests in ingest/file/tests.rs and keep helper visibility pub(super) only where sibling modules or tests need it.

The web/ directory now has two TypeScript projects: (1) the Vite web UI (tsconfig.json, includes src/ but excludes src/setup/) and (2) the Ink setup wizard (tsconfig.setup.json, includes only src/setup/ with Node types instead of DOM). The main tsconfig.json has `"exclude": ["src/setup"]` to prevent DOM type conflicts. Build commands: `npm run build` for web UI, `npm run build:setup` for setup wizard. Dev: `npm run setup` runs the wizard via tsx.

Trust prompt detector (src/gobby/agents/prompt_detector.py): TRUST_DISMISS_KEYS must be '\n' (Enter only), NOT '2\n'. Option 2 is 'Trust parent Folder' which trusts the parent directory — dangerous when parallel dev pipelines use sibling clones. TRUST_PROMPT_PATTERNS has 3 patterns: 'Do you trust the files' (old Claude), 'Is this a project you created or one you trust' (new Claude), and 'Trust.*Folder'. Lifecycle monitor (check_trust_prompts) uses these to auto-dismiss within 30s.

SafeExpressionEvaluator.evaluate() in src/gobby/workflows/lifecycle_evaluator.py explicitly wraps results in bool() (line ~81: return bool(self.visit(tree.body))). Test assertions should use `is True`/`is False`, not `== ""`/`== "abc"`. CodeRabbit incorrectly flagged these assertions — they are correct as-is.

tmux set-titles-string gotcha: When enabling `set-titles on` globally, tmux uses the default `set-titles-string` which is `#S:#I:#W - "#T" #{session_alerts}`. This prepends session name and window index to the title (e.g. `8:1:My Title`). Must explicitly set `set-titles-string "#W"` to get just the window name. The _rename_tmux_window function in summary_actions.py had this bug for user sessions (agent_depth 0) while TmuxSessionManager.rename_window already had the correct behavior for spawned agents.

Unified Filter Button for Workflows Page: Consolidated filter row (search, source dropdown, hide built-in toggle) and per-tab chip bars into a single Filter button with popover in WorkflowsPage.tsx. Tab-specific filter state (pipelineEnabledFilter, agentProviderFilter, ruleEventFilter) is lifted to WorkflowsPage and passed as props. Dynamic options (agentProviders, ruleEventTypes) are reported by tabs via callbacks. Bulk actions (Install All, Enable All) moved to toolbar-right. FilterPopover is a local component in WorkflowsPage.tsx with Source chips, tab-specific section, and Hide Built-in toggle. Click-outside closes popover. Badge shows active filter count. CSS uses .workflows-filter-btn, .workflows-filter-badge, .workflows-filter-popover classes. Old .workflows-source-select CSS removed.

Codex should use the same dedicated scratch-planning apparatus as Claude for large Gobby review/fix batches: write concise, decision-complete scratch plans under .gobby/plans/ after the required task is claimed. Plans must be execution artifacts only: no open questions, options, or stream-of-consciousness reasoning.

Bug fix: storage.get_memory() raises ValueError for missing memories, but manager.py search paths (lines 541, 571) and crossref lookup (line 899) expected it to return None. Fixed by wrapping calls in try/except ValueError to gracefully skip deleted/missing memories referenced by stale search indices.

Step and pipeline workflows do not replace lifecycle workflows: they run concurrently. The primary difference between the workflow types is that you can have multiple lifecycle workflows running in a session but only one step or one pipeline workflow active at a time in a session.

FilesTab renders root-level file tree entries from rootEntries, while nested directories render from childrenMap. Its loadChildren callback treats the empty path as the root and updates rootEntries, allowing delete, rename, move, and duplicate handlers to share the same post-mutation refresh path.

In Gobby, normal SessionStart startup-context idempotency is owned by the shared _session_start context classifier. It should call SessionVariableManager.claim_startup_context(session_id) as soon as a durable session_id exists, including freshly registered sessions, so duplicate startup events get full default agent role/personality context only once. Explicit context-loss starts such as clear/compact and resume with pending_context_reset intentionally bypass the claim and replay full context.

Validation-command detection is centered in src/gobby/config/validation_detection.py and consumed by src/gobby/workflows/observer_verification.py. Summary-preserving pipelines can still be classified and tagged with validation_summary.pytest|ruff|mypy, but unified command correlation deliberately treats textual-summary provenance as unknown. Completion now requires a trusted terminal machine outcome correlated to the exact command; contradictory summaries, nonterminal results, unstructured output, and provenance-free results remain unknown.

send_keys and capture_output MCP tools live on gobby-sessions (not gobby-agents), targeting by session_id. Session→tmux resolution: agent sessions via LocalAgentRunManager.get_by_session() → tmux_session_name; interactive CLI sessions via Session.terminal_context. TmuxSessionManager has a `literal` parameter: literal=True for text input, literal=False for tmux key names (C-c, Escape, etc.).

For structured stage-native plan-review rejection, use StageReviewRejectionMutation at advisory-lock priority 290 outside the dispatch mutex (300) and plan-review evidence mutation (475). This makes stage transition, description projection, round_result, and evidence finalization atomic without lock inversion. Round uniqueness indexes exclude expired plan_review_evidence rows, preserving failed-spawn audit rows while allowing same-round re-preparation.

Dependency decision: the voice extra relies on [tool.uv].override-dependencies to force gradio>=6.14.0, overriding chatterbox-tts==0.1.7's gradio==6.8.0 pin, while preserving the Starlette >=1.0.1 floor. Without the override, chatterbox-tts==0.1.7 is unsatisfiable given the starlette>=1.0.1 requirement.

In gwiki session ingest, deterministic session frontmatter metadata is carried through ParsedSessionMetadata plus ParsedSessionMessage.tool_names. render_session_markdown emits model, tool_counts, token_totals, duration_seconds, hour_buckets, is_subagent, and gitBranch via MetadataValue bool/json support. Claude Code token usage is de-duplicated by message.id before summing; Codex token_totals uses the latest cumulative event_msg.payload.info.total_token_usage, with model from turn_context.model and branch from session_meta.git.branch.

gcore `StandaloneConfig::from_yaml_str` derives default `ai.text_generate.*` LM Studio direct routing settings for non-empty standalone `gcore.yaml` files when no explicit text-generation routing/base/model keys are present, and copies `ai.embeddings.api_key` into the derived text-generation API key. Explicit `ai.text_generate.*` YAML values are preserved.

Codex app-server commandExecution item/completed outcomes are normalized in src/gobby/adapters/codex_impl/item_normalization.py before shared tool normalization: aggregatedOutput, exitCode, and status become a structured tool_response/tool_output contract consumed by direct AFTER_TOOL observers and web-chat post-tool lifecycle handling. Live Codex CLI 0.144.5 evidence captured on 2026-07-17 proved exitCode=0/status=completed for success and exitCode=7/status=failed for nonzero execution; the sanitized fixture is tests/fixtures/provider_contracts/codex/command-execution-items.json. ACPHookAdapter.normalize_tool_name must consult the concrete provider's TOOL_MAP before normalize_acp_tool_name so provider-only aliases such as Grok run_terminal_command remain canonical Bash after shared ACP extraction. Validation detection treats jq as evidence only for explicit jq empty, jq -e, or jq --exit-status prefixes; plain jq selectors remain read-only and produce no readiness evidence.

Task #16065 established workflow rule/variable template sync ownership semantics: orphan cleanup runs only after a nonempty, error-free authoritative scan; a single non-gobby root is partial and cannot prune; project and global user roots are passed together as one authoritative namespace. Sync-managed installed rows are restored when their template reappears. Implemented in commit a3f9246e3.

Gobby rule authoring should prefer semantic workflow events `turn_start` and `turn_end`; raw `before_agent`, `after_agent`, and `stop` are provider/runtime escape hatches. Installed rule definitions use `RuleDefinitionBody` with an `effects` list, and agent termination is handled separately via `end_agent_run`.

Gobby web UI theming discipline (user feedback, learned the hard way in #14718): light-mode design changes MUST be scoped to [data-theme="light"] in CSS, or branched via the existing useResolvedTheme() hook for Tailwind/TSX (e.g. SegmentedControl). NEVER alter shared selectors or shared tokens globally for a light-only fix — it regresses dark. Dark mode is a FROZEN shipped baseline; the user's reference is .gobby/screenshots/IMG_3754.PNG (accent/chartreuse text+tints on near-black; transparent .app-header over var(--bg-primary)). Concretely: body backdrop is theme-split — default/dark body = var(--bg-primary) (near-black, matches IMG_3754), [data-theme="light"] body = var(--bg-secondary) (intentional light recessed-depth). .impeccable.md 'one system, two postures' means different problems per theme: accent washes look muddy on light's near-white paper but are the correct signature on dark's near-black — do not neutralize dark to fix light. font-semibold on selected segmented options + .chat-scope-btn.active is a confirmed universal good-fit kept in both themes. Verify dark is byte-unchanged (diff screenshot vs IMG_3754) whenever touching shared chrome.

Shipped light selected-state system (#14722, commit 68dca99bf; rebuilds the globally-applied c16fecad1 that was reverted in 3b39e531e): light-only token --surface-selected: oklch(98.5% 0.005 125) — a brighter neutral well lifted ABOVE the --bg-secondary track and --bg-primary canvas; selection reads via lightness + font-semibold, NOT hue. It is undefined in dark (only referenced by light-scoped rules) so dark never resolves it. Light treatments: selected (SegmentedControl active via useResolvedTheme branch, .command-palette-item.active, .chat-scope-btn.active which also DROPS the inset accent stripe in light, .session-item.attached) = --surface-selected + --text-primary; applied filter/constraint (.activity-filter-button[aria-expanded], .activity-filter-dropdown__item--active) = solid --accent + --accent-foreground (the one decisive accent moment, 5.51:1); session-kind .chip--* = neutral mono pills (--bg-tertiary/--text-secondary), accent NOT spent on identity metadata. Verify light WCAG 2.2 AA via chrome-devtools canvas-2D sRGB readback (Chrome returns computed colors as oklch() strings, so JS regex parsing is invalid — rasterize via canvas fillStyle+getImageData).

task_ref workflow variable: Set to `#{seq_num}` (e.g., `#8978`) when claiming/creating a task, cleared to `""` when closing. Previously the require-task-close rule template used `{{ task_ref }}` which rendered empty when task_ref wasn't initialized (not a missing-from-context issue — task_ref IS available via _build_eval_context() flattening session variables). Template was changed to `{{ claimed_task_id[:8] if claimed_task_id else '(unknown)' }}`. task_ref is also used in commit_policy.py context. Must be initialized to `""` via init-task-ref.yaml to prevent empty rendering. Similarly, task_claimed must be initialized to `false` via init-task-claimed.yaml to prevent NameError in the `when` condition.

Epic #15741 Python require-python-skill discovery rule (#15757) triggers on .py and .pyi writes, exact Python tooling/package config basenames pyproject.toml, setup.cfg, setup.py, tox.ini, noxfile.py, pytest.ini, mypy.ini, ruff.toml, .python-version, Pipfile, and py.typed, plus requirements*.txt and requirements*.in. This is intentional coverage for Python source, type stubs, package type markers, and dependency/tooling config without broadly matching unrelated TOML/YAML/JSON files.

Skills template-to-installed pattern: The skills table now has a `source` column with values 'template', 'installed', 'project' (matching workflow_definitions). Templates are bundled content (enabled=False), installed are active copies, project are project-scoped copies. Also has `deleted_at` for soft deletes. Migration v125 adds these columns. The source taxonomy has NO 'global' concept — installed = not project-scoped, project = has project_id. Key files: storage/skills.py (Skill dataclass + LocalSkillManager), skills/sync.py (template sync pattern), hooks/skill_manager.py (DB-backed with filesystem fallback), skills/manager.py (coordinator). Auto-install happens in cli/installers/shared.py after sync_bundled_content_to_db().

gwiki librarian near-duplicate detection treats the current `lint::collect_pages()` snapshot as authoritative. `near_duplicate_pairs` builds `pages_by_path` before semantic queries and ignores any semantic hit absent from that map, preventing removed pages retained in a stale semantic index from becoming candidate pairs. Live pairs still pass through existing structural, redirect, session/source, citation, and reviewed-distinct exclusions. Implemented by task #18864 in commit f030a26ca.

Task #17257 decomposed gobby-clones MCP tools: public factory stays in src/gobby/mcp_proxy/tools/clones.py, with implementation registries in _clones_creation.py, _clones_read.py, _clones_operations.py, _clones_cleanup.py, and shared dependencies in _clones_context.py.

Telegram operator documentation authority (task #18895, commit fef59fed8): docs/guides/telegram.md is the canonical operator guide for BotFather setup, secure channel updates, DM/group authorization, Telegram privacy modes, responder/project/model behavior, shipped capabilities, limits, and troubleshooting. docs/guides/comm-integrations.md remains the cross-channel architecture and API overview; docs/reviews/channel-parity-matrix.md records Telegram parity completion and defers only the Mini App dashboard under #18498. Documentation prose and parity research are reviewed against source rather than enforced by committed pytest contracts.

Task #18702 / commit 54551f396 makes verification evidence durable in verification_receipts. The table intentionally stores session_id as an audit UUID without a session foreign key: a BEFORE DELETE session trigger removes only unassigned receipts, while task-attributed receipts survive session cleanup and are deleted by task/project cascades. close_task no longer consumes the bounded 50-item session variable; that variable remains only for readiness compatibility. Close validation builds a separate deterministic 32,000-character packet that always catalogues failed, conflicting, and unknown receipts, aggregates the low-risk tail with count/ID range/outcome disclosure, and returns evidence_completeness in the validation verdict/close response.

To check if a gobby task has already been implemented: 1) search git log for commits referencing the task ID (git log --grep), 2) search codebase for the specific fix mentioned in the task, 3) run relevant tests to confirm they pass. Tasks often get fixed as side effects of other work without being closed.

When loading bundled prompt .md files at runtime (not via PromptLoader/DB), you must strip YAML frontmatter manually. Pattern: split on '---' with maxsplit=2, take parts[2].strip(). The sync system (sync.py) handles this via parse_frontmatter(), but direct file reads (like instructions.py) need manual stripping. See build_gobby_instructions() for the pattern.

Gobby integrations docs audit finding: `gobby github import/sync/pr` CLI paths use the configured `github` MCP server via `GitHubSyncService`, while the `gobby-tasks-ops:import_github_issues` MCP tool shells out to the local `gh` CLI. Document these prerequisites separately to avoid drift.

CommunicationsManager channel lifecycle now keeps adapter initialization failures in runtime state via _channel_init_errors and exposes real active/init_error status through channel_to_dict(); HTTP communications routes and the communications MCP add_channel tool should use channel_to_dict for channel payloads instead of plain dataclass asdict when runtime status matters.

Workflow hook project-path warning policy: keep warnings when project_id is missing or unknown because that catches lost project context; only demote no project_path resolution to debug for known no-repo system projects such as _personal/_global via _is_known_no_repo_project. Dirty-file helpers should treat None project_path as no-repo and return empty DirtyFiles without shelling out.

Agent definition source of truth for current Gobby: `AgentDefinitionBody` lives in `src/gobby/workflows/definitions.py`; bundled agent YAML lives under `src/gobby/install/shared/workflows/agents/` with deprecated templates in its `deprecated/` subdirectory. Agent definitions do not have a `max_turns` field; stale YAML/API payload keys are ignored or scrubbed on normalized write/output paths, and `timeout` is the only definition-level runtime limit. Normal spawned-agent self-completion is via `gobby-agents:end_agent_run`; `kill_agent`/`stop_agent` are operator or parent cancellation/process cleanup controls.

For the PostgreSQL 18 upgrade immediately after the SQLite-to-PostgreSQL hub migration, Gobby has not launched publicly, so do not build a PG17 backward-compatibility or dual-runtime path. The accepted approach is backup-first, then destructive Docker volume recreate/restore for internal installs.

As of task #18800, gwiki operational AI config construction uses gcore ai_source_for_conn/ai_source_without_primary helpers, while hub_ai_config_source passes its owned HubPrimary through lazy ai_source_with_primary so daemon mode opens no PostgreSQL connection. gwiki indexing/shared-code config selects daemon-served values plus routing-only YAML when available, otherwise its prior Postgres/environment plus full YAML stack. Database URL resolution order is GWIKI/GOBBY environment, daemon-served DSN, bootstrap.yaml, then gcore.yaml, with daemon effective-config errors propagating.

- prevention: When parsing function.arguments strings, fall back to Value::Null on serde_json parse failure.
