Project names are unique only among live rows: `idx_projects_active_name` is a partial unique index on `projects(name) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL`. `LocalProjectManager.get_or_create` uses an atomic PostgreSQL upsert against that index, while `ensure_exists` resolves conflicts by requested ID first and live name second.

In Gobby terminal CLI compaction/compression (/compact or /compress), the CLI compacts in place and does not create a new Gobby session row or child session. Post-compact continuation behavior should key off the compact SessionStart/pre-created session path for the same session, not wait for a child session.

HTTP telemetry middleware derives http.target from the routed request scope after call_next (and in the exception path), uses the fixed value "unmatched" when no route exists, and excludes request-derived session_id/project_id labels to keep Prometheus metric cardinality bounded.

One-surface UI (epic #14767) design directives from the user: (1) Standalone TasksPage is deleted, and its LifecycleBoard is obsolete. (2) New web UI work must use Tailwind utility classes with design tokens, NOT new legacy .css files (in-place Tailwind 4 migration). (3) The activity Tasks board was superseded by a list-only view per subsequent product decision. (4) ui/SegmentedControl in the activity-panel toolbar must use controlHeight="sm" to match the app-header Personal|Gobby ProjectSelector height.

Codex app-server `token_count.info.last_token_usage.output_tokens` already includes reasoning tokens. Gobby's Codex transcript and web-chat usage normalization must use `output_tokens` directly and must not add `reasoning_output_tokens`, which would double-count usage. This contract was established by task #16090.

In gobby-cli task #931, ghook recognizes `--cli=agy` for Google Antigravity CLI with canonical source `agy`. Antigravity CLI's documented command hook events are PascalCase: `SessionStart`, `UserPromptSubmit`, `PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse`, and `Stop`. In ghook's registry only `SessionStart` and `Stop` are fail-closed critical hooks; prompt/tool hooks are non-critical but still dispatch and spool normally. Regression coverage includes `cli_config::agy_uses_antigravity_hook_contract`, `diagnose::agy_uses_antigravity_pascal_case_hooks`, and contract forwarding for all five event names.

HTTPServer consumes runner-owned text-generation and LLM service references through ServiceContainer. Runner initialization is the single construction point; HTTPServer must preserve missing/degraded references instead of recreating them, so daemon consumers and HTTP routes share identical service state.

Session event-loop offload design (#16236): async HTTP session routes should use server.run_db for synchronous SessionManager/database calls and asyncio.to_thread for filesystem/archive work. SessionLivenessMonitor has no HTTP server dependency, so its synchronous DB query, tmux subprocess batching, session touch, and status update run through asyncio.to_thread. Regression tests verify the exact liveness offload calls and that transcript restore/stat execute on worker threads.

consecutive_tool_blocks counter is sticky and only resets on BEFORE_AGENT (new user prompt). If a rule blocks a tool (setting tool_block_pending=True), every subsequent BEFORE_TOOL increments the counter. After count >= 2, ALL tools are hardcoded-blocked regardless of type. A stop block clears tool_block_pending (allowing the next tool through) but does NOT reset consecutive_tool_blocks. This means after cascading sibling errors from parallel tool calls, you can get stuck where no tools work and stop is also blocked. The only escape is a new user turn (BEFORE_AGENT). Native CC task tools (TaskCreate/TaskUpdate) are blocked by the block-native-task-tools rule, and sibling errors from parallel calls cascade, which triggers this trap.

TranscriptReader.get_rendered_messages() intentionally bypasses the database to avoid corrupted str() data, reading directly from JSONL or gzip archives instead. A robust gzip decompression implementation in transcript_reader.py now gracefully handles truncated or malformed archives by returning partial lines and logging warnings.

Gobby task #17168 made daemon vector sync treat gcode indexed-file misses as expected stale per-file work: `sync_worker` catches `GcodeIndexedFileNotFoundError` from `vector_sync_file`, reloads the indexed row, logs INFO with no warning/error if the row disappeared, purges the project if the root disappeared, silently leaves pending if the source file disappeared, and logs one WARNING without traceback when the row and source still exist. It leaves `vectors_synced=false` and does not clear vector projection cleanup state for these stale misses; real vector failures still log ERROR with traceback.

Task #17405 removed dead Gemini-as-a-Gobby-provider runtime/test coverage while intentionally retaining Gemini model-family metadata for AGY/Droid/Qwen paths. Remaining src gemini references in provider_model_defaults, model_registry google/ mapping, provider_models model-family handling, context window lookup, AGY .gemini installer/config paths, Qwen auth type, typed transcript legacy value, and migration 295 are expected keep-list items rather than live Gemini provider support.

Merge delivery stage behavior: record_merge_result persists merge_commit_sha and merge_campaign_report, then success delegates directly to StageStatesManager.complete_stage(task_id, 'merge', commit_sha=merge_sha). The terminal close happens inside StageStatesManager via _close_task_in_txn(reason='manifest_exhausted', cascade_descendants=True); public close_task is intentionally not used. Failure delegates to fail_stage('merge'), with retry cap escalation owned by StageStatesManager.

AgentCleanupHandler.post_terminal_cleanup treats remove_agent_completion_subscribers as best-effort: failures are logged with exc_info and later worktree, session, runtime, and artifact cleanup must continue. Regression coverage: tests/agents/test_agent_cleanup.py::test_post_terminal_cleanup_subscriber_failure_does_not_stop_later_cleanup. Fixed for task #17088 in commit f4949f7ff.

Provider roadmap context: Gemini is deprecated in Gobby because Google's intent is for AGY to replace it, but AGY does not yet have full parity. Keep Gemini in agent/web-chat provider surfaces until AGY parity is reached; do not treat Gemini deprecation as permission to remove it broadly.

Agent rule_definitions enforcement chain: 1) AgentDefinitionBody.rule_definitions in definitions.py stores rules, 2) _load_agent_rule_definitions() in hooks.py loads from DB and creates synthetic WorkflowDefinitionRow+RuleDefinitionBody, 3) passed as extra_rules to RuleEngine.evaluate(). Critical: rules with source='agent' must bypass _filter_by_active_rules() which can filter everything out when _active_rule_names is []. Session variable _agent_type must be preserved from spawn (fixed in _session.py to not overwrite with 'default').

Task #17173 / commit 718fa7a72 reverted the false-positive Claude ingress ACP/Grok payload guard from 8d300207f. Hook ingress no longer infers provider identity from inner input_data field names such as hookEventName/sessionId; source remains the adapter-selection authority, so source='claude' traffic dispatches to ClaudeCodeAdapter. The Grok installer change from #16054 remains the correct prevention layer: it disables Grok's Claude-hook compatibility by setting ~/.grok/config.toml [compat.claude].hooks = false while still writing native Grok hooks to ~/.grok/hooks/gobby.json.

Task #17555 established the shared Python datetime helper contract for epic #17553: `gobby.utils.datetime` now exposes `utc_now`, `to_aware_utc`, `parse_stored_datetime`, `datetime_to_iso`, and `to_json_safe`. `PostgresHubDatabase` merges `-ctimezone=UTC` into psycopg conninfo options rather than overriding existing DSN options, and `_normalize_value` now preserves datetime rows as tz-aware UTC `datetime` objects while leaving DATE values as `date` objects. Boundary serialization should use the helper functions instead of storage cursor normalization.

codewiki module-link integrity invariant (crates/gcode/src/commands/codewiki): a file page renders `Module: [[code/modules/<file.module>]]`, where `file.module` comes from `cluster_file_modules` -> `cluster_module_name`. For a call-connected cluster spanning sibling subdirectories, that name is SYNTHETIC (common-prefix + `semantic_cluster_leaf`, e.g. `crates/gwiki/src/source_execute`), matching no real directory. INVARIANT: the module-doc emitter (`build_module_docs_with_filter`) MUST emit a page for every distinct non-empty `file.module` a file page links to, regardless of the doc-prune scope filter (`doc_scope.includes_module` -> `in_scope`, which keys on file-PATH scopes). Before commit 6292f52ac, a scoped/incremental heal emitted the file pages but the scope filter dropped the synthetic cluster module page, producing dangling file->module links that GREW every heal (curated_broken_link_count diverged 21->38->57->117->140 under the pre-fix binary) and pinned `gwiki trust` at attention_required. Fix: keep direct `file.module` link targets in the emitted set regardless of the scope filter; the filter still bounds ancestor-only modules. Whole-vault trust flip also needs daemon-synthesis concept-page citations (#17704) and pending-source compilation (#17705, note: default `gwiki compile` fail-loud is intended #17635 behavior, use --write-intent).

When a Gobby skill requires entering native Plan Mode and no direct EnterPlanMode tool is available, use the Gobby send_keys command path to send `/plan` plus Enter. Client-specific Gobby triggers like `/gobby plan` or `$gobby plan` may also be used when they are the configured native Plan Mode trigger.

Task #15433 introduced a frontend transport boundary: WebSocket usage payloads use RawSessionUsageUpdatedMessage/RawTokenEventMessage for string-or-number wire values, then normalize through normalizeSessionUsageUpdatedMessage and normalizeTokenEventMessage before consumers such as handleTokenEvent and useTokenEventsStream see strict numeric fields.

Daemon one-shot feature text-generation (gobby.ai text-gen lanes) MUST run the spawned model CLI/SDK in a NEUTRAL temp cwd, never the project dir. Spawning gemini/codex/claude inside a gobby project loads project context AND the gobby lifecycle hooks wired in ~/.gemini/settings.json (ghook SessionStart/BeforeTool/etc.), adding a variable 20-40s startup tax. Measured: gemini-3.5-flash json one-shot ~7s in an empty/$HOME dir vs 28-48s in the repo dir; GOBBY_HOOKS_DISABLED=1 alone restores ~7s. This tax (plus oversized validation prompts) is what pushed every candidate past the 60s candidate cap and caused recurring 'No JSON generation candidate succeeded; candidate timed out after 60s' for tasks.validation. Implementation (task #17100, commit d1cba914f): src/gobby/llm/textgen_cwd.py neutral_textgen_cwd() context manager owned by each adapter's generate*(); _run_cli_text_generation_command takes a required neutral_cwd: Path, sets cwd + stdin=DEVNULL, never request.cwd; codex no longer emits --cd; claude ClaudeAgentOptions sets cwd; Grok/Droid temp artifacts live under the same neutral root. Related: per-lane candidate timeout cli_candidate_timeout_seconds=150s for spawn-cold adapter_styles (CLI/DAEMON/LLM_PROVIDER/ACP) vs candidate_timeout_seconds=60s for LOCAL/OPENAI_COMPATIBLE; validation prompt bounded to VALIDATION_PROMPT_BUDGET_CHARS=14000; infra failures raise FeatureGenerationUnavailableError -> ValidationResult status='error' (distinct from 'invalid', migration 284) with durable per-task backoff in task_validation_backoff (migration 285) that escalates after 5 consecutive failures and resets on a real verdict.

As of task #18830 / commit 153ae3b63, daemon code-index projection sync handles GcodeProjectNotFoundError through shared vector/graph lifecycle logic: a vanished root purges the indexed project once; an existing root logs one warning without traceback and stays pending. Vector handling exits the file before graph sync and does not record a circuit-breaker success/failure. Memory KG relation cleanup now fetches outbound then inbound relations through entity_key-anchored UNWIND queries, excludes CO_OCCURS, preserves first-seen exact-triple order, and propagates either query failure to the service partial-failure path. The deletion prompt exposes deterministic r0/r1-style opaque IDs via relation_ids_to_delete; extractor maps valid IDs back to canonical triples, deduplicates, and warns on malformed/unknown IDs.

Postgres hub migration task #14086 added `gobby.storage.hub.protocol`: a backend-neutral protocol module with `Row = Mapping[str, Any]`, `Cursor`, `Savepoint`, `Transaction`, `LockTarget` (`PRIORITY: ClassVar[int]`), `LockAcquisitionOrderError`, and transaction-only `HubDatabase` (`transaction()`, `apply_migrations()`, `close()`, `dialect` literal). Later migration tasks extend adapters and manager-facing convenience methods.

Task #18560 hardened pg_search sanitization and PostgreSQL backend errors. Commit 8e78486ae1c320833b8f708a3ff5b16b5734d3e8. `sanitize_pg_search_query` in crates/gcore/src/search.rs now counts unescaped quotes before scanning: balanced quoted phrases retain their interiors, while dangling quotes are escaped. Outside balanced phrases it escapes Tantivy metacharacters `? ' * : ^ ~ { } / !` in addition to the existing brackets, literal parentheses, leading-minus, and boolean handling. gobby-code and gobby-wiki expectations were updated. gobby-wiki now maps postgres errors through `backend_error`, preserving database detail when present, across all BM25 queries. A real pg_search integration test covers the reported crash corpus, balanced phrases, and dangling quotes; focused results were 9 gobby-wiki BM25 tests, 10 gobby-core search tests, and 4 gobby-code sanitizer tests passing. Targeted cargo fmt and clippy -D warnings passed, and the mandatory test-quality audit found 37 tests with 0 issues. `.gobby/project.json` now registers `gobby-test-quality-audit` as a custom validation matcher so the required `gobby test-quality audit ... --fail-on-new --min-severity ...` command is retained as structured validation evidence.
Gobby Linear sync CLI: `gobby linear sync-all --forward` is the shipped command for active-only forward sync. The earlier pre-release `--active` alias was removed and is now an unrecognized option.

Task #13688 shutdown cleanup fix: HTTPServer._process_shutdown now treats asyncio.CancelledError during graceful shutdown as expected cancellation and does not increment shutdown_failed_total; MCPClientManager.disconnect_all finalizes cleanup under cancellation by cancelling/awaiting health, reconnect, and disconnect tasks, clearing _connections/_reconnect_tasks, marking health disconnected, and clearing lazy connected_at before re-raising cancellation; search.embeddings._fetch_embeddings owns and always awaits AsyncOpenAI.close() in finally.

Gobby storage SQL now uses psycopg/PostgreSQL %s positional placeholders directly; the old hub-layer qmark/$N placeholder remapper was removed, so callers must duplicate/reorder params themselves and escape literal percent signs in parameterized SQL.

For Gobby cross-repo tasks where the assigned task belongs to one project but the target files live in a different repository, use gobby-worktrees.create_worktree with project_path set to the target repo and worktree_path set to a writable temp path (for example /private/tmp/...) to create an editable target-repo worktree. Commit in that target worktree with the task ID in the message, then submit the original task stage for review. (Originally established for the pre-merge gobby-cli sibling repo, which is now merged into gobby as crates/.)

Tasks are NOT required for: (1) plan mode work, (2) pure research/investigation unless the user explicitly asks for a research task (e.g., to feed to a pipeline later). CLAUDE.md rule #3 'create or claim a task before editing a file' should be interpreted literally — it's about file edits, not all work. Don't create tasks just to satisfy the rule when no files will be edited.

Gobby build is fire-and-forget: after build_task starts lifecycle automation, the dispatcher should advance routine stage transitions itself. For example, when a QA reviewer calls approve_review, dispatcher should advance review_approved -> done and continue merge/downstream dispatch without requiring a coordinator to tick build_task. Coordinator agents for build epics exist to debug/fix automation bugs, not to drive normal lifecycle progression.

In gcode Rust call extraction, local Rust import targets must compute Symbol::make_id with the tree-sitter declaration node byte_start, not the identifier name byte_start. Rust `function_item`/`struct_item` symbols start at the declaration line start (e.g. `pub(crate) fn ...` at `pub`), so `LocalImportBinding.byte_start` for Rust local imports must use declaration-start offsets or graph CALLS edges point at synthetic non-canonical target IDs and `blast-radius` cannot traverse the real symbol.

In gcode Rust call extraction, local Rust import targets must compute Symbol::make_id with the tree-sitter declaration node byte_start, not the identifier name byte_start. Rust `function_item`/`struct_item` symbols start at the declaration line start (e.g. `pub(crate) fn ...` at `pub`), so `LocalImportBinding.byte_start` for Rust local imports must use declaration-start offsets or graph CALLS edges point at synthetic non-canonical target IDs and `blast-radius` cannot traverse the real symbol.

CLI Postgres ownership is centralized in gobby.cli.runtime.CliRuntime. One top-level Click invocation lazily memoizes a single HubDatabase, shares it with DB-backed config loading and operational helpers, and closes it through Click teardown. Operational helpers borrow injected databases; runtime_hub_database is reserved for bounded standalone/bootstrap composition roots. PostgresHubDatabase keeps a strong open-instance registry so leaked or failed-close pools remain retryable at atexit.

When writing block-reason text or any agent-facing recovery guidance in Gobby rule templates, do NOT include tool calls that invite the agent to browse for work (e.g. list_ready_tasks). An agent blocked here should either create a task for the specific work in front of them, or claim a specific task they already know about. Suggesting they 'discover' available tasks is scope creep in disguise — the agent should stay focused on what the user asked for, not shop the backlog. Recovery suggestions should be scoped to the immediate task at hand, never framed as 'here's how to find work.'

Pipeline stale-execution recovery has two deliberately different sweeps (post #17756): (1) daemon startup `_recover_pipelines` (runner_lifecycle_subsystems.py) runs `resume_interrupted_pipelines` for resume_on_restart pipelines, then `interrupt_stale_running_executions` → INTERRUPTED (non-terminal, retryable), scoped to the runner's home project only; (2) executor-level `PipelineExecutor.startup_sweep()` → `fail_stale_running_executions` → FAILED (terminal), run by `ServiceContainer.get_pipeline_executor` on lazy per-project executor creation — the only sweep point for projects outside the runner's home project. Both share `_mark_stale_running_executions(exclude_ids, *, status)` in storage/pipeline_executions.py (atomically fails RUNNING steps + writes daemon-restart note, leaves WAITING_APPROVAL alone). Never wire the FAILED sweep into init_orchestration/daemon startup: it would run before resume_interrupted_pipelines and break resume_on_restart. Detached runs (`start_detached`, POST /api/pipelines/run background:true → 202) are retained in `_detached_tasks` with execution ids in `_detached_execution_ids` so the sweep excludes in-flight runs; done-callback treats ApprovalRequired as a park (info), not a failure.

Gobby web `useChat` tests should use `web/src/hooks/__tests__/useChat.setup.ts` helpers (`createUseChatTestContext`, `cleanupUseChatTestContext`, `loadUseChatModule`) instead of duplicating WebSocket, fetch, localStorage, and console setup. The shared context seeds `gobby-conversation-id`/`gobby-db-session-id` and mutes console `log`, `debug`, `warn`, and `error` output for Vitest.

Daemon YAML secret migration pattern: GobbyRunner._migrate_yaml_secrets() (runner.py) runs after Phase 2 config reload. It checks known secret fields for plaintext values (not $secret: refs or None), encrypts them via ConfigStore.set_secret() into the SecretStore, rewrites the YAML to use $secret:<name> references, and reloads config. To add a new secret field to migration, add a tuple to the secret_fields list: (dotted_attr_path, secret_name). The $secret:<name> pattern is resolved by expand_env_vars() in config/app.py during config loading.

Obsolete history: earlier PostgreSQL bootstrap work kept daemon-brokered refs for isolated gcode helpers after removing root keyring refs. Current behavior removes that compatibility path too: root and helper bootstraps use database_url directly, and daemon/keyring database_url_ref values are rejected.

Web-chat interactive permission gates must preserve tool_use_id end-to-end: pending waiter dictionaries, UI pending frames, and approval, question, and plan response handlers all use the same ID. This prevents one concurrent response from resolving a different tool call's waiter.

Codewiki per-run observability can be threaded without expanding GenerateDocsOptions: let generate_hierarchical_docs own and return the aggregate, pass a mutable reference only through producers, then attach the completed aggregate to DocSink before finish. Diagram statistics use the unique slot key (page path, diagram kind), log only on first record, and serialize only counters so `_meta/codewiki.json` stays stable while the in-memory slot set enforces one final outcome per attempted slot.

Gobby session boundary contract after task #18742 / commit d2e273e6d: SessionEnd(reason='clear') expires the session; only reason='compact' marks handoff_ready. SessionStart(source='clear') creates an independent session with no parent discovery, predecessor expiry, summary/task/skill transfer, or claim reassignment. Compact retains parent matching, bounded summary injection, required-skill preservation, task ownership carryover, pending-context reset, and compact_self continuation. Resume and ordinary exits expire; idle web-chat sessions pause. Clear remains a native provider hook value and context-loss source for startup, memory, skill, and progressive-discovery resets.

For gobby-cli CodeWiki/gwiki narrative generation, Josh superseded the codex-pinned CodeWiki writer design: delete /api/llm/codewiki/write and gcore/gcode writer plumbing, use profile-based generation with provider from config, and build a shared local tool-enabled Lane B for aggregate narrative instead of routing through a codex exec subprocess.

For gobby-cli CodeWiki/gwiki narrative generation, Josh superseded the codex-pinned CodeWiki writer design: delete /api/llm/codewiki/write and gcore/gcode writer plumbing, use profile-based generation with provider from config, and build a shared local tool-enabled Lane B for aggregate narrative instead of routing through a codex exec subprocess.

Pipeline templates now live in src/gobby/install/shared/workflows/pipelines/ as individual YAML files with `type: pipeline`. The sync_bundled_workflows() handles both workflows and pipelines by detecting the `type` field. There is no separate pipelines sync target. The orphan cleanup in sync_bundled_workflows filters by workflow_type='workflow', so pipeline rows are preserved.

wait_for_agent is an immediate subscribe-and-return MCP tool as of task #18604 / commit a6b6bede5. Its public signature is wait_for_agent(run_id: str). Terminal runs return inline with notification_registered=false. Active runs require ambient session context plus completion registry, session manager, and DB; they persist lineage with subscribe_agent_completion(strict=True), return notification_registered=true, and rely on the daemon wake path. The status re-read, registration, post-registration re-read, and fresh-entry cleanup form one owning-loop no-await critical region. Fresh race cleanup deletes only subscription.inserted_session_ids; merged entries remain for the pending notify snapshot.

Rule engine mcp_call effects are dispatched by HookManager._dispatch_mcp_calls() (added in ddc4aa7c). The rule engine builds mcp_calls into HookResponse.metadata['mcp_calls'] but does NOT dispatch them itself — HookManager.handle() extracts them after workflow evaluation and dispatches via ToolProxyService. Context injection: session_id comes from event.metadata['_platform_session_id'], prompt_text from event.data['prompt']. Background calls use asyncio fire-and-forget pattern matching broadcasting.

Web chat sendMode semantics: before a conversation exists, changing mode is an intentional local selection and succeeds. Once a conversation exists, sendMode commits currentMode only after set_mode is sent successfully over the still-open same WebSocket; SendModeAction returns boolean success so transport failures are observable.

In Codex sessions, Gobby skill routing is commonly invoked with `$gobby <skill> ...`; `/gobby <skill> ...` is the router-contract form used in Gobby skill docs. Skills intended for Codex should mention `$gobby` when giving user-facing invocation examples.

RuleDefinitionBody no longer supports singular `effect=` parameter. Only `effects=[...]` (list) is accepted. The backward-compat `_normalize_effect_to_effects` model validator was removed. All YAML templates already used `effects:` — only test code used the singular form.

Tmux window-title repair should derive the visible session prefix from Session.seq_num when available and treat any literal "session_ref" text in a ref, title, or window name as an unresolved placeholder. The repair sweep intentionally re-renames already-managed tmux windows when their current window name contains that placeholder.

Task #17410 made Droid todo_state snapshots first-class transcript records: the Droid parser emits a synthetic completed TodoWrite tool_use/tool_result pair with tool_use_id prefix droid-todo-state- keyed by session_id plus todos payload, while transcript_normalization.py collapses only consecutive Droid synthetic todo_state pairs with the same id and leaves non-consecutive repeats in order.

SearchConfig strangler fig: There were two duplicate SearchConfig classes — one in search/models.py and one in config/search.py. The config/search.py version was the strangler fig artifact. The search/models.py version had `from __future__ import annotations` which breaks Pydantic v2 field resolution for uppercase fields like EMBEDDING_API_KEY, causing daemon crash loops during skill indexing. Fix: consolidated into search/models.py (removed `from __future__ import annotations`), deleted config/search.py, updated config/app.py to import from search.models. IMPORTANT: config/search.py cannot re-export SearchConfig because it imports SearchMode from search.models which triggers search/__init__.py creating a circular import.

Migration v126 adds chat_mode TEXT DEFAULT 'plan' column to sessions table. BASELINE_VERSION bumped from 125 to 126. The chat_mode column persists ChatSession.chat_mode to DB for surviving reconnections. session_variables.chat_mode (workflow rule engine) and sessions.chat_mode (DB column) serve different consumers and both are needed.

Task escalation storage keeps `tasks.escalated_at` and `tasks.is_escalated` synchronized. `update_task()` handles this automatically; direct lifecycle SQL such as `escalate_task()` must write both columns atomically so raw queries, dispatch filters, and model state agree.

Codex terminal sessions without a recorded tmux_pane are intentionally weak liveness records: do not fast-expire them solely because parent_pid is dead. Live wake cannot force these non-tmux interactive Codex sessions; durable mailbox delivery, hook/transcript activity revival, and capture_output transcript-tail fallback are the expected behavior.

As of 2026-06-25, the gobby repo mirrors the gobby-cli wiki branch separation: active branches ignore top-level `gobby-wiki/`, `.githooks/pre-push` publishes the local vault to a sibling `../gobby-wiki` worktree on orphan branch `wiki` when pushing `main`, and tracked vault placeholder files were removed from the active-branch index in commit 285a24e91 (`[gobby-#17362]`). This repo may already use a Gobby-managed `.git/hooks/pre-push`; chain `.githooks/pre-push` from that hook rather than replacing `core.hooksPath`.

Gwiki health citation discovery and matching lives in crates/gwiki/src/health/citations.rs. The child module owns source citation/needle indexes, link and text matching, fenced-code removal, and boundary checks. crates/gwiki/src/health.rs crate-privately re-exports SourceNeedleIndex and build_source_needle_index because exports/pages.rs consumes them.

Claude Code 2.x records hook blocks as top-level `type: "attachment"` entries whose `attachment.type` is `hook_blocking_error`. The observed attachment carries `hookName`, `hookEvent`, `toolUseID`, and nested `blockingError` with string fields `blockingError` and `command`. It is not a top-level `system/subtype: hook_blocking_error` record, and observed Stop-hook blocks are not followed by a duplicate tool_result line.

Gobby workflow rule evaluation expands raw `before_agent` to semantic `turn_start`, and raw `after_agent`, `stop`, and `stop_failure` to semantic `turn_end` in `src/gobby/workflows/engine/core.py`. `src/gobby/workflows/hooks.py` uses a narrower observer turn-end helper for `after_agent` and `stop` during hook-side bookkeeping.

Telegram link-preview control contract (task #18860, commit 311b3544f): channel config link_preview_options is validated at adapter initialization against the Bot API fields is_disabled, url, prefer_small_media, prefer_large_media, and show_above_text. gobby-communications.send_message exposes a per-message link_preview_options object; it is merged over the channel default, while internal metadata null explicitly clears the default. Resolved options are applied to every text chunk and preserved through editMessageText/overflow sends for streamed replies. ## Lesson
- principle: After verifying a local branch with refs/heads/<name>, every revision-consuming command in the merge flow must use that exact ref.
- root_cause: The implementation qualified ancestry and target SHA lookup but still passed the unqualified source name to git diff and git merge, allowing Git's tag precedence to select a same-name tag.
- prevention: Keep source_ref and target_ref variables derived from verified refs/heads names and use them for ancestry, incoming-diff, merge, and authoritative SHA operations; retain a regression asserting no unqualified merge command.

Dependabot/security dep bumps in web/: do NOT force esbuild to >=0.28 globally. Vite (^0.25.0) uses esbuild to downlevel for the old build target (chrome87/es2020/etc.), and esbuild 0.28+ dropped destructuring downleveling for that target, so `vite build` fails with 'Transforming destructuring to the configured target environment is not supported yet'. The vulnerable esbuild (CVE range >=0.27.3 <0.28.1) is pulled by tsx (~0.27.0), NOT vite (vite stays on esbuild 0.25.x, which is below the vuln floor and build-safe). Fix: scope the override to tsx only — `"overrides": { "tsx": { "esbuild": ">=0.28.1" } }` — leaving vite/direct esbuild at ^0.25.0. Also prefer within-major override caps (e.g. undici/protobufjs/@babel/core `>=X <8`) so a `>=` override doesn't silently jump a transitive dep to a new major.

GOTCHA (#15642, fixed commit c11aa7173): managed web-chat backends must broadcast the pending plan ONCE at the true end of the send_message stream with the FULLY accumulated text — never on an in-stream DoneEvent, and never `return` after one. Droid (stream-jsonrpc, backends/droid.py) emits an intermediate `result`/DoneEvent after its preamble text but BEFORE its tool calls (Read/LS) and the real plan. The old code did `if isinstance(chat_event, DoneEvent): _maybe_broadcast_pending_plan(...); yield; return` which fired on that FIRST DoneEvent: it broadcast only the ~120-char preamble as the 'plan' AND the return cancelled the in-flight tool ('Tool execution cancelled by user') and aborted the turn before the plan was generated — so for any Droid plan turn that explores with tools first, the approval card never surfaced (live-found by the #15619 matrix; Codex worked only because it planned without tools / single terminal DoneEvent). Fix: track `final_done = chat_event; continue` on in-stream DoneEvents and defer the single _maybe_broadcast_pending_plan to after the `async for` loop, yielding `final_done or DoneEvent(...)`. This matches the ACP path (acp_session.py), which already broadcasts only after the loop and never had the bug. Because _maybe_broadcast_pending_plan is idempotent (returns if _pending_plan_content is not None), the FIRST broadcast wins — so a partial/early broadcast is sticky; always broadcast with the full text. Codex (codex.py) broadcasts on every in-stream DoneEvent without return; it works today but shares the latent partial-broadcast risk if it ever uses tools before planning.

Product navigation direction for Gobby web UI: long term, Chat and Config should become the only top-level pages, with the hamburger/sidebar retired. Fix for bundled rule tests failing with get_by_name() returning None: Bundled rules are synced with source='template'. Tests calling get_by_name() without include_templates=True get None. Fix: modify _sync_bundled() helper in each test file to execute `db.execute("UPDATE workflow_definitions SET source = 'installed' WHERE source = 'template'")` after syncing. This marks templates as installed so get_by_name() finds them. CAUTION: For files with RuleEngine integration tests, this can cause interference if other rules were synced with enabled=True. In that case, the engine fixture must disable all rules first (`UPDATE workflow_definitions SET enabled = 0`) before enabling only the rules under test.

The public fetchWorkflows(params?) and fetchRules(params?) callbacks treat an omitted argument as an explicit unfiltered fetch. Internal mutation and WebSocket refreshes therefore use private refetch callbacks backed by refs holding the latest caller filters, preserving include_deleted and other active filters while retaining the public ability to clear filters with an argument-less fetch. Implemented in task #16671 / commit a70bdbf6b.

For Gobby stdio MCP session references, DaemonProxy derives project_id from GOBBY_PROJECT_ID or the nearest .gobby/project.json. Gobby chat attachments are implemented with `chat_attachments` PostgreSQL metadata plus project-scoped files under `GOBBY_HOME/projects/<project-id>/attachments/<id-prefix>/<id>/...`. HTTP routes live in `src/gobby/servers/routes/chat_attachments.py`; WebSocket binding/prompt reference helpers live in `src/gobby/servers/websocket/chat_attachments.py`. Main chat and terminal proxy messages send stored references as `attachments: [{id}]`; the backend binds IDs and injects filename/MIME/size plus `id=<attachment-id>` into prompts, not local filesystem paths. Settings overlay sections (epic #16998/#17011, built on the #17108 foundation in web/src/components/settings/) wire dotted config paths through the per-section draft shell. Two non-obvious facts every config-backed section needs:

1. useConfiguration().configValues is a NESTED object, not flat dotted keys. /api/config/values returns {values:<nested>} (unflatten_config in src/gobby/servers/routes/configuration_values.py::get_config_values). The #17108 pickPaths in SettingsSection.tsx originally did configValues[path] with a dotted path, returning undefined for any real nested path. #17117 fixed pickPaths to walk nested config by dotted path (split on '.'). AppearanceSection never caught this because its OWNED_PATHS is empty (client-only).

2. Save round-trips through the backend flattener. SettingsSection passes the flat dotted-keyed draft to saveConfig -> PUT /api/config/values -> save_config_values runs flatten_config(request.values) then unflatten_config + deep_merge. So sending {"recommend_tools.profile":"feature_high"} is accepted. Caveat: deep_merge adds/overwrites but does not delete, so removing a map entry (e.g. context_window_overrides) is not persisted as a deletion (pre-existing limitation shared with the old ConfigFormTab).

Schema for selects: useConfiguration().schema is the raw nested DaemonConfig JSON schema with $defs + $ref. Resolve a node by dotted path (resolving $ref at each step, including the leaf's own $ref) to read .enum -- all *.profile fields $ref FeatureProfile enum [feature_low, feature_mid, feature_high]. #17117 added web/src/components/settings/configSchema.ts (resolveSchemaNode, enumOptionsAt, numberBoundsAt) for this; reuse it rather than importing the dying ConfigurationPage.helpers.ts (deleted in #17047). Scalar primitives: reuse activity/fields TextField/SwitchField + the new NumberField; selects via the foundation BoundedSelectField; arrays via StringListField; maps via KeyValueMapField (custom renderValue for number/array/object values).

Gobby uuid-column driver asymmetry (post-migration-304/305): Python psycopg3 binds str→uuid transparently (and PostgresAdapter._normalize_value stringifies uuid on reads), but the Rust `postgres` crate (gcode/gwiki) is strict both ways — String/&str binds against uuid columns AND try_get::<_, String> reads from uuid columns fail at runtime with 'cannot convert between the Rust type String and the Postgres type uuid'. Rust uses boundary conversion: domain structs keep String ids, Uuid::parse_str at bind, .to_string() on read (with-uuid-1 feature on the postgres dep). Any new code_*/gwiki_* column or query must follow this. Also: migration tests provision fresh empty schemas and replay all on-disk migrations atop the current baseline, so data-dependent migration failures (uncastable populated rows) are invisible to CI — data-dependent casts need preflight DO guards (see migrations.py module docstring and test_uuid_cast_migrations_ship_a_preflight_guard).

Async DB offloading is path-sensitive in Gobby. Path B plan-keystroke mapping for Gemini CLI (task #15730, epic #15606, commit fab14a4a0). KEY ARCHITECTURE: gemini/grok/qwen are ACP-driven under Gobby -- launched as `gemini --acp` over stdio pipes (asyncio.create_subprocess_exec, GOBBY_HOOKS_DISABLED=1 + GOBBY_ACP_CHILD=1), permission via structured JSON-RPC session/request_permission auto-resolved by _select_permission_option in src/gobby/adapters/acp_client_requests.py. There is NO native TUI keystroke menu in any Gobby-MANAGED gemini flow (web-chat ACP = Path A, agents = one-shot --approval-mode yolo). Path B keystroke mapping applies ONLY to a USER-run NATIVE gemini TUI: Gobby installs native hooks via src/gobby/install/gemini/hooks-template.json (SessionStart/BeforeTool/AfterTool/etc., NO approval-suppressing hook like codex's PermissionRequest), so the native approval menus render and a user TUI registers as session_type=terminal for handle_attached_plan_approval. CAPTURE (Gemini v0.44.1): plan mode `--approval-mode plan` is read-only and gates the PLAN conversationally ('Does this plan look good to you?') with NO selectable menu (mode cycled via Shift+Tab). The keystroke-selectable gate is the per-action approval menu in manual/default mode: 'Apply this change?' (edit) = 1.Allow once / 2.Allow for this session / 3.Modify with external editor / 4.No, suggest changes (esc); 'Allow execution of [Shell]?' = 1.Allow once / 2.Allow for this session / 3.No, suggest changes (esc). Top two options STABLE; reject DIGIT varies (4 edits/3 shell) but '(esc)' constant. Digit activates immediately, no Enter. MAPPING in src/gobby/adapters/plan_keystrokes.py _GEMINI_PLAN_MENU: approve_act->PlanKeystroke('1' literal) [keep prompting=normal], approve_yolo->PlanKeystroke('2' literal) [stop prompting=bypass], request_changes->PlanKeystroke('Escape' literal=False, named tmux key) [shape-independent reject]. Static map, requires_pane('gemini')=False. Gemini is the FIRST CLI where approve_yolo != approve_act (claude/codex/droid collapsed both to one). PROCEDURE: throwaway tmux -L plancap -f /dev/null, GOBBY_HOOKS_DISABLED=1, /tmp scratch; verify non-destructively by pressing the SAFE reject (Esc / 'No') and confirming the file is untouched. Related: droid capture [[bf1d429d]], capture procedure [[59385f3f]], codex [[14895604]]. Remaining leaves: #15731 grok, #15732 qwen (both ACP; qwen infra-blocked Internal error -32603) -- same architecture caveat applies, verify the native-TUI menu empirically before mapping.

Daemon health timeouts on macOS had three independent causes: dial targets using `localhost` could stall while `127.0.0.1` remained responsive; synchronous PostgreSQL calls from SessionMessageProcessor (`UnmodeledObservationStore.record` and `TokenEventStore.record`, plus related session writes) blocked the asyncio event loop under contention; and `/api/admin/health` synchronously read the ghook runtime stamp with `Path.read_text`. Keep daemon dial hosts numeric, pass daemon database work through the bounded `DatabaseExecutor`, and offload health-endpoint filesystem reads with `asyncio.to_thread`. One-shot SIGUSR2 `faulthandler.register` plus an external numeric-loopback probe was effective for identifying the exact Python caller; avoid repeating faulthandler dumps on Python 3.14 because the sampler itself can spin.

Dev-loop pipeline inputs for multi-provider setup: developer_provider='gemini', qa_provider='claude', qa_model='claude-opus-4-6'. CURRENT (epic #18599, July 2026): WAIT_TOOL_NAMES in src/gobby/mcp_proxy/wait_tools.py is ("wait_for_output", "wait_for_summary") — wait_for_agent was REMOVED by task #18607 / commit a3667e2d5. wait_for_agent is now an ordinary fast tool: subscribe-and-return (task #18604 / commit a6b6bede5), no wrapper wait guard, no heartbeat, no timeout rewrite, no special /api/mcp/tools/call routing. The wrapper fingerprint staleness guard (mcp_wrapper_fingerprint_stale_result) applies only to WAIT_TOOL_NAMES members, so tests must use wait_for_summary (gobby-sessions) as the wait-tool exemplar (commit 094816beb). Bounded PostgreSQL async work lives in src/gobby/storage/hub/async_ops.py. run_bounded_db opens a dedicated psycopg.AsyncConnection outside the sync pool, reserves RUN_BOUNDED_DB_CLEANUP_SLICE_SECONDS (1.0s) inside the caller deadline, cancels once, observes via asyncio.wait, hard-closes the main pgconn locally with finish(), cancels a second time to interrupt psycopg's separate cancel-connection wait, and reaps the child before returning. Expiry before COMMIT submission raises BoundedDBTimeoutError and the socket close guarantees rollback; failure or cancellation after submission raises IndeterminateCommitError because server commit state may be applied. PostgresHubDatabase.conninfo exposes the normalized DSN for these consumers.

gobby-cli close_task LLM validator gotchas (learned closing #911): (1) It reads the raw commit diff through a ~15.8K-char window in ALPHABETICAL file-path order and TRUNCATES the rest — a file late in the alphabet (e.g. build_parts/curated_content.rs after architecture_diagrams.rs) can be entirely omitted, and the validator then rejects with 'full diff ... not present in the validation evidence'. Fix: for large multi-file commits, INLINE the key code of late-alphabetical files directly in the changes_summary so the validator can verify the criteria without the diff. (2) It demands a confirmed clean validation run on the FINAL COMMITTED TREE — reporting a pass on a 'behaviorally-identical prior tree' is rejected; run the exact validation_criteria command (e.g. cargo nextest run -p gobby-code => 923 passed exit 0) on the committed SHA and state that explicitly. (3) The completion-readiness gate needs a FRESH successful validation command run in the FOREGROUND (background `{...} >> LOG` runs are not auto-recorded as evidence).

## Lesson
- principle: Tests that exercise production entry points must be hermetic with respect to ambient daemon state: process-global caches initialized from the live environment make suite results depend on what happens to be running on the developer's machine and on test scheduling order.
- root_cause: gcore's effective-config OnceLock is process-global and initialized from ambient env/token at first touch; gwiki unit tests call production config entry points (local_index_options, hub_ai_config_source) with no way to force the standalone path, and a validation run that happened to pass (daemon quiescent or cache initialized as Unavailable) recorded 'cargo test -p gobby-wiki passes' as satisfied.
- prevention: Give ambient global caches an explicit kill-switch consulted on every read before the cache (GOBBY_DAEMON_CONFIG_DISABLE in gcore effective_config), set it inside the shared test EnvGuard so guarded tests are standalone by construction, keep exactly one env lock per test process, and recover from mutex poison so one genuine failure cannot cascade. When validating 'suite passes' criteria for code that probes live services, run the suite with the service both up and down.

## Diagnostic
- title: gwiki test suite depended on live daemon state via gcore's process-global effective-config cache
- message: cargo test -p gobby-wiki failed 14 tests whenever the developer's daemon was running: gcore's EFFECTIVE_CONFIG_STATE OnceLock was initialized from ambient env by whichever test thread first touched it, caching the live daemon's served config; env-guarded gwiki tests then resolved daemon values instead of their temp gcore.yaml, and a bespoke second env lock in support/config.rs tests raced test_env's ENV_TEST_LOCK on GOBBY_HOME while mutex poison cascaded one failure into twelve.

Settings overlay (epic #16998) pattern for App-owned ui_settings.* preferences: a ui_settings field that is NOT a useSettings field — e.g. ui_settings.selectedProvider, ui_settings.selectedProjectId — is owned and persisted by App.tsx (its own useState + a PUT /api/config/ui-settings effect), NOT by the useSettings hook. To expose such a preference inside a settings section, do NOT call useSettings or useProjects for the selection state in the section. Instead thread a dedicated *Selection context value through SettingsSectionContext, mirroring the providerSelection precedent: define a <Name>SelectionContextValue interface in SettingsSectionContext.ts, add an optional field on SettingsSectionContextValue, create a memoized object in App.tsx bound to App's existing state+setter, and pass it App -> SettingsOverlay -> SettingsSectionProvider -> context. The section consumes it via useSettingsSectionContext() and renders a controlled control (e.g. ProjectSelectField value/onChange), with a graceful fallback when the context value is absent. This keeps a single source of truth shared with the app chrome. Implemented for projectSelection in leaf #17119 (commit 4de10c9cc). Sections owning daemon DaemonConfig dotted-path config still use the per-section draft via SettingsSection's render-prop fields, separate from these live client selections.

Memory dream planner prompt policy as of task #18623 / commit 2909cb725: `DreamCandidate.to_prompt_dict()` preserves candidate content in full and conditionally emits `related_newer_memories` from immutable `RelatedMemoryEvidence` records with JSON-safe ISO timestamps. `MemoryDreamConfig.planner_batch_max_chars` defaults to 100,000. Droid CLI 0.174.0 live command-result contract: `droid exec --output-format stream-json` emits `tool_result.isError` as a boolean for both successful and failed `Execute` commands (`false` for exit 0, `true` for exit 7). The terminal hook path emitted `PostToolUse` for the successful command but emitted neither `PostToolUse` nor `PostToolUseFailure` for the nonzero command. Gobby therefore uses stream `isError` as the definitive managed-chat outcome, treats terminal `PostToolUse` as definitive success, and preserves unknown when a failure hook is absent, a stream flag is missing/non-boolean, or only human-readable text is available. Managed lifecycle payloads omit `is_error` for those ambiguous stream results. Captured fixture: tests/fixtures/provider_contracts/droid/command-outcomes-0.174.0.json. Implemented by #18380 in commits e8417351f and 2ae9746d0.

Circular import pitfall when re-exporting from __init__.py: In gobby, `prompts/__init__.py` re-exporting `sync_bundled_prompts` from `prompts/sync.py` caused a circular import because `sync.py` imports from `storage/prompts.py`, which imports from `prompts/models.py` (triggering `prompts/__init__.py`). Fix: don't re-export from __init__.py; callers import directly from `prompts.sync`. General rule: avoid re-exporting from __init__.py when the submodule has cross-package dependencies.

PostgreSQL migration advisory locks must be scoped by current_schema(), not database-global: pytest-xdist uses one isolated schema per worker, and a global lock can deadlock against each worker's open schema DDL transaction when a non-transactional migration runs. The local managed PostgreSQL instance also cannot safely handle unbounded xdist auto workers dropping large schemas concurrently; cap auto workers at 8 and serialize final DROP SCHEMA operations with a dedicated advisory lock.

When fixing pytest report failures in gobby, use the combined focused pytest command over the reported nodes after individual fixes; some Postgres-backed storage parity cases can run only in the larger focused context and skip when isolated. The memory keyword BM25 backend now tie-breaks memories by created_at then id for equal scores.

_dispatch_mcp_calls (hook_manager.py) and dispatch_mcp_calls (mcp_dispatch.py) must NOT inject extra parameters into MCP call arguments. ToolProxyService.call_tool() validates arguments against tool schemas and rejects unknown parameters, causing silent failures. The return value was also being discarded, hiding the validation errors. Fixed in commit 54b9a8f3 by removing prompt_text injection and adding result logging (warnings on success=False).

## Lesson
- principle: Do not delete discovery rows for orphaned external projections until all configured projection cleanup paths have completed without skip or failure.
- root_cause: The prune loop used a boolean cleanup result that stayed true when graph or vector cleanup was skipped because the corresponding service was unavailable, allowing SQL orphan rows to be deleted and preventing later rediscovery.
- prevention: Track skipped projection stores separately from failed stores and gate SQL deletion on confirmed non-skipped cleanup.

Global dispatcher agent-cap admission must use HubDatabase.advisory_lock(AgentCapAdmission(project_id=None)) across count-through-agent_run visibility. PostgresHubDatabase.advisory_lock uses a dedicated non-pooled psycopg connection with the same UTC-normalized conninfo, PGAPPNAME, prepare_threshold=None, and dict_row session options as the typed-config worker pool. Memory dream run interruption is unified on the 'interrupted' status of memory_dream_runs. Two complementary mechanisms: (1) MemoryDreamService.execute_run's `except asyncio.CancelledError` handler marks the run 'interrupted' (INTERRUPTED_CANCELLED_ERROR) for shutdown/timeout cancellations that do not involve a restart; (2) reconcile_interrupted_dream_runs (memory/dream/cron.py) -> MemoryDreamStore.mark_interrupted_runs, called from init_orchestration during synchronous startup BEFORE the daemon serves (hard no-clobber guarantee), marks orphaned 'running'/'started' rows 'interrupted' (INTERRUPTED_RESTART_ERROR) to recover hard-crash orphans. Codex hooks.json output schema per event type (from https://developers.openai.com/codex/hooks):

## Model-facing context delivery
- SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PostToolUse: use hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext (hidden from user, fed to model)
- PreToolUse, Stop: use systemMessage (the ONLY model-facing option — additionalContext is rejected/ignored)

## Visibility behavior
- systemMessage on SessionStart/UserPromptSubmit/PostToolUse: visible in chat but NOT fed to the model
- systemMessage on PreToolUse/Stop: fed to the model (only option)
- additionalContext on PreToolUse/Stop: rejected by Codex

## All events accept
- continue (bool), systemMessage, decision ('block'), reason
- PreToolUse additionally: hookSpecificOutput with permissionDecision/permissionDecisionReason

## Practical guidance (from Codex)
- SessionStart: durable session-wide instructions, repo context
- UserPromptSubmit: request-scoped context tied to user's latest message
- PostToolUse: observations from tool result (e.g. 'Python file detected; conventions: ...')
- PreToolUse: short, imperative gating/constraints before tool runs
- Stop: final blocking or shutdown-time instructions

## CodexHooksAdapter routing (fixed 2026-04-06)
- SessionStart: system_message → BOTH systemMessage (visible banner) AND additionalContext (model-facing)
- UserPromptSubmit, PostToolUse: system_message → additionalContext only
- PreToolUse, Stop: system_message → systemMessage; context_parts appended to systemMessage

MCP merge lifecycle invariant: merge_start, merge_resolve AI work, and merge_apply share try_acquire_resolve_lock keyed by resolution ID. A concurrent operation for the same resolution fails fast with retry_later. Every acquired lock is passed to release_resolve_lock in finally; release_resolve_lock both releases and evicts the keyed entry so completed resolution IDs do not accumulate in process memory.

Two-of-three = limbo (Gobby can finish with code). One-of-three with the rest unavailable upstream = blocked.

Full evaluation matrix: docs/research/cli-integration-matrix.md — scores all 35 ACP-speaking agents plus named non-ACP candidates (Aider, Windsurf/Devin) against the 3-surface gate. Consult it before starting any new CLI integration. Verify all three surfaces exist IN THE CLI before integrating — a hooks-only CLI traps you in hook-only limbo with no completion path except waiting on upstream.

Key findings: (a) agy = Antigravity CLI, Google replaced Gemini CLI with it on 2026-06-18. Gobby has a partial agy hook adapter BUT agy is BLOCKED, not finishable: Antigravity exposes NO ACP server and NO parseable transcripts, so the transcript-parser and web-chat-backend surfaces are upstream-blocked. Gobby's agy.py extending ACPHookAdapter is an internal hook-translation choice, NOT evidence agy speaks ACP as a server. Do not plan to 'finish agy' as if it were just code. (b) The highest-ROI Ready candidates are Cursor CLI and GitHub Copilot CLI — both have comprehensive lifecycle hooks AND speak ACP AND expose transcripts; Copilot's hooks are Claude-compatible (cheapest adapter), Cursor has 21 hook events + headless/CI. (c) Goose (AAIF, Apache-2.0, local-LLM via Ollama) is the open-source local-LLM CLI — Ready* but needs a SQLite transcript parser (sessions migrated JSONL->SQLite in v1.10). (d) Cline is Ready* (ACP + hooks, verify transcript persistence). (e) Aider = Skip (no hooks, no ACP, markdown chat, wrong architecture). (f) Windsurf/Devin = Defer (Cascade EOL, pivoting to Devin Local, no ACP). (g) Watchlist fully-ready: Kiro CLI and OpenClaw (ACP + hooks + transcripts). OpenCode is missing hooks (pending GitHub #12472).

Tmux window-title contract: persisted Session.title is authoritative. Manual and digest-owned title changes share the post-commit rename side effect. Queued asynchronous renames reload the current session from daemon storage before applying and skip when persisted state cannot be loaded, preventing stale provisional captures from overwriting newer digest titles. The periodic repair sweep also reloads persisted state, compares the managed window name with the authoritative resolved title, and repairs mismatches even when automatic-rename is off.

JSONL sync architecture (tasks.jsonl, memories.jsonl): Continuous daemon sync was removed in #10075. Shutdown export was further removed in #10198. JSONL files are now exported on-demand only: pre-commit hook and explicit CLI/MCP calls. The DB is the source of truth — stale JSONL has no impact on daemon operation. TaskSyncManager no longer has trigger_export, stop, or shutdown methods. MemoryBackupManager no longer has trigger_export, shutdown, or _process_export_queue.

Session activation reconciliation backstop is implemented in src/gobby/hooks/session_activation.py and is invoked by HookManager after SESSION_START registration and before every BEFORE_AGENT workflow rule evaluation. It repairs durable session_variables markers, agent/rule/skill/tool-block variables, baseline dirty tracking, terminal pickup metadata from agent_runs, and spawned-agent step workflow state without replaying prompt/context injection side effects.

Literature review for adaptive memory-recall parameter tuning (epic #17099) lives at docs/research/memory-recall-adaptive-tuning.md (paper seed). Durable findings: (1) Adaptive retrieval-weight tuning from usefulness feedback is a real GAP in production OSS agent-memory systems — Mem0, Zep/Graphiti, Letta/MemGPT, LangMem, A-MEM all use STATIC hardcoded retrieval weights; only Cognee has a feedback EMA loop (one scalar, off by default). Generative Agents (arXiv:2304.03442) is the copied archetype with all blend weights hardcoded to 1. (2) The idea is established in research; our exact framing (interpretable scalar weights + citation/referenced usefulness label + local-first) is near-frontier. Named prior art to differentiate against: RMM (arXiv:2503.08026, ACL 2025, neural reranker from cited evidence) and Learn-to-Memorize (arXiv:2508.16629, interpretable weights from task success). (3) Design corrections from the literature: 'referenced-in-output' is a documented WEAK label (ContextCite arXiv:2409.00729; up to 57% of citations post-rationalized, arXiv:2412.18004) — use ablation/leave-one-out as the gold usefulness signal (AttriBoT arXiv:2411.15102 makes it cheap); de-bias the LLM-judge (preference leakage arXiv:2502.01534, position bias arXiv:2305.17926); IPS-correct implicit feedback for position/selection bias (unbiased LTR arXiv:1608.04468); use PARTIAL pooling not naive full pooling (Gelman & Hill); gate offline on must-beat-static (Safe Exploration arXiv:2002.00467) plus a judge-independent quality eval (reward hacking arXiv:2210.10760). Verdict: defensible engineering synthesis, not a novel mechanism.

User feedback (session #5122, Tasks board mobile work): when a request contains an exploratory phrase like "figure out a better way to display it", scope STRICTLY to the literal ask and keep the diff surgical. Concretely here: the ask was only "make the kanban/Board desktop-only (>=768px) and fall back on mobile" — I over-interpreted it, added an unrequested mobile stage-chip bar to the List (non-jira) view, plus unrelated refactors (TasksTabModel/TasksBoardView dedup, TasksTabDetailSection extraction), and steered the user into it via a "Recommended" AskUserQuestion option. User reacted strongly ("looks like garbage", "I didn't ask for the stage chips", "you made changes to the non-jira view in mobile that I didn't request") and it cost a full revert (#14787).

**Why:** an exploratory phrase is an invitation to think, not license to expand scope onto surfaces the user didn't name; a 'Recommended' option in AskUserQuestion can rail-road a user into scope creep they later reject.

**How to apply:** Implement the minimal literal interpretation first; do not modify adjacent/untouched surfaces or bundle drive-by refactors into a feature fix. If additive UI seems valuable, ship the minimal version and let the user pull for more, or ask plainly/neutrally (no 'Recommended' steering) BEFORE building. Prefer the smallest diff that satisfies the exact words. Related: [[a297c0c5-3dca-58a7-8d05-e15bb56be8b0]], [[84c71ffc-4e44-5aba-bcb0-5649a29c50f8]].

Gwiki gateway timeout architecture (as of task #17593): `src/gobby/gwiki_gateway.py` defines INTERACTIVE_GWIKI_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=30.0 and GENERATION_GWIKI_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=270.0 as subprocess kill guards. Generation-backed gwiki calls (wiki_compile always — its --ai defaults to auto; wiki_ask when llm=true or ai not in {None, off}) get the generation guard in both the gobby-wiki MCP registry (src/gobby/mcp_proxy/tools/wiki.py) and /api/wiki routes (src/gobby/servers/routes/wiki.py); reads and retrieval-only asks keep the interactive guard. wiki_compile and wiki_ask are in EXTENDED_TIMEOUT_TOOL_NAMES (src/gobby/mcp_proxy/wait_tools.py), giving DaemonProxy a 300s HTTP timeout plus client guard/heartbeat. Standalone gwiki (Workstream D / #950) CANNOT read the handoff/session_end prompt from ~/.gobby/prompts/ — that directory does not exist. The daemon's PromptLoader.load() resolves from the DB (manager.get_by_name(path, project_id)), not the filesystem. So gwiki (no daemon, no hub in standalone mode) must EMBED the prompt at build time (e.g. include_str! a vendored copy in crates/gwiki) rather than read an installed file. The daemon-side golden fixture tests/prompts/fixtures/handoff_session_end_golden.md (daemon repo commit e0c6e6bd4 on branch 0.5.0) is the cross-repo drift guard: gwiki's minijinja render of its vendored prompt body + the same GOLDEN_CONTEXT (all 10 required+optional vars supplied as plain strings) must equal those exact golden bytes. The daemon renders via gobby.llm.prompt_rendering.render_summary_prompt -> jinja2 Environment(autoescape=False); the prompt body is PURE {{ var }} substitution (no {% %}/{# #}/filters), which minijinja matches byte-for-byte. Required vars: transcript_summary, last_messages, git_status, file_changes. Optional: structured_context, git_diff_summary, claimed_tasks, session_memories, first_digest_turn, recent_digest_turns.

Storage row factories in Gobby should preserve PostgreSQL JSONB fields that arrive already decoded as dict/list containers and only json.loads string values. Task-close evidence redesign is organized under epic #18705, with four ordered unclaimed children: #18701 -> #18702 -> #18703 -> #18704. Promote existing VerificationEvidence to durable project/task-scoped receipts; normalize outcomes independently from semantic sufficiency; add tokenless close_task(preview=true) with full reevaluation on real close. Evidence prompt overflow uses bounded risk-ranked inspection plus server-computed completeness disclosure and aggregates the low-priority tail (count, receipt ID range, outcome tally); hard refusal is reserved for the pathological case where disclosure plus all high-risk failed/conflicting/unknown rows cannot fit. Command previews middle-elide. Validation accounting changes only if regressions disprove current taxonomy: semantic code/test failures increment, infrastructure environment/dependency/provider/timeout failures use backoff without incrementing, and successful/override closure resets live count while retaining history. AGY tasks and compatibility changes are explicitly excluded from #18705 and belong under the existing AGY epic until the CLI meets minimum Gobby provider requirements. Do not restore deleted pre-#18666 validation_tool_loop or validation_coverage machinery.

Session detail transcript now reuses chat page components (MessageItem, ToolCallCard) via a transcriptAdapter (web/src/components/sessions/transcriptAdapter.ts). The adapter's sessionMessagesToChatMessages() function transforms SessionMessage[] to ChatMessage[] by: (1) grouping tool-use messages into the preceding assistant message's toolCalls array, (2) skipping user-role tool_result protocol messages, (3) parsing assistant JSON tool_use arrays into ToolCall objects, (4) extracting server_name from double-underscore naming (mcp__gobby__X → gobby). Hook feedback messages ('Stop hook feedback:', 'PreToolUse hook', 'PostToolUse hook', 'UserPromptSubmit hook') must be classified with role: 'system' (not role: 'user') for correct transcript rendering—system shows grey System label, user incorrectly shows blue You label. An isHookFeedback() detector function identifies these messages. Hook errors must be attached to the preceding tool call in the transcript structure rather than created as standalone error blocks, to maintain transcript integrity. Two additional bugs were fixed: (a) stop hook feedback was incorrectly rendered as 'You'—fixed by extracting user text from parsed content blocks; (b) raw content block arrays were not properly parsed, causing hook_context metadata to appear in output—fixed by stripping hook_context metadata. SessionDetail layout uses sticky header with compact inline stats, collapsible <details> for summary, and Ask Gobby button in header-right. Commit bba9d1f6.

WorkflowLoader runtime lookup is DB-only. Filesystem workflow imports under ~/.gobby/workflows and <project>/.gobby/workflows must be validated/upserted into workflow_definitions and the daemon loader cache cleared; shared logic lives in gobby.workflows.imports.

In gobby-cli `gobby-core`, `fernet` is an unconditional dependency (`fernet = "0.2.2"`) and should not be listed as `dep:fernet` in the `postgres` Cargo feature. PostgreSQL-backed secret resolution still depends on the `postgres` feature for datastore access, but Fernet crypto is compiled directly because `crates/gcore/src/secrets.rs` uses `fernet::Fernet` as part of the shared secret-resolution module.

Sessions activity interaction contract: SessionInteractionModal is intentionally context-only and always calls gobby-agents/send_message; semantic Send Context remains available for non-tmux sessions when a web chat source exists. Blind send_keys and one-shot capture_output UI were removed because the live terminal composer/view supersedes them. SessionsContextMenu exposes Open Terminal only when WatchingSessionEntry.hasTmux and dispatches gobby:show-activity-tab with { tab: 'terminal', sessionId: entry.id }, which useActivityPanel stores for TerminalTab focus consumption.

Managed ~/.gobby/bin native binary auto-updates are implemented as a daemon background loop using GitHub Releases only. Core modules live under src/gobby/install/bin_freshness_*.py, version floors in src/gobby/install/version_pins.py, and persisted state in bin_update_state. The daemon updater intentionally has no cargo, cargo-binstall, submodule, or ghook env override fallback paths; missing releases/assets record source_unavailable or floor_violated while leaving binaries untouched.

## Lesson
- principle: Client-directed ACP requests handled on the stdout stream must use bounded waits so one request cannot stall unrelated stream processing.
- root_cause: terminal/wait_for_exit awaited the terminal manager process wait directly from the request dispatcher.
- prevention: Wrap terminal wait_for_exit in asyncio.wait_for using the ACP request timeout and return a controlled JSON-RPC timeout error.

Linear sync for Gobby registers tasks under a Linear project named after the Gobby project/repo. It treats the Gobby task ref (#N) as the canonical identity inside that project, while any Linear-generated identifier (e.g. GOB-6) is secondary metadata. Local Gobby task titles remain unprefixed, while Linear issue titles use the prefix '#N: Title'. Gobby uses a Linear GraphQL fallback via linear_api_key for discovery, project/issue operations, status push resolution, and assignee preservation.

Settled personal multi-machine topology and portability requirement: AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 desktop with 128 GB runs Linux and is the first always-on Tailscale hub for the shared Gobby daemon, Docker-managed PostgreSQL/Qdrant/FalkorDB, shared tasks/sessions/memory/workflows, and durable full raw transcript replicas. MacBook Pro, Mac Mini, Windows machines, and other clients keep project checkouts, CLI processes, spawned agents, clones, worktrees, and filesystem/Git operations local to whichever machine Josh is actively using; the hub must never execute those as fallback. Although Linux is the first hub and Windows is not yet validated, the product goal is multi-platform support: protocols, schemas, path handling, process execution, worker interfaces, and persistence must remain OS-neutral, avoid POSIX-only assumptions, and carry Windows-focused contract/unit acceptance from the start.

The public session-storage module must keep re-exporting gobby.storage.sessions.logger. Tests and patch sites treat that module logger as a stable compatibility surface, so changes should preserve the public logger symbol rather than removing it.

HTTP task routes centralize request-session canonicalization in create_tasks_router's _resolve_session_ref helper. Sub-routes that write session attribution should receive this resolver through dependency injection and resolve X-Gobby-Session-Id with the task's project_id before storage writes.

Gobby web CSS architecture as of task #14832: Tailwind is imported only from web/src/styles/index.css, semantic Tailwind theme aliases live in web/src/styles/tailwind-theme.css, runtime design tokens live in web/src/styles/tokens.css, and chat variables.css is alias-only for legacy chat token names.

CodexAdapter approval responses: block→cancel, auto_approve→acceptForSession, exec_policy_amendment metadata→acceptWithExecpolicyAmendment. Build lifecycle artifact cleanup helpers now live in src/gobby/build/control_artifacts.py. src/gobby/build/controls.py still re-exports BuildArtifactSummary and calls public helper functions for collect/delete/defer/project path behavior; tests should patch gobby.build.control_artifacts.WorktreeGitManager for artifact cleanup behavior.

Task #15037 implementation: Grok is now a first-class Gobby provider via ACP using `grok agent --no-leader --always-approve [--model <id>] [--reasoning-effort <effort>] stdio`, with cached-token authenticate support, Grok `_x.ai/session_notification`/`session/update` normalization, terminal/create client request handling, Grok hooks at `~/.grok/hooks/gobby.json`, Grok model discovery from ACP then `~/.grok/models_cache.json` then static `grok-build`, and Grok transcript paths under `~/.grok/sessions/<url-encoded-cwd>/<session-id>/updates.jsonl`. In the Gobby web UI, image-generation tool results and show_file artifacts depend on two separate paths: shared extraction in web/src/lib/imageSources.ts for Codex shapes like { output: [{ type: 'input_image', image_url: 'data:image/...' }] }, and App.tsx forwarding useChat().setOnArtifactEvent into ChatPage. If App does not pass setOnArtifactEvent, websocket artifact_event messages can arrive but ChatPage never registers its artifact handler, so show_file images are not opened in the Artifacts tab.

Post-Phase-5 PostgreSQL concurrency re-audit (#14112): follow-up commit 84fa87b2ee3a934c1dffbe916467eb1259baa9b9 restores the SQLite-to-Postgres non-dry-run import contract. `_copy_validate_and_mark` now opens one outer PostgreSQL transaction, takes transaction-scoped advisory lock `gobby_sqlite_to_postgres_import`, re-checks target readiness and `imported_from_sqlite_at` under that lock, runs reset/drop/copy/recreate/reseed/validation/marker in that transaction, and forces deferred constraints to `IMMEDIATE` before validation/marker write. `_copy_sqlite_rows_to_postgres(..., manage_transaction=False)` is used from the import path so copy does not create an inner transaction there; its default standalone transaction behavior remains for direct helper callers/tests.

Linter revert behavior: When editing web/src/components files, if WorkflowsPage.tsx has TypeScript type mismatches with child component props (e.g. missing required props like enabledFilter, filterProvider, eventFilter), the linter will revert ALL modified files in the web/src/components directory back to their git HEAD state. To avoid this, always write WorkflowsPage.tsx (the parent) BEFORE editing child tab components, or apply all edits atomically. The linter runs after each Write/Edit tool call.

Voice TTS switched from Kokoro ONNX to Chatterbox Turbo (resemble-ai/chatterbox). PyPI package is chatterbox-tts (not chatterbox). Uses ChatterboxTurboTTS with 1-step distilled decoder for sub-200ms latency. Supports voice cloning from reference audio at ~/.gobby/voice/reference.wav. Memory session-title heuristic helpers live in `gobby.memory.title_heuristics`; `gobby.memory.digest` imports them for digest orchestration, and summary repair uses `_heuristic_title_from_transcript` from that module.

Workflow handler-route linting is implemented in src/gobby/workflows/handler_route_lint.py and integrated into WorkflowDryRunValidator structural checks. It reports MISSING_FAILURE_ROUTE when an MCP success handler lacks an exact error-handler counterpart, and ORDERING_VAR_UNSATISFIABLE when a handler guard depends on state that cannot be assigned on the relevant route. WorkflowStep.mcp_error_policy="stay" is the explicit, step-level annotation for an intentional MCP failure fallback that leaves the workflow on its current step; bundled agent definitions use this only where no exact error route is intended. assigned_task_id is treated as known runtime state because spawn infrastructure injects it. merge-worker keeps explicit exact failure handlers for merge_start and record_merge_result, and close-linked-issue has a satisfiable error guard. tests/workflows/test_handler_route_lint.py enforces the invariant across every bundled agent YAML, preventing future corpus drift. Implemented for task #17673 in commits 4ce1b591731ed677b52232116177b7fded202d23 and ad2180201.

LLM generate_text() returns error STRINGS instead of raising exceptions (e.g., 'Generation failed: {e}'). Downstream code like validation can't distinguish 'bad LLM output' from 'LLM call failed entirely'. When debugging 'Could not parse response' from extract_json_object(), always check if the input is an error string rather than actual LLM output. The real error is logged at ERROR level in claude.py but swallowed before reaching the caller.

Task #17215 hardened shell rule matching by making src/gobby/hooks/_normalization_shell.py tokenize Bash quote-aware tokens and src/gobby/hooks/_normalization_canonical.py classify compound shell commands segment-by-segment. canonical_tool_kind now merges visible segment intent with write > search > read > execute precedence, rebases relative operands after literal cd segments, preserves code-navigation metadata for mixed commands, and only keeps canonical_code_index_navigation for pure gcode navigation with neutral setup/read-only filters.

Project convention: Gobby is cleaning up legacy compatibility paths as they are encountered. Do not preserve or cite legacy `injected_skills` behavior when updating skill-loading logic; prefer canonical `loaded_skills` only unless explicitly told otherwise.

ChatInput centralizes primary composer-button state and PTT gesture behavior in web/src/components/chat/useChatInputPrimaryAction.ts. While PTT recording is active, the `mic-recording` action must take precedence over text/attachment `hasInput` so the visible button continues to stop and transcribe the latched recording.

TranscriptIndexAppender exposes a public `hydrate(index, state, current_id, next_parser_index, next_raw_line_no)` method so resume helpers can seed persisted index state without writing private appender attributes directly. `hydrate_appender_from_index` now builds the renderer seed state and delegates to this public method.

As of task #18589 / commit d8006d1c9, `gcode invalidate` accepts `--project-id <UUID>` and resolves an empty-root `Context` through `Context::resolve_for_project_id_with_services(..., ServiceConfigSelection::projection_cleanup())`. Both root and ID modes call crate-internal `commands::status::invalidate::invalidate_project`, which acquires `IndexLockPolicy::maintenance_try()` before any backend I/O, clears configured FalkorDB then Qdrant projections, and deletes PostgreSQL index/discovery rows only after both succeed. Missing backend configuration is a per-backend skip; configured backend errors and busy locks abort before SQL so retry inputs remain.

SessionManager in gobby.storage.sessions is the canonical public session storage class.
