Project purge lifecycle design (#18594, commit 78551b2a2): all in-daemon derived writers share one ProjectWriteFence. Service-level project/global admission spans asynchronous compute through the final vector/graph mutation; the final ProjectFencedVectorStore gate remains as defense in depth. Fence admission is task-reentrant so a writer admitted before purge can finish through nested store gates after purge claims exclusivity, while new tasks are rejected. Purge soft-deletes first, disables/drains/deletes project cron jobs, takes exclusive project admission plus the cross-process gwiki drain barrier, cleans wiki/code/vector/graph projections, and only then hard-deletes hub rows. The embedding switch is daemon-owned, single-flight, cooperatively abortable before FLIPPING, forward-only after FLIPPING, and persists its hidden internal journal under the same config mutation lock. Installer embedding writes are allowed only for proven first bootstrap.

PostgresHubDatabase hub connections intentionally set psycopg prepare_threshold=None in ConnectionPool kwargs. The hub storage layer has many SELECT * reads over long-lived pooled connections, so disabling psycopg auto-prepare avoids cached-plan result-shape failures after schema changes while preserving application_name and dict_row row_factory behavior. Regression coverage lives in tests/storage/hub/test_postgres_prepared_statements.py.

Assistant output arrives as `droid.session_notification` events such as `thinking_text_delta`, `assistant_text_delta`, `tool_call`, `tool_result`, and `droid_working_state_changed` with `newState: idle` for turn completion. The old Claude-shaped stdin payload `{"type":"message","message":{"role":"user",...}}` is rejected by Droid.

Task #17019 added backend rule rename support in commit 99d590a6e. `RuleUpdateRequest` in src/gobby/servers/routes/rules.py accepts `name`; update_rule_endpoint rejects renaming bundled/template rules using the loader's bundled-template provenance marker, checks name collisions only among `workflow_type='rule'` rows via manager.list_all, strips `name` from YAML definition bodies, and passes the row-level name into manager.update alongside definition/metadata fields. tests/servers/routes/test_rules_routes.py covers happy rename, type-scoped collision behavior, true rule collision 409, bundled rejection 400, and rename+definition update.

gobby-cli nextest rollout: .config/nextest.toml uses default/ci profiles with fail-fast=false and a serial-db test group. The serial-db group currently resolves to 19 live PostgreSQL tests: gcode schema/setup/graph reads/freshness/index_lock/search predicates plus gwiki configured PostgreSQL search/smoke tests. gwiki cli_output.rs, cli_parse.rs, cli_sources.rs, and common/mod.rs only remove GWIKI/GCODE_POSTGRES_TEST_DATABASE_URL or provide helpers, so fixture modernization including cli_sources.rs is tracked as a follow-up rather than grouped as live DB tests.

`verify_in_worktree` runs validation commands in a new POSIX session (`start_new_session=True`). Its timeout path sends `SIGKILL` to the process group via `os.killpg(proc.pid, signal.SIGKILL)` so forked test-runner descendants cannot outlive verification or continue mutating the worktree.

When extracting web/src/hooks/useChat.ts into helper hooks, do not leave params typed only as Record<string, any>. Type the setter/ref props used by functional updaters so TypeScript can infer updater callback parameters under noImplicitAny; also name ref props with a Ref suffix to satisfy react-hooks immutability checks.

Web light-theme semantic-token contrast tests live in web/src/styles/__tests__/tokens.contrast.test.ts and parse tokens.css directly. For color-mix(... transparent) badge surfaces, use contrastRatioOnSrgbTint from web/src/lib/colorContrast.ts so WCAG checks include sRGB tint compositing over the actual base surface.

Session variable `is_subagent` (default false) is toggled by SUBAGENT_START/STOP hooks in `_agent.py`. When a Claude Code native subagent is active, it unblocks native task tools (TaskCreate etc.), blocks gobby-tasks MCP tools, and disables require-task-before-edit, require-error-triage, require-memory-review, and require-commit-before-status gates. Separate from `is_spawned_agent` which controls worker-safety rules for Gobby-managed agents. Gemini/Codex don't have SubagentStart/Stop hooks.

StageStatesManager storage is split after task #14518: src/gobby/storage/tasks/_stage_states.py is a thin public facade; row conversion and read queries live in _stage_state_rows.py and are shared by _stage_hydration.py; schema repair, mutex construction, manifest mutation, and transition logic live in _stage_state_schema.py, _stage_state_mutex.py, _stage_state_manifest_ops.py, and _stage_state_transitions.py. tests/meta/test_import_hygiene.py enforces storage task modules stay under 1,000 LOC.

Tool normalization architecture: `normalize_tool_fields()` in `src/gobby/hooks/normalization.py` is the primary entry point for all CLI adapters. It runs two phases: (1) field alias normalization (function_name→tool_name, toolName→tool_name, toolArgs→tool_input with JSON parsing, parameters→tool_input, args→tool_input, mcp_context→mcp_server/mcp_tool), (2) delegates to `normalize_mcp_fields()` for mcp__ prefix parsing, call_tool inner extraction, and tool_result/tool_response→tool_output. All 6 adapters (Claude Code, Gemini, Cursor, Copilot, Windsurf, Codex) plus web chat now use this shared function. Cursor has additional handling for beforeMCPExecution/afterMCPExecution hooks (JSON string parsing + MCP server/tool extraction from tool_input + result_json→tool_output). Windsurf's _extract_tool_info uses mcp_server_name/mcp_tool_name with fallback to server_name/tool_name.

Task #18824 / commit 592ec7e843fd0a77cd7551afbe9607e6f155a8a6 wires ToolResultOffloader into ToolProxyService with an explicit wrapper_originated delivery policy. FastMCP call_tool and both HTTP MCP routes activate offloading; stdio reaches the same boundary through HTTP. Internal services, workflow pipelines, and call_tool_by_name retain full results by default. Dispatch applies after-tool workflow processing to the full output before maybe_offload. Wrapper intent is metadata at top level or beside nested routing, while innermost target arguments.intent remains untouched. Final envelope and retrieval budgets were verified after FastMCP metadata, HTTP success wrappers, and stdio wait-timeout keys are composed.

Task #18821 / commit 94c9b3b0c established the tool-result offload foundation. `ToolResultOffloadConfig` lives in `gobby.config.features`, is owned by `DaemonConfig.tool_result_offload`, and is exposed by `get_tool_result_offload_config()`. Its load-bearing invariants are `max_envelope_chars < threshold_chars`, `preview_chars <= max_envelope_chars`, and `max_stored_chars >= threshold_chars`; every size/count/retention integer also has explicit lower and upper bounds. PostgreSQL migration 340 creates `tool_results` plus cascade-owned `tool_result_chunks`, with unique `(result_id, ordinal)` and the pg_search BM25 index `tool_result_chunks_search_bm25` on `(id, content)`. The fresh baseline snapshot is intentionally unchanged because post-baseline migrations replay automatically in test fixtures and new installs.
MCP tools replace plugins as the extension mechanism in the project.

ACP-backed web chat sessions genuinely created through Gobby are canonical Session rows with source equal to the provider and session_type=`web_chat`; there is no literal source=`acp`. Provider-native `session/list` history is excluded. Detect ACP lifecycle support through backend capability/enrichment: sessionCapabilities keys are supported only when present with a non-null value, and an empty object means no lifecycle actions.

Gobby 0.4.0 voice docs should describe voice as a local web-chat pipeline: `voice_prepare` lazily warms STT/TTS, `/api/voice/status` reports `voice_ready`/`voice_loading` plus warmup errors, `VoiceConfig` has separate `stt_enabled` and `tts_enabled`, Chatterbox is the only registered TTS provider, and `gobby-voice` exposes `add_vocab`, `remove_vocab`, `list_vocab`, and `clear_vocab` for Whisper vocabulary.

HookManager._dispatch_mcp_calls bug (fixed in #9186): The hook manager subprocess has no persistent event loop, so MCP call effects from rule engine evaluation were silently dropped. The fallback path logged 'no event loop for blocking call' at DEBUG level and returned without executing. Fix: added asyncio.run() fallback when neither a running loop nor self._loop is available. This pattern matches how WorkflowHookHandler.evaluate() handles the same sync-to-async bridge. Key files: src/gobby/hooks/hook_manager.py (_dispatch_mcp_calls), src/gobby/workflows/hooks.py (WorkflowHookHandler.evaluate). The rule engine itself was confirmed working correctly via direct test — the issue was purely in dispatch.
Build target controls in Gobby preserve a task's `unattended` flag across stop/resume operations; `build_stop_target` and `build_resume_target` only toggle `allow_automation`.

MCP tool inventory contract: unfiltered GET /api/mcp/tools is passive and reads cached external tool summaries from MCPServerConfig.tools without connecting, regardless of connection health. Filtered inventory and POST /api/mcp/refresh are explicit live discovery paths; successful live discovery persists the tool cache. Gobby-bundled external servers launched via npx receive npm_config_prefer_offline=true unless their server env explicitly configures another value.

User wants visual consistency across ALL chat/transcript code-rendering surfaces, including CodeMirror. CodeMirror keeps its widget (editing requires capabilities react-syntax-highlighter doesn't have) but its theme tokens (background, gutter color, line-number style, font, padding, border-radius) must come from the same CODE_CHROME_VARS module that drives CodeBlock. User pushed back when initial #13794 scope marked CodeMirror as 'out of scope' — the user's actual frame is 'how things look', not 'which widget renders them'. Filed item #14238 for token alignment.

Telegram native command-menu contract (task #18857, commit 1df154f63): supported comms responder slash commands are defined once in communications.commands and drive both transport-neutral /help text and the BotCommand payload. TelegramAdapter calls setMyCommands on every channel initialization with the deterministic new/reset/stop/status/help payload, so restarts refresh the menu idempotently. HTTP failures are token-redacted and Bot API ok=false responses raise a descriptive initialization error; CommunicationsManager's existing lifecycle exposes that failure as channel init_error diagnostics.

In gobby-cli, gwiki synthesis is split with `crates/gwiki/src/synthesis.rs` as the public facade. Child modules live under `crates/gwiki/src/synthesis/`: `types.rs` defines `ArticleKind`, synthesis input/source/prompt/page types, and write outcome/policy types; `generate.rs` contains article/source-page synthesis orchestration and explainer grounding; `paths.rs` contains vault-boundary checks, slug/link/relative-path helpers, and source-page path/link selection; `render.rs` contains frontmatter, source excerpt, list-section, and YAML scalar rendering helpers; `write.rs` contains write policy checks and atomic page writes; `tests.rs` holds the existing synthesis behavior tests with narrow imports for private helper coverage. The facade still exports the public synthesis/write APIs and data types.

gobby-code Rust tests resolve PostgreSQL test URLs from explicit variables/components and finally `GOBBY_HOME/bootstrap.yaml`. Any in-process test that mutates `GOBBY_HOME` must use `#[serial_test::serial(serial_db)]`, the same key as database-backed tests, and must scope the mutation with `temp_env` so the prior value is restored. Task #18485 / commit 9bb88c298 fixed a full-suite race where the standalone setup test removed the caller's GOBBY_HOME and config/graph tests used different or no serialization, causing configured DB tests to panic nondeterministically.

Session terminal_context writes from registration, backfill, and generic SessionManager.update() use atomic PostgreSQL JSONB shallow merges. Incoming null values are ignored, scalar fields remain in the same transaction, and each generic update emits one session-change notification, so liveness metadata such as tmux_pane survives partial, stale, and concurrent updates. The SESSION_START gobby_session_id binding updates external identity first and delegates context persistence to atomic backfill. Generic update coverage landed in task #18656 / commit faa673746.

In the gobby task storage package, task lifecycle event storage lives in src/gobby/storage/tasks/_lifecycle_events.py. TaskLifecycleEventManager returns TaskLifecycleEvent objects and lists in insertion order by default for audit assertions; the module-level record_lifecycle_event helper returns the inserted event id, and module-level list_lifecycle_events returns newest-first using created_at DESC, id DESC to satisfy the #12784 task API.

CLI commands init, install, and uninstall now support -C/--path to specify target directory. Before this, running from source required: `cd target && uv run --project ~/Projects/gobby gobby init`. Now: `uv run --project ~/Projects/gobby gobby init -C ~/Projects/target`. The option uses click.Path(exists=True, file_okay=False, path_type=Path) and resolves to replace Path.cwd(). initialize_project() already accepted a cwd parameter so no downstream changes were needed.

Gobby's memory IndexingService coalesces concurrent global embedding reindex requests with a service-level in-flight task, so duplicate callers await the same rebuild result instead of logging a post-rebuild unchanged-snapshot skip. Sequential same-snapshot global calls still dedupe for 60 seconds by fingerprinting the source memory snapshot and verifying Qdrant point IDs match, preserving manual repair reindexes after the short window and invalidating the dedupe cache when vector indices are cleared.
